The anchor position `-1` means none. `\z` and `\Z` are not made to fail on a line that is not the last (`NotEndString` is never set by vscode-textmate).

## 4.3 TextMate tokenizer

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-4.3-textmate-tokenizer
- **Summary:** the grammar model and the core of the line tokenizer (SPEC §8.3), a port of vscode-textmate's `rule.ts`, `grammar.ts` and `tokenizeString.ts`. `rawgrammar.go`: `ParseGrammar` reads a JSON grammar into `RawGrammar`/`RawRule` (all the keys of the format, injections in file order for 4.4; errors have the tag `GrammarInvalid`). `grammar.go`: the `Registry` interface (scope name → `*RawGrammar`, which 4.5 implements), `NewGrammar`, the rule factory (`compileRule`, captures, patterns with every kind of `include`: `$self`, `$base`, `#name`, `scope`, `scope#name`; the `$base` of an included grammar is the grammar tokenized; a rule whose patterns are all missing is left out; a rule is compiled once for all the places that include it), `collectPatterns` and the scanner of a rule (`regex.Scanner` of 4.2 over the patterns of the rule with its end pattern first or last by `applyEndPatternLast`; an end with `\1` references gets a scanner of its own for each text it was completed with). `rule.go`: `regexSource` (the `\z` replacement, back references completed with the escaped captured text) and `template` for names with `$1` and `${1:/upcase}`. `tokenize.go`: `Grammar.TokenizeLine(line, prev, timeLimit)`, the scan loop with begin/end, match rules, captures (including captures with patterns, which tokenize the captured text again, and nested captures with their local stack), contentName, the anchor position and the beginning of a line after a begin that matched the line break, and the endless-loop guards of vscode-textmate. `state.go`: `State`, a persistent list that is `Equal` when the open rules, their end patterns and the scopes are (the positions the tokenizer keeps in a state are tied to the line that made them, so a state is never changed after it is returned and can be shared by threads); `scopes.go`: the persistent `ScopeStack`. The limit of `editor.maxTokenizationLineLength` (20,000 bytes by default) makes a line one token without scopes; a pattern past its 100 ms ends the line as plain text.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/textmate/{rawgrammar.go,grammar.go,rule.go,tokenize.go,state.go,scopes.go}`; tests `firstmate_test.go`, `tokenize_test.go`, `grammar_test.go`; `docs/SPEC.md` §8.3.

The same for injections, the standard token type and the embedded language of tokens (`TODO(step 4.4)` where the scan looks for rules). The suite1 cases of vscode-textmate need plist grammars and are not part of the step. The tokens are not merged when their scopes are equal (vscode-textmate merges them only after the theme gives them the same style, which Emetos does when it resolves the styles). The scan loop has a guard of `4 * length + 64` rounds for a grammar that goes on without advancing in a way the checks of vscode-textmate do not see. The cycle of include-only rules that include each other is cut when patterns are collected (vscode-textmate overflows its stack).

## 4.4 TextMate: while, injections, embedded languages

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-4.4-textmate-while-injections
- **Summary:** the rest of the tokenizer (SPEC §8.3). `begin`/`while` rules (`ruleBeginWhile`, `Grammar.compiledWhile`; `tokenizer.checkWhile` checks the while patterns of the open rules at the start of each line, outermost first, closing the rule whose pattern fails and taking its `whileCaptures`; a while pattern with `\1` is completed with the text of the begin like an end pattern). `matcher.go`: scope selectors (`L:`/`R:`, `-`, `,`, `|`, parentheses) and the matcher of names that match a scope or its prefix before a dot. Injections (`attributes.go`, `tokenizer.scan`): the `injections` of the grammar in file order and, through the new `Registry.Injections(scope)`, the grammars injected into it with their `injectionSelector`, sorted by priority; they are looked for after the rule of the state and win when they start earlier or, with `L:`, at the same place. Embedded grammars through the registry were in 4.3 (an include of a scope name); what 4.4 adds is that each token has its **type** (comment, string, regex, other; `meta.embedded` resets to other; `GrammarOptions.TokenTypes` selectors override) and its **language id** (`GrammarOptions.EmbeddedLanguages`, `InitialLanguage`), kept in each `ScopeStack` node by `Grammar.push` and read by `lineTokens.produce`. `Token` gained `Type` and `Language`; scope stacks are now made by the grammar (`pushPath`). The `TODO(step 4.4)` marks of 4.3 are gone.

## 4.9 Tokenization in documents and highlighted painting

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-4.9-tokenization
- **Summary:** `core/tokens` (SPEC §8.3): a per-document `Tokenizer` with per-line tokens and end states, invalidation from the first edited line, early stop on an equal end state, `Ensure` (synchronous, budgeted), `Run` (background, 5 ms slices on snapshots, stale results dropped by a generation counter), `SetGrammar`, `OnChange`. Tokens are compact (`End`, interned `ScopeID`, language, type; `Scopes` is a trie). `language.Registry` gives `NewGrammarWith`, `GrammarSettings` and `HasGrammar`; `editor.maxTokenizationLineLength` is registered. `kit.Theme` carries an optional `TokenTheme` (`TokenThemeOf`), `gui/app` builds it from the theme service. The editor builds spans from tokens plus the theme, caches paragraphs with the spans in the key, and repaints the lines that the background loop finishes. `core/regex` gained a per-(line, scanner, pattern) cache of the leftmost match (valid for later start positions up to the match start; a "no match" stays valid; patterns with a live `\G` are not cached), which made tokenization 2.5× faster.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/tokens/`, `internal/core/regex/scanner.go`, `internal/core/textmate/scopes.go` (`ScopeStack.Parent`), `internal/core/language/registry.go`, `internal/core/settings/builtin.go`, `internal/gui/kit/theme.go`, `internal/gui/app/{theme,process,window,app}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{highlight,tokens,text,cache,render,widget,viewmodel}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §8.3, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.

Benchmarks: `BenchmarkTokenizeGoLines` (about 160 µs per line), `BenchmarkTypeCharacter10kLinesHighlighted` (0.62 ms), `BenchmarkScrollPage100kLinesHighlighted` (8.2 ms for a page of unseen lines).

The first view of unseen lines in a very large file spends up to the 6 ms synchronous budget and exceeds the 8 ms scrolling target slightly (8.2 ms); the remaining lines are tokenized in the background and painted when ready. The remaining cost is regexp2's word-boundary and character-class lookups. An earlier run of the scroll benchmark with `-benchtime 2000x` ran out of memory (it tokenizes new lines each iteration); the notes in `PERFORMANCE.md` say to use a small count.

- **Date:** 2026-10-23

- **Summary:** C, C++ (and CUDA C++), Rust, Diff, Git commit, Git rebase, Ignore files and the Go module files (`go.mod`, `go.work`, `go.sum`) are bundled. `copy_extension` now copies a `languages/` folder too (git-base keeps its language configurations there). The Go module grammars come from `golang/vscode-go` (v0.59.0): `scripts/update-assets.sh` writes the extension `go-mod` from its two grammars and its language configuration, with a `package.json` that names only the three languages (`go.work` uses the `go.mod` grammar, scope `go.mod`); the license is in `third_party/vscode-go/`. All grammars have permissive licenses (cgmanifest.json: MIT, TextMate bundle license), so none was left out.
- **A fix in `core/regex` that the C++ grammar needed:** one pattern of the grammar (a function definition) took 130 to 200 ms on a line such as `puts("\n***…")`, doubling for every two `*`, so the 100 ms limit stopped the line. The pattern has a loop over `&` and `*`, each followed by the grammar's whitespace group, which ends in the empty alternatives `(?<=\W)|(?=\W)|^|…`: each `*` can be followed by an empty match in several ways, and a failed search tries every combination. Oniguruma 6.9.9 and later remembers where a search has failed; regexp2 does not. `emitter.alternation` now writes a run of neighbouring branches that consume nothing and capture nothing as one atomic group, which cannot change the result (after one of them has matched, the others lead to the same state). SPEC §8.2 says so.
- **Main files:** `scripts/update-assets.sh`, `internal/core/regex/emit.go`, `internal/core/language/{bundled.go,bundled_test.go,oracle_test.go,systems_test.go,assets/}`, `third_party/vscode-go/`, `NOTICE`, `docs/SPEC.md` §8.1, §8.2.

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-4.12-brackets
- **Summary:** `core/brackets` (SPEC §8.5). `Language` holds the brackets of a language, made from its configuration as VS Code's `LanguageBracketsConfiguration` does (`brackets` plus `colorizedBracketPairs`, whose pairs are brackets too; the default colorized pairs leave out `<` `>`; a closing text may close several openings, as `endcase` closes `case` and `casez`; case-insensitive; a bracket that starts or ends with a letter is found at the edge of a word only). `Index` reads a `Source` (lines, tokens, document language, whether the tokens are complete), keeps the brackets of every line until an edit (`Apply`, `Splice`, `Reset`) or new tokens (`Invalidate`) touch it, and pairs all of them lazily in one pass with a stack, as VS Code's parser does: a closing bracket closes the innermost pair it fits, the pairs above stay unclosed, one that fits none is unexpected, and an opening bracket deeper than 150 pairs is text. Queries: `Pairs`, `Brackets` (with `onlyColorized`), `Match`, `Enclosing`, `MatchingUp`, `Prev`, `Next`, `HasUnmatchedClosingAfter`. Brackets are found in tokens of the standard type "other" only, in the language of the token. `Attach` follows a document and its tokenizer; `RegistryLanguages` makes the languages from the language registry; a document in large file mode has an index that finds nothing.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/brackets/`, `docs/SPEC.md` §8.5, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.
- **Tests:** ported from VS Code: `brackets.test.ts` (the Verilog and LaTeX brackets with their closing sets), `tokenizer.test.ts` (the bracket tokenizer on tokens that are split, a comment that holds a bracket), `getBracketPairsInRange.test.ts` (all 10: Basic 1, Basic 2, Basic Empty, Basic All, `getBracketsInRange` with the levels of equal brackets, Test Error Brackets, colorized brackets against brackets in both modes, and the three about unmatched closing brackets: after a position, waiting for the tokens, and scoped to a language), and `textModelWithTokens.test.ts` (brackets1 for previous and next bracket from every column, bracket matching 1 to 4, issue #95843 with two languages in a line, #88075 with strings in a template, #11856). Emetos's own: a fuzz test that edits a text at random (replacing ranges with random text, with some lines without tokens, and some tokens changing) and checks that the index that followed the edits finds the same pairs, brackets (both modes), matches and enclosing pairs as a new index on the same text (60 seeds of 60 edits); the pairs against a plain stack on 200 random texts; edits that move and invalidate lines; `Enclosing`, `MatchingUp`; unclosed pairs and their ends; the depth limit; the document and tokenizer attached (Go, with brackets in strings and comments, an edit that changes the tokens of the lines below it, undo, `SetText`, large file mode); the languages of the bundled configurations (HTML lists no colorized pairs, JSON has braces).
- **Not ported:** the tests of the tree, `beforeEditPositionMapper`, `combineTextEditInfos`, `concat23Trees`, `length` and `smallImmutableSet`, because the tree of VS Code (a 2-3 tree reused across edits) is not ported (SPEC §8.5 allows a simpler scheme that passes the ported tests and the fuzz test); the old matching code for models too big to build the tree (`canBuildAST` false), because large files have no index.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none (the step names none)
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** an edit costs one pass over all the brackets of the document (18 ms at 100,000 lines and 600,000 brackets, about 2 ms at 10,000 lines; `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`), where VS Code reuses the nodes an edit did not touch. Pairing only from the first edited line and stopping when the open pairs match the old ones would fix it; it is left until the editor of 4.13 shows it matters. `getBracketPairsInRangeWithMinIndentation`, which the guides of 4.14 need, is added there. Tokens with the same scopes are merged as VS Code merges tokens with the same metadata (the colors are not part of Emetos's tokens). The balanced-bracket selectors of grammars (`unbalancedBracketScopes` in the markdown extension) are not read yet; brackets are looked for in every token of type "other".

## 4.13 Brackets in the editor

- **Summary:** the bracket features of the editor (SPEC §8.5.1). `core/edit/brackets.go`: `JumpToBracket`, `SelectToBracket` (with and without the brackets), `Commands.RemoveBrackets`, and `NewBracketSelectionRanges`, the provider of the bracket steps of Expand Selection (VS Code's `bracketSelections.ts`: inside, the pair, the line it starts on or the one above); `core/edit/stringselect.go`: `NewStringSelectionRanges`, the string steps (inside the quotes, the string), from the tokens of type "string". The commands `editor.action.jumpToBracket` (Ctrl+Shift+\\), `editor.action.selectToBracket` and `editor.action.removeBrackets` (Ctrl+Alt+Backspace) are registered, with their keybindings, and run in the editor. Settings `editor.matchBrackets`, `editor.bracketPairColorization.enabled` and `editor.bracketPairColorization.independentColorPoolPerBracketType`. Colors `editorBracketMatch.{background,border,foreground}`, `editorBracketHighlight.foreground1..6` and `editorBracketHighlight.unexpectedBracket.foreground` in the registry and in `kit.Colors`. `ViewModel.SetBrackets` takes the index (`brackets.Attach`), which the shell makes next to the tokenizer. ## 4.14 Indentation detection

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-4.14-indentation-detection
- **Summary:** `core/indent.Guess`, a port of VS Code's `guessIndentation` (first 10,000 lines; tabs or spaces by the lines that start with each; the tab size from the differences between lines that follow each other, in the order 2, 4, 6, 8, 3, 5, 7; alignment after a comma skipped; 2 over 4 with two thirds of its occurrences). `Documents.OpenFile` now gives a file the indentation its language asks of the settings (`editor.tabSize`, `editor.insertSpaces`, which no code applied to documents before) and, with `editor.detectIndentation` on, the one `Guess` finds. Emetos's own: ten edge cases of `Guess` (empty text, white-space-only lines, a tie, tabs winning, 3 spaces, 2 over 4 and 4 over 2, a difference over 8, more than 10,000 lines); `ConvertIndentation` (tabs to spaces with sizes 2 and 4, spaces to tabs with leftovers, white-space-only lines, the selection following the text, nothing to convert, an empty text, tabs after the text, several cursors collapsing to the primary); in the editor: the commands through `RunCommand` (with undo of the conversion), the arguments of "Indent Using…" (a number, an object, the display size keeping what Tab inserts, nine invalid arguments with the `TabSizeRequired` route), Detect Indentation with and without defaults; `configurationDefaults` of a manifest (several languages in one key, a key that is not a language block, a block that is not an object) and of the bundled languages; the shell opening files: 10 cases (two spaces and tabs found in text, the settings when the text says nothing, detection off, detection over settings, Go, YAML, Makefile, empty).

Changing `editor.tabSize`, `editor.insertSpaces` or `editor.detectIndentation` while a file is open does not re-apply them to it (VS Code does for files whose indentation was not detected); the settings apply when a file opens. `indentSize` (`editor.indentSize`) is not a separate option yet (it equals the tab size, as `edit.Options` already says).

## 4.16 Guides

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-4.16-guides
- **Summary:** indent guides and bracket pair guides (SPEC §8.6.3). `core/indent` gets `Levels` (the indentation of each line in columns, computed when asked, forgotten when an edit touches the line, with the smallest indentation of each block of 64 lines; `AttachLevels` makes it follow a document) and `Guides` with `LinesIndentGuides`, `ActiveIndentGuide`, `BracketGuides` and `LineGuides`, a port of `guidesTextModelPart.ts` and of `IndentGuidesOverlay.getGuidesByLine` (the options `editor.guides.*`, the interplay of the two kinds: a bracket guide takes the place of the indent guide at its column and the active indent guide is not highlighted on a line that has bracket guides unless `highlightActiveIndentation` is `"always"`). The smallest indentation inside a pair (VS Code's `minVisibleColumnIndentation`) is the smallest level among the lines after the opening bracket's up to the closing bracket's, which `Levels.MinLevel` answers in a few hundred steps even for a pair around most of a file. In the editor: the settings `editor.guides.indentation`, `highlightActiveIndentation`, `bracketPairs`, `bracketPairsHorizontal` and `highlightActiveBracketPair`; the colors `editorIndentGuide.background2..6`, `editorIndentGuide.activeBackground` and `1..6`, `editorBracketPairGuide.background1..6` and `activeBackground1..6` in the registry and in `kit.Colors`; `ViewModel.SetGuides` (the shell makes the levels next to the tokenizer and the brackets, with the language's `folding.offSide`); the layer below the text draws the guides after the selections and before the bracket boxes, in the colors of `NewGuideColors` (a level with a transparent color is left out and the levels go round the rest; a bracket guide with no color of its own takes the bracket color of its level, at 30% opacity when inactive).

Folded lines are not in the projection yet either (step 8.7). The vertical position of a guide is `(visible column − 1)` times the width of `0` in the font (VS Code uses the width of a space; they are equal in a monospace font). `Levels` is built for the document's tab size (`SetTabSize` follows a change); Emetos has no separate `editor.indentSize`, an indent level is a tab size. ## 4.17 Auto-closing and surrounding

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-4.17-auto-closing
- **Summary:** auto-closing pairs, quotes and comments, typing over, deleting a pair and surrounding a selection (SPEC §8.6.4). A new `core/autoclose` holds the pairs of a language (VS Code's `CharacterPairSupport` and `StandardAutoClosingPairConditional`: `notIn`, `beforeText`, the neutral character, the maps by first and last character of the opening and the closing, `autoCloseBefore`, the surrounding pairs) and the values of `editor.autoClosingBrackets/Quotes/Comments/Delete/Overtype` and `editor.autoSurround`. `edit.Commands.Type` with one character now types over a closing character, closes a pair (longest opening, `beforeText`, the allowed characters after the cursor, the bracket balance from `brackets.Index.HasUnmatchedClosingAfter`, quotes after a word character, the token before the cursor, a neutral character asked of the tokenizer through the new `tokens.Tokenizer.TypeIfInserting`, a pair contained in another, an opening of several characters with its second undo step through `Result.FollowUp`) or surrounds a selection, in VS Code's order after the type-time indentation, which now also inserts the closing text (`Result.AutoClosed`). `edit.AutoClosedTracker` keeps the closing characters as decorations and forgets a pair when a cursor leaves it (`Cursors.SetOnChange` tells it), and Backspace deletes a pair the editor typed. ## 5.1 Find model

- **Date:** 2026-10-23

A multiline search reads the text in windows of 5,000 lines with 500 of lookahead (SPEC §9.8: "a bounded window of lines") and a regular expression gives up after one second. `ReplacePattern` (`ParseReplaceString`: `\n \t \\ \u \U \l \L $$ $& $0 $n $nn` with JavaScript's reading of a number that is not a group) and the preserve-case builder. `State` (VS Code's `FindReplaceState`: the strings, the switches with their one-change overrides, the scopes, `loop`, position, count and current match, change events). `Model` over a `Host` interface (the selection, scrolling, word separators, `editor.find.cursorMoveOnType`, timers): the matches are decorations of the document (`findMatch`, `currentFindMatch`, `rangeHighlight`, `findScope`), searched again 100 ms after an edit, `MoveToNextMatch`, `MoveToPrevMatch` (from the decorations below 19,999 matches, by searching above), `MoveToMatch`, `Replace`, `ReplaceAll` (one undo step, the touching matches one edit, the selection tracked through the edit; at 19,999 matches or more with no scope the whole text is replaced at once), `SelectAllMatches` (the selection that is a match stays primary), find in selection as the search scopes. Settings `editor.find.cursorMoveOnType` and `editor.find.loop`.

## 5.3 Word wrap

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-5.3-word-wrap
- **Summary:** word wrap through the line projection (SPEC §9.2). `core/wrap` computes the breaks of one line (`Compute`, a port of VS Code's `MonospaceLineBreaksComputer`: kinsoku rules, break after spaces and some punctuation, hard break for a word wider than a row, continuation indent from `wrappingIndent`). The view model holds the breaks of every line (`wordwrap.go`): the wrap key (columns, character width, indent, tab size, strategy, font) decides when they are recomputed; the document is broken in slices through the view model's timer (edited lines first, then the viewport, then the rest; synchronously when there is no timer) and an edit splices the breaks of the changed lines; the scroll position is anchored to the top visible row when rows above it change. ASCII lines in a monospace font are broken by counting columns, other lines through the paragraph's measurements. `wrappedProjection` (with folds) replaces the identity or folded projection while wrapping; `edit.ModelLineLayout` takes an `edit.RowMap` so Up/Down, Home and End work on rows. Painting: continuation rows are indented by an x offset, the current line highlight covers all rows of a line, selections and find matches cross rows, the cursor and hit testing use the row of a position. Settings `editor.wordWrap`, `wordWrapColumn`, `wrappingIndent`, `wrappingStrategy`, `stopRenderingLineAfter`; command `editor.action.toggleWordWrap` (Alt+Z), which turns wrapping on or off for one editor over the setting. No wrapping in large file mode or for lines over `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter`.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/wrap/{doc.go,breaks.go}`, `internal/core/edit/layout.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{wordwrap,wordwrap_commands,wrapproj}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{viewmodel,options,text,render,geometry,overlay,pointer,commands}.go`, `internal/gui/app/app.go`, `internal/core/{settings/builtin,command/builtin,keybinding/defaults}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.2 and §9.4.
- **Tests:** `wrap`: break tables (plain words, hyphens, long words, tabs, wide characters, kinsoku, indentation modes, a narrow width). `edit`: row-aware vertical moves, Home/End on rows, the pixel column kept across rows. `wrapproj`: tables with wraps and folds together, rows, indents, `RowStarts`, `Indent`, empty document. View model: wrap columns for each mode, breaks after edits (typing, joining and splitting lines, undo), the breaks are known by slices with a timer, resizing, the anchor, folds with wraps, cursor movement on wrapped lines, toggling, large file mode, lines over the stop limit, paragraph route for non-ASCII. Widgets: wrapping on screen, clicks on continuation rows and past the end of a line, the rectangle of a cursor on a row, resizing both ways, the current line over all rows, toggling live; goldens `wordwrap` (selection over wrapped rows), `wordwrap_cursor` (cursor on a continuation row, current line), `wordwrap_fold_find` (a fold and find matches on wrapped rows), each viewed.
- **Not ported:** `editor.wordBreak`, `editor.wordWrapBreakAfterCharacters` and `BeforeCharacters` (not registered; VS Code's defaults are used), the browser-specific `advanced` details (the strategy uses paragraph measurements), the cursor affinity at a wrap point, indent guides on continuation rows, wrapping by view zones.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none (the plan lists none; the goldens show the result)
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** breaks run on the UI thread in slices (SPEC says background): a goroutine adds nothing until the paragraph route needs the text engine, which only the UI thread may use. Tabs after a wrap are measured from the start of the row. `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter` is registered but only stops wrapping: the render cutoff of §6.4 is not implemented yet. The cursor has no affinity at wrap points, so End on a row and the start of the next row are one position drawn at the start of the next row. Step 5.4 (whitespace) must draw on rows through `RowSpan`; the minimap (5.5) and sticky scroll (5.6) must use the projection's rows, not lines.

## 5.4 Whitespace, rulers and highlights

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-5.4-whitespace-rulers-highlights
- **Summary:** the remaining display options of SPEC §3.1. `editor.renderWhitespace` (`none`, `boundary`, `selection` (the default), `trailing`, `all`) draws VS Code's dot and arrow on the spaces and tabs it says (`whitespaceMarks`, a port of the SVG whitespace overlay, with the selection parts of each row, the single trailing space of a row that continues, and `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter`). `editor.renderControlCharacters` (default true) draws a dark red box with the Control Pictures glyph over the C0 controls, DEL and the directional formatting characters, above the text. `editor.rulers` (numbers or `{column, color}`, sorted) draws 1-pixel lines at their columns in `editorRuler.foreground` or their own color. `editor.occurrencesHighlight` (`off`, `singleFile`, `multiFile`) and `editor.occurrencesHighlightDelay` mark the other occurrences of the word at the cursor (VS Code's textual document highlight: case sensitive, whole words, after the delay, kept while the cursor moves inside a marked word, dropped by typing and edits); `editor.selectionHighlight`, `selectionHighlightMaxLength` and `selectionHighlightMultiline` mark the text that equals the selection with the find widget's switches, apart from the selections and from what the open find widget already marks. Both highlights are document decorations (owners 4 and 5) made by the view model (`highlights.go`) from `edit.Commands.WordQuery`, `SelectionQuery`, `Occurrences` and `OccurrencesApartFrom` (`core/edit/highlight.go`, over the literal search of the occurrence commands), follow the settings live, and are drawn between the guides and the find matches. New colors `editor.selectionHighlightBackground` and `Border`, `editor.wordHighlightBackground`, `StrongBackground`, `TextBackground` and the three borders.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/edit/highlight.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{whitespace,display_paint,highlights}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{overlay,options,viewmodel,folding,widget}.go`, `internal/gui/kit/theme.go`, `internal/core/{settings/builtin,theme/colors_builtin}.go`, `internal/gui/app/app.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.2 and §9.4.

Goldens `whitespace_all`, `whitespace_boundary`, `whitespace_trailing`, `whitespace_selection`, `rulers_control`, `highlight_word`, `highlight_selection`, each viewed (zoomed for the dots).
- **Not ported:** the marks of the highlights on the overview ruler, `editor.selectedTextMatchMode`, `editor.renderWhitespace`'s `experimentalWhitespaceRendering` variants (only the SVG look), the `[U+XXXX]` text VS Code shows for the directional formatting characters (a 2-pixel bar here), the word highlight of language servers (read and write access: area 3), highlights in other files (`multiFile` marks the file itself).

- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the word highlight uses the editor's word separators for both the word and the whole-word search (VS Code's textual provider uses its usual separators for the search). The highlights are computed on the UI thread: a document of a million lines searched for a short selection each time it changes would be slow (the selection highlight skips large file mode). The control character box takes the cell width the font gives the character (Go Mono gives the C0 controls a full cell); a character with no width (the bidi marks) gets a bar, so the next character is not covered. The Control Pictures glyph is the one the font fallback finds, or the font's own empty-glyph box. Step 5.5 (minimap) and 5.6 should show these decorations only if SPEC §9.5 says so.

## 5.5 Minimap

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-5.5-minimap
- **Summary:** the minimap of SPEC §9.5. `computeMinimapLayout` (a port of VS Code's `_computeMinimapLayout`: width from the room left by the gutter, scale and pixel ratio, `maxColumn`, left or right, `proportional`, `fill` and `fit` with the scale growing up to one more and sampling of the rows when there are too many) and `createMinimapRenderLayout` (`MinimapLayout.create`: the slider's height and place, the first and last line drawn, the padding at the top, the anti-flicker rule against the last layout) are pure and tested by tables. `minimapPainter` draws the lines into premultiplied RGBA pixels (a block of `scale × 2·scale` pixels per character that is not a space, in the color of its token blended into the background, tabs to their stop, full-width characters two blocks) and keeps the rows of the last frame by key (line, row span, text, colors): a frame draws only the rows whose key changed and copies the others to their new place. `RenderEditorMinimap` shows the image (`ui.NewImageFromRGBA`, drawn at the size of the window), the marks of the selections (a half-transparent bar over each selected line and the covered part of the line), the find matches and the text equal to the selection, and the slider (`mouseover` or `always`; hover and drag colors). The editor widget wraps its body in a `LayoutBuilder`, computes the layout from the size of the editor, gives the text area the room (padding on the minimap's side, and the left inset of the horizontal scrollbar) and puts the minimap next to the vertical scrollbar. The pointer: a press on the slider drags it, a press elsewhere scrolls the clicked row to the middle (proportional) or drags from the middle of the slider (fill, fit), the wheel scrolls the editor. New settings `editor.minimap.enabled`, `side`, `size`, `showSlider`, `scale`, `renderCharacters`, `maxColumn`; new colors `minimap.background`, `foregroundOpacity`, `selectionHighlight`, `findMatchHighlight`, `selectionOccurrenceHighlight`, `minimapSlider.background`, `hoverBackground` and `activeBackground`.
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/editor/{minimap,minimap_layout,minimap_render,minimap_paint}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{widget,viewmodel,options,tokens}.go`, `internal/gui/kit/theme.go`, `internal/core/{settings/builtin,theme/colors_builtin}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.5.
- **Tests:** layout: 12 layouts (default, capped by `maxColumn`, left, scale 2, two pixels per pixel, `fill` of 10 and 30 rows, `fit` short and long, `fill` with sampling, off, no room), the sampling (582 lines for 1,000 rows, the first lines, row to line), 10 slider and line cases (short and long texts at the top, middle and end, a partial first line, scrolling up and down against the last layout, another text, `fill`) and the slider arithmetic; the expected values come from a second implementation of VS Code's formulas, since VS Code has no test of its layout. Painter: the blocks of a line pixel by pixel (gutter, spaces, tabs, empty line, full-width), colors and opacity, the right edge, scale 2 and one-pixel lines, a translucent background, a frame that changed nothing, one line edited or colored (1 drawn, 9 copied), scrolling by a line (the same pixels as a frame drawn from scratch), padding at the top, a jump, an empty canvas. View model: the pointer with no minimap, a click revealing the row in the middle, a press on the slider and the drag (from where it began, ended by the release), `fill` dragging from the middle, the rows of the sampled lines, hover and the change notices. Widget: the text loses the minimap's width, on the left the text is shifted and clicks in the text land right, off and in a large file, only the changed line is repainted after an edit and after a scroll, a click reveals the line, dragging the slider scrolls, hover, the wheel; goldens `minimap` (a selection on the minimap, the slider) and `minimap_left_find` (left, with find matches), each viewed zoomed.
- **Not ported:** `editor.minimap.autohide`, the section headers (`showMarkSectionHeaders`, `showRegionSectionHeaders`, `sectionHeaderFontSize`...), the character rendering (always blocks, so lines are 3 pixels at scale 1 where VS Code's default is 2), touch gestures, the shadow while the text is scrolled sideways, marks for the diff, the problems and the git changes (later steps), the smooth scroll of a click, the memory VS Code keeps of the last layout against the loop of `fit` with wrapped text.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:**
  ![5.5 minimap](implemented-proof-images/5.5-minimap.png)
  `scripts/proof.sh docs/implemented-proof-images/5.5-minimap.png --after 3s -- internal/gui/editor/widget.go`: the editor in a headless window with a Go file, the minimap at the right of the text next to the scrollbar, its lines in the colors of the tokens, as I saw by viewing the image. (The plan lists no proof for this step.)
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the line height of the minimap is that of the blocks mode for every value of `renderCharacters`. The first minimap line of a sampled minimap shows the row VS Code's formula gives it (its code writes the first entry twice). The wheel over the minimap goes through the editor's own wheel handler. The minimap is a stack child above the text and next to the scrollbar; with the horizontal scrollbar visible it covers the bottom of the minimap, as in VS Code. Sticky scroll (5.6) and the breadcrumbs (5.7) sit above or below the editor and need no change; the diff editor (9.x) will give each side its own minimap settings.

## 5.6 Sticky scroll

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-5.6-sticky-scroll
- **Summary:** sticky scroll of SPEC §9.6. `newStickyTree` turns the folding regions (at least two lines) into a tree; `stickyTree.candidates` and `vm.stickyLinesAt(top)` choose the lines that stick for a scroll position (a region sticks when the slot of its depth is below the natural y of its start line, and until the slot reaches the bottom of its end line, when the last sticky line is pushed up by `Offset`), at most `min(editor.stickyScroll.maxLineCount, 25% of the viewport rows)`, never the lines a fold hides. `RenderEditorSticky` paints the lines over the top of the text in `editorStickyScroll.*` colors with the gutter (line numbers, folding controls), the hover, a border and a gradient shadow, clipped to the pushed height; the last line is drawn first so it slides in under the others. The widget is a stack child inset by the left minimap and takes the pointer only over the lines. A click moves the cursor and scrolls the line clear of the sticky lines (`RevealStickyPosition`); a click on the folding control folds; Shift click reveals the end of the range. `RevealPosition` now keeps a revealed row clear of the rows that may be sticky while sticky scroll is on. Settings `editor.stickyScroll.enabled`, `maxLineCount`, `scrollWithEditor` (registered earlier, now read into `Options.StickyScroll`); new colors `editorStickyScroll.background`, `editorStickyScrollGutter.background`, `editorStickyScrollHover.background`, `editorStickyScroll.border`, `editorStickyScroll.shadow`.
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/editor/{sticky,sticky_paint}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{widget,viewmodel,options}.go`, `internal/gui/kit/theme.go`, `internal/core/{settings/builtin,theme/colors_builtin}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.6.
- **Tests:** tree and candidates tables (nested regions, equal starts, single-line regions, folded lines hidden, the limit by setting and by viewport), the lines for scroll positions in nested code including the push-up at the end of a region, the reveal padding table (on/off, near the top, above the screen), hover and click positions in the view model; widget tests (the lines appear on scroll, clicks land on the line and column, the folding control, Shift click, the pointer passes through below the lines, the minimap inset, off by setting); options read from the settings; goldens `sticky_scroll` (three nested headers) and `sticky_scroll_pushed` (the last header pushed up at the end of its range), each viewed.
- **Not ported:** the outline model of language servers (the candidates come from folding ranges; area 3 may add them), `editor.stickyScroll.defaultModel`, the keyboard commands (`focusStickyScroll`, `selectNext`/`Previous`, `goToFocusedStickyScrollLine`, `selectEditor`), the context menu, sticky lines in the diff editor, animation of the changes.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none
- **Proof:** none here; step 5.7's proof shows the sticky lines with the breadcrumbs
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the candidates are folding regions, so a header that VS Code's outline model would show but the indentation or grammar folding does not (or the reverse) differs. The sticky widget is repainted by the scroll controller's listener. The breadcrumbs (5.7) sit above the editor and need no change here.

## 5.8 Snippet parser and variables

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-5.8-snippet-parser
- **Summary:** `core/snippet` reads VS Code's snippet grammar (SPEC §9.9.1): a port of `SnippetParser` (the scanner, the marker tree of text, placeholders, choices, variables, transforms and format strings under a `TextmateSnippet`, the parent links, `Replace`, `Walk`, `Offset`, `EnclosingPlaceholders`, `ToTextmateString`, `Clone`, default values of repeated placeholders with cyclic references cut, the final tab stop, `ParseFragment` for the session of 5.9) and of the variable resolvers over plain values (selection, file, clipboard, comment, time, workspace, random, composite) with `SelectionValuesOf` to gather the selection's values from a document. Transforms run on `core/regex` (ECMAScript syntax, flags `dgimsuvy`, a search limited to one second) and the case shorthands (`upcase`, `downcase`, `capitalize`, `pascalcase`, `camelcase`, `kebabcase`, `snakecase`) handle Unicode letters. Invalid syntax stays text, as in VS Code. Lengths and offsets are bytes.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/snippet/{scanner,marker,parser,transform,variables}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.9.1.
- **Tests:** ported all 54 tests of `snippetParser.test.ts` (as tables: the scanner, escapes, text, the text-and-marker table of 54 cases, transforms, choices, `toTextmateString` and its identity, real-world snippets, default placeholder values, markers' lengths, parents, offsets, `replace`, placeholder order, the shorthand and Unicode case tables, and the regression cases of the issues named in them; the checks that need JavaScript's `RegExp` objects read the pattern and flags of the `Transform` instead) and 16 of the 17 tests of `snippetVariables.test.ts` (the one skipped, #76840, is about VS Code's label service; the others that used its text model, label and workspace services and `sinon` timers are rewritten for the plain-value resolvers, with a fixed moment in several zones). More cases not in VS Code: scanner tokens in bytes, the flags and the failures of `NewTransform` by route (`NewTransform->Transform.init.SnippetInvalidFlags`), `Source()` of patterns, transform replacing (`g`, `i`, `y`, `s`, `m`, empty matches, groups that did not match, multi-byte text), the random and clipboard resolvers, re-indentation of a selection, the overtyped text, `ParseFragment`. A seeded property test (30,000 snippets of the pieces of the syntax) and a fuzz target `FuzzParse` check that every snippet parses to a consistent tree (parents right, no two texts side by side), resolves, clones and serializes to something that parses; the default run covers the corpus of the cases.
- **Not ported:** `OvertypingCapturer` (the session of 5.9 gathers it into `Overtyped`), the label service (`FileResolver` takes paths), localized day and month names, JavaScript's `RegExp` details that `core/regex` does not have (a regular expression of the snippet is checked when the snippet is parsed, and a snippet whose regular expression `core/regex` cannot compile stays text).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none. `FuzzParse` ran 220,000 inputs under `-parallel=1` and a memory limit without a finding.
- **Proof:** none
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** `Marker.replace` of a marker that is not found does nothing (VS Code's `splice(-1)` would remove the last child). A placeholder index too big for an int is text. A search of a transform that runs past its limit ends the replacing instead of failing. `CURRENT_TIMEZONE_NAME` is the name of the zone of the moment unless the caller gives the IANA name (5.9 should). CLAUDE.md got a section about memory (a fuzz run without limits was killed for using too much memory).

## 5.12 Large files and long lines

- **Date:** 2026-10-23
- **Branch:** feat/step-5.12-large-files
- **Summary:** SPEC §6.4 end to end. Large file mode (from 1.4) was verified feature by feature: the tokenizer, bracket pairs, folding, minimap, word wrap and the highlights already checked it; sticky scroll did not and now does. The window posts one warning (`LargeFileNotice`) for each large document, and the new setting `editor.largeFileOptimizations` (default true) turns the mode off (`Documents.SetLargeFileOptimizations`, `AnnounceLarge`). Long lines: a row is laid out and drawn only up to `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter` bytes (`shownLength`); `geometry` works out columns beyond it with the width of a character (`x`, `rowEnd`, `positionAt`, `rectOf`), and the scroll extent counts the hidden bytes. `editor.maxTokenizationLineLength` was already wired to the grammar (checked). A file that looks binary opens as `editor.Notice` with an "Open Anyway" button (click, Enter, Space) which reads it again with `AllowBinary` (`Documents.OpenFileWith`); a file over the limit fails with `FileTooLarge` and a notification. `BenchmarkOpen200MB` and the rows in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. New colors `button.foreground/background/hoverBackground/border` and `descriptionForeground` (also in `kit.Colors`).
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/editor/{geometry,render,notice,sticky}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{app,devopen,window,theme}.go`, `internal/core/settings/builtin.go`, `internal/core/theme/colors_builtin.go`, `internal/gui/kit/theme.go`, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, `docs/SPEC.md` §6.4.
- **Tests:** `shownLength` table (8 cases, no cut inside a character), positions beyond the drawn part (x, row end, the column of a point and back, the rectangle of a character, far to the right), a line cut at a character, a 5 MB single line (word wrap on) that is shown and moved in, the large-file mode table (word wrap, sticky scroll, highlights, with and without; the other features have their tests in `tokens`, `brackets`, `folding`, `minimap`), the notice (click, Enter, Space, another key, no action) and its two goldens `notice_dark.png`/`notice_light.png` (looked at), the shell showing the binary notice and opening anyway (and the failure kept as a notification and the notice staying), the large file notification once and not for a small document, `editor.largeFileOptimizations` off, and the `FileBinary` and `FileTooLarge` routes.
- **Not ported:** VS Code's "renderValidationDecorations", semantic highlighting and word-based suggestions switches of large file mode (those features do not exist yet).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none. `BenchmarkOpen200MB`: 361 ms, 1.15 GB allocated.
- **Proof:** none
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter` counts bytes, not UTF-16 units; a limit of zero means no limit (VS Code would draw nothing); a binary file blocks the whole window until the workbench (6.x) has tabs to show the notice in; the benchmark's 200 MB read allocates about 1.15 GB (text and buffer), so the memory of opening the largest file is about six times its size.

## 6.9 Editor grid

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-6.9-editor-grid
- **Summary:** several editor groups (SPEC §3.2, §10.3). `editorgroup.Grid` is a tree of splits whose leaves are groups (the root is always a split, a split never has one child, sizes are shares of 1): add, remove, merge, move and copy groups, split in every direction, move and copy editors between groups (a moved editor keeps its input and so its view model), maximize and restore, even sizes, neighbours by box geometry, groups by index and in most-recently-used order, and `RestoreGrid`/state in and out for 7.5. `Model.Clone`, the `Copier` interface and `TextInput.CopyInput` copy an editor into a split. Decoration owners are now per view model (`document.AllocOwners`; each view model reserves 8 owners with the slots autoClosed 1, folding 2, find 3, word 4, selection 5, snippets 6; the first view model of a document keeps owners 1-6; `snippet.Editor.Owner`), so two editors of one document do not collide. The window shows the grid as nested `kit.SplitView`s of groups (a tab strip and an editor each), sash drags recorded in the grid, the active group shown by the `tab.unfocused*` colors on the others, empty groups with the empty state, a focus request retried for up to 6 frames. The VS Code grid commands (split in four directions and orthogonal, focus and move to a neighbour or numbered group, move and copy groups and editors, join, close group, maximize, even widths, editor layouts), the keys, a View > Editor Layout submenu, `workbench.editor.openSideBySideDirection`, `workbench.editor.closeEmptyGroups` and one more setting, 3 colors, and `dev.openFile`'s `group` argument (tags `DevOpenFileInvalid`, `DevOpenFileGroupInvalid`).
- **Main files:** `internal/core/editorgroup/{grid,grid_editors,grid_state,input,textinput,model}.go`, `internal/core/document/decorations.go`, `internal/core/snippet/session.go`, `internal/gui/editor/*` (owners), `internal/gui/app/{gridview,groupcommands,group,devopen,editors}.go`, `internal/core/{command,keybinding,settings,theme}`, `docs/SPEC.md` §3.2, §7.1, §10.3, §11.2, §15.2.
- **Tests:** about 61 new test functions (33 of grid operation tables: every split direction and operation, closing, merging, maximize and restore, even sizes, neighbours in nested layouts, indices, state round trip; 22 widget tests: splitting through commands and keys, sash drags, focus commands, two editors of one document (an edit in one shows in the other, independent cursors, owners that do not collide), closing a group releasing the document, `dev.openFile` with `group` and its routes), `model_port_test.go` now ports 33 of the 49 tests of `editorGroupModel.test.ts`; 6 goldens (`grid_two_groups`, `grid_three_groups`, `grid_empty_group`, Dark and Light; looked at) and the regenerated View menu goldens of the workbench.
- **Not ported:** the commands that expand a group (`minimizeOtherEditors`, `minimizeOtherEditorsHideSidebar`, `toggleEditorWidths`), `maximizeEditorHideSidebar`, moving by tab index other than for the active editor.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.

## 6.10 Tab interactions

## 6.13 Workspace model and watcher

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-6.13-workspace
- **Summary:** `core/workspace` (SPEC §10.5). `Open(ctx, path)` opens the window's folder as a `Workspace` with an `Item` tree read lazily (errors per directory kept on the item, symlink loops not followed), the sort orders of `explorer.sortOrder` (`default`, `mixed`, `filesFirst`, `type`, `modified`, `foldersNestsFiles` like `default`; lexicographic options and reverse) with VS Code's comparers on `golang.org/x/text/collate`, `files.exclude` (dropped at read time), compact folder chains (`explorer.compactFolders`, as `ExplorerCompressionDelegate`), `Refresh`, and `Apply` of watcher events keeping the loaded state. The watcher uses inotify through `golang.org/x/sys/unix` (no cgo): the folder recursively (new subfolders get watches, `files.watcherExclude`/`files.watcherInclude`), the parents of open files outside it, events coalesced over 50 ms with VS Code's `EventCoalescer` rules plus inotify move pairing (cookie renames, atomic save by rename is a `Changed` of the target), own writes dropped through `Suppress(path, FileStat)`, and a polling fallback (no inotify, `ENOSPC`, forced) with one notice per kind. The window wires it: `cmd/emetos <folder>` opens the workspace, settings (user and `<folder>/.emetos/settings.json`) and snippet files are reloaded through the watcher, an `explorer.*`/`files.exclude` change refreshes the tree, the breadcrumbs are folder-relative, the title uses the folder, `WORKSPACE_NAME`, `WORKSPACE_FOLDER` and `RELATIVE_FILEPATH` get values, watcher notices become one warning notification each. Settings registered: `files.exclude`, `files.watcherExclude`, `files.watcherInclude`, `explorer.sortOrder`, `explorer.sortOrderLexicographicOptions`, `explorer.sortOrderReverse`, `explorer.compactFolders`.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/workspace/*.go`, `internal/gui/app/{workspace,window,process,app,editors,gridview}.go`, `cmd/emetos/main.go`, `internal/core/settings/builtin.go`, `go.mod` (`golang.org/x/sys` is now a direct dependency, same version), `docs/SPEC.md` §10.5, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`.
- **Tests:** 52 test functions in `core/workspace` (141 passing sub-results: model, apply, coalescing with a fake clock, comparers, real-inotify watcher tests and polling-mode runs: create, change, delete, renames, replace by rename, own writes, nested folders, excluded folders, outside files, unwatch, ctx cancel, `ENOSPC` and init-failure fallbacks, queue overflow), 10 in `gui/app` (folder open and missing folder, settings and snippet reload through the watcher end to end, following open files outside the folder, folder-relative breadcrumbs and title, `WORKSPACE_*` in a snippet); a route test for every new tag (three of them skip as root); no goldens changed; no proof image.
- **Not ported:** multi-root workspaces, file nesting, `explorer.excludeGitIgnore`, Open Folder and Close Folder commands, the explorer view (6.14), file operations, `files.exclude` in the Problems panel and the breadcrumbs picker, renames in the polling fallback, keybindings reload (no user keymap yet), `Suppress` wiring (`TODO(step 7.1)`: no save command exists yet).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.
- **Proof:** none (the step has none; the explorer comes in 6.14)
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** `gluttertest.Tester` does not dispose the widget tree at the end of a test, so state `Lifetime()`s are never cancelled; workaround `ProcessOptions.WatchFiles` (tests leave it off, the editor sets it) in `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** names compare with the root collation, not the user's locale; a first save of a new file by rename arrives as `Changed` (`Apply` adds unknown paths); symlinked folders are not watched unless listed in `files.watcherInclude`; `Watch` reads the tree synchronously, so the app calls it from a goroutine.

## 6.16 Fuzzy scorer

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-6.16-fuzzy-scorer
- **Summary:** `core/fuzzy` (SPEC §10.6), a port of VS Code's `fuzzyScorer.ts` and the `fuzzyScore` part of `filters.ts`: `PrepareQuery` (multi-word values, path separators, quoted contiguous queries), `Scorer` (owns the scratch buffers; one per goroutine) with `ScoreFuzzy`, `ScoreFuzzy2` and `FuzzyScore`, the generic `ScoreItemFuzzy`/`CompareItemsByFuzzyScore` over an `ItemAccessor` (label, description, path) with a hash-keyed `Cache`, `CreateMatches`, `MatchesPrefix`. ## 7.1 Saving

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.1-saving
- **Summary:** saving and reverting (SPEC §3.1, §6.3, §7.1). `document.Save`/`SaveAs`/`Revert` run in three steps: `BeginSave` on the UI thread (runs the participants, captures the text and the version), `SaveJob.Write` on a goroutine (atomic temp-file write through `fileio.Write`, mode kept, owner and group kept best effort, symlink targets written, `WriteOptions.IfUnchanged` fails with `FileModifiedSince` when the file changed since the document last saw it, a deleted file is recreated), and `FinishSave` on the UI thread (the saved version is the version that was written, so a document edited during the write stays dirty and the next save does not conflict with its own write; a second request for the same document waits and runs again). `Overwrite` handles read-only files and Save As over an existing file, `IgnoreConflict` skips the conflict check (the Overwrite button and `files.saveConflictResolution` `overwriteFileOnDisk`). Save participants (`edit.SaveParticipants`, a port of `saveParticipants.ts`): `files.trimTrailingWhitespace`, `files.insertFinalNewline`, `files.trimFinalNewlines`, in that order as one undoable batch, with the cursor-line exception for auto save (`SaveAuto`); language-scoped values honored. Untitled documents: `Documents.NewUntitled` (lowest free `Untitled-N`, `files.defaultLanguage`, dirty means "has text"), Save As re-keys the document, re-detects the language, keeps the undo history, and the editor input follows (`InputCapabilities`). Save As uses the portal dialog on a goroutine; when it is unavailable a quick input path prompt (`Controller.Prompt`, with validation messages) takes over; an existing target asks "Replace". Save All saves the files and runs Save As for each untitled one, stopping when one is cancelled. Errors are notifications with Retry, Save As and, for conflicts, Overwrite and Revert, one per document. `Watcher.Suppress` is called after every write (the `TODO(step 7.1)` of 6.13). "Save with Encoding" is in the encoding picker. Commands: `workbench.action.files.save` (Ctrl+S), `saveAs` (Ctrl+Shift+S), `saveAll`, `revert`, `newUntitledFile` (Ctrl+N), `saveWithoutFormatting` (Ctrl+K S); File menu rows New Text File, Save, Save As..., Save All, Revert File; Save and Save As in the tab menu of a dirty tab; settings `files.trimTrailingWhitespace`, `files.insertFinalNewline`, `files.trimFinalNewlines`, `files.defaultLanguage`, `files.saveConflictResolution`; context keys `activeEditorIsDirty`, `activeEditorCanRevert`, `dirtyWorkingCopies`.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/document/save.go`, `internal/core/edit/saveparticipants.go`, `internal/core/fileio/{write,fsys_linux}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/saveparticipants.go`, `internal/gui/app/{save,window,app,group,statuspickers}.go`, `internal/gui/quickinput/{controller,picker,host}.go`, `internal/core/editorgroup/{textinput,input}.go`, `internal/core/{command,keybinding,settings}`, `docs/SPEC.md` §3.1, §6.2, §6.3, §7.1, §10.3, §10.5, §10.6, §11.2.

## 7.2 Closing with unsaved changes

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.2-closing
- **Summary:** prompts when editors, groups or the window close (SPEC §10.3, §10.10, §10.11). `editorgroup.PlanClose(grid, targets)` is a pure-Go planner: it returns the dirty editors among the ones about to close whose document no staying editor shows, each document once (a dirty document open in another editor or group does not ask until its last editor closes; an empty untitled document is clean). Every way of closing goes through one app function (`closeConfirmed`/`closeEditors`): tab X and middle click, Ctrl+W, all the close commands (`closeUnmodifiedEditors` never asks), Open Editors X, the switcher's X, Close Folder and Open Folder (the 6.14 refusal is replaced by the dialog). One dialog per batch: "Do you want to save the changes you made to {name}?" or "...to the following N files?" with the names listed (ten, then "...N additional files not shown") and "Your changes will be lost if you don't save them."; buttons Save ("Save All" for several, default), Don't Save, Cancel (Escape). Save runs the 7.1 pipeline in order (untitled documents through Save As); a failed save, a cancelled Save As or a document edited meanwhile cancels the whole close; Don't Save closes without touching the files. While the dialog is open or its saves run, other requests that would ask are ignored (re-entry guard). Window close: `Window.RequestClose(reason)` (per window, for 7.8) runs the planner over all editors and the dialog, then closes through the injectable `Window.Quit` seam or `ExitApplication(Required)`; the Glutter hook for the implicit first window is the app-exit request (an `AppLifecycleListener.OnExitRequested` that calls `RequestClose` and returns cancel at once). Commands `workbench.action.closeWindow` (Alt+F4, Ctrl+Shift+W) and `workbench.action.quit` (Ctrl+Q), File menu rows Close Window and Exit; setting `files.hotExit` (`off`, `onExit`, `onExitAndWindowClose`, default `onExit`), for which `shouldAskBeforeClose` returns "ask" until 7.6.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/editorgroup/closeplan.go`, `internal/gui/app/{closing,app,window,group,groupcommands,explorer,switcher}.go`, `internal/core/{settings,command,keybinding}`, `docs/SPEC.md` §3.1, §10.3, §10.10, §10.11, §11.2, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`.

## 7.3 Auto save

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.3-auto-save
- **Summary:** `files.autoSave` (SPEC §3.1, §6.3, §10.3, §10.10). `document.AutoSave` is a pure-Go controller (no I/O, no goroutines, injectable clock and host) with the modes `off`, `afterDelay`, `onFocusChange`, `onWindowChange`: `afterDelay` keeps a timer per document restarted on every edit (the save happens `files.autoSaveDelay` after the last edit; a save, an undo back to clean or a revert cancels it); `onFocusChange` saves when the editor widget loses focus (decided one frame later), when another editor or group becomes active, and when the window loses focus; `onWindowChange` saves everything dirty when the window loses focus. Eligibility: never untitled, virtual or read-only documents; `files.autoSaveWorkspaceFilesOnly` excludes files outside the folder; `files.autoSaveWhenNoErrors` holds a document with an error marker back until the markers change; a document with a Save As dialog open is left alone. A failed save, manual or auto, pauses auto save for that document (VS Code's conflict/error state) until a save succeeds or the file is read again; the single sticky notification per document stays. Only the `afterDelay` timer saves with `SaveAuto` (the trim-whitespace participant keeps the cursor line); focus saves use the new `SaveFocusChange` and `SaveWindowChange` reasons, which trim like an explicit save, as VS Code does. Changing the setting at runtime saves the dirty documents at once when auto save is on (VS Code's `onDidChangeAutoSaveConfiguration`). Closing an editor with `onFocusChange` or `onWindowChange` saves the savable dirty documents first (awaited, in order) and the 7.2 dialog asks only about what is still dirty (a failed save stays in the dialog, Cancel keeps saved content saved); closing the window saves every dirty savable document in any mode but `off` first; "Don't Save" can never be undone by a focus save. `workbench.action.toggleAutoSave` (File > Auto Save, a checked row by `config.files.autoSave != 'off'`; it writes the user settings, or the workspace settings when the workspace sets the key); keybinding `when` clauses now resolve `config.*` settings.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/document/{autosave,save}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{autosave,app,closing,editors,gridview,group,keys,save}.go`, `internal/core/{settings,command}`, `docs/SPEC.md` §3.1, §6.3, §10.3, §10.10, §11.2.

## 7.4 External changes

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.4-external-changes
- **Summary:** files changed on disk (SPEC §3.1, §6.3, §10.3, §10.5). A watcher event is only a trigger: the window stats (and if needed reads) the file on a goroutine and applies the result on the UI thread (`Document.BeginExternal` → `ExternalJob.Probe` → `ApplyExternal`), so repeated or late events are harmless; a look is repeated if the document was saved, edited, reloaded or renamed meanwhile (at most 3 times), a save in flight defers it, a read that fails or a file that changes during the read is retried after 300 ms and 2 s and on the next event. A clean document reloads in its current encoding keeping cursors, scroll and folds (undo history is dropped as `Reload` does, kept when only the mtime changed). A dirty document is never touched: it is marked conflicted and one sticky warning per document says "The file 'x' has changed on disk and you have unsaved changes." with Overwrite (save with `IgnoreConflict`) and Revert (Compare comes with 9.6); the note goes away on save, revert or reload, when the file returns to the same stat, on close, or when the changes are undone (then the clean document reloads). A deleted file leaves the document orphaned with its text and dirty state kept; the tab and the Open Editors row are struck through in `list.errorForeground` (setting `workbench.editor.decorations.colors`), the tooltip reads "title • Deleted", with `workbench.editor.closeOnFileDelete` the clean editors close; saving recreates the file and clears the flag; when the file reappears a clean document reloads, a dirty one with the same stat just clears the flag, a dirty one with another stat is conflicted. Paired `Renamed` events re-point the documents through the code path shared with the Explorer operations (`followPaths`, refactored out of `followFileOp`: tab, language, recent files, history, every open file below a renamed folder; the echo of an own rename changes nothing); an unpaired rename is a delete. Deleted or renamed folders and Rescan events touch every open document below the path; untitled and virtual documents are ignored. Conflicted and orphaned documents are not auto saved (also not on close and shutdown).
- **Main files:** `internal/core/document/{external,document,edits,save,autosave}.go`, `internal/core/editorgroup/{input,textinput}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{external,app,editors,explorer,fileops,gridview,group,save,statuspickers,workspace}.go`, `internal/gui/kit/{tabs,theme}.go`, `internal/gui/views/explorer/openeditors.go`, `internal/core/{settings,theme}`, `docs/SPEC.md` §3.1, §6.3, §10.3, §10.5, §11.2.
- **Tests:** 27 top-level tests in `core/document/external_test.go` (every case in a temp folder, route tests for `ExternalNoFile`, `ExternalStatFailed`, `ExternalReadFailed`), 24 in `gui/app/external_test.go` (events through `Window.onFileEvents`; view preservation; the single notification and both buttons; auto save blocking; the 7.2 prompt; the `closeOnFileDelete` table; save recreating a file; directory rename and delete; Rescan; read-failure retries; two end-to-end tests with the real inotify watcher: the folder and a file outside it), the tabs strikethrough widget test, a deleted-input test, a color test; 4 goldens (`external_changes_{dark,light}`, `tabs_deleted_{dark,light}`; looked at).
- **Not ported:** Compare (9.6, `TODO(step 9.6)`), `workbench.editor.decorations.badges`, "(deleted)" in the tab name.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.

## 7.5 UI state and restore

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.5-ui-state
- **Summary:** the window's UI state is saved and restored (SPEC §10.10). `core/storage.StateStore` keeps `state.json` (global: recently opened folders and files with VS Code's MRU rules, 500 each, no repeats, git temp files skipped; the last window; the last geometry; the id of the empty window) and `windows/<id>.json` (one per window) under `XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos`, JSON with `version` 1, mode 0600 (folders 0700), written atomically through a debounced writer (a change is encoded on the UI thread 250 ms later and the store writes 1 s after that, as the SPEC says; close, quit and shell disposal write at once; a failed write is logged and retried on the next change; a corrupt or newer file is ignored with a warning and overwritten later). The window id is `WindowID(folder)`: the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the cleaned absolute path; the window without a folder gets a random id kept in `state.json`. A window's state holds the folder, the layout, the geometry (size, maximized, full screen; no position), the editor groups (tree and sizes, editors with pinned, preview and sticky state, order of use, active editor) with each editor's view state (cursors, scroll, folds; `ViewState` is now versioned JSON), the expanded Explorer folders and the quick-open recent list. Restore (`Window.PrepareRestore`, in `Run` before the window shows): the saved files open synchronously and the shell builds the grid from them; editors whose files are gone are dropped with one notification ("1 editor could not be restored because its file no longer exists." / "N editors could not be restored because their files no longer exist."); with no arguments the last window's folder reopens; a file argument opens on top of the restored editors; `window.restoreWindows=none` restores nothing; the geometry goes through `WindowConfig` (`window.restoreFullscreen` for full screen). File > Open Recent (Reopen Closed Editor, folders, files (10 each, only existing paths, `~` paths), More..., Clear Recently Opened...) and Ctrl+R (`workbench.action.openRecent`: a picker with "folders" and "files" sections and a remove button per row); `workbench.action.clearRecentFiles` asks for confirmation as VS Code does and clears both lists, the quick-open list and the editor history. Settings `window.restoreWindows` (default `all`), `window.restoreFullscreen` (false). Also in this commit range: the test infrastructure fix (below).
- **Main files:** `internal/core/storage/{windowid,recent,statefiles,writer,statestore,paths}.go`, `internal/core/storage/storagetest/clock.go`, `internal/core/editorgroup/{serialize,grid_state}.go`, `internal/core/workspace/recent.go`, `internal/gui/editor/viewstate_json.go`, `internal/gui/app/{state,recent,app,process,window,group,editors,explorer,workspace,closing,save}.go`, `internal/core/{command,keybinding,settings}`, `docs/SPEC.md` §3.1, §10.3, §10.10 ("UI state as built"), §11.2.

## 7.6 Hot exit

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.6-hot-exit
- **Summary:** backups of unsaved work and their restore (SPEC §3.1, §10.10 "Hot exit as built (step 7.6)", §10.11). `storage.BackupStore` keeps one JSON file per document at `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/backups/<window id>/<SHA-256 hex of the URI>.json` (mode 0600, atomic; fields `version`, `uri`, `content`, `encoding`, `bom`, `lineEnding`, `language`, `stat` (mtime ns, size, mode), `orphaned`), with `Write`, `Read`, `List`, `Discard`, `DiscardAll`, `Check` (removes unusable files and leftover `.tmp` files at start) and the crash marker `running` in the same folder. `storage.BackupTracker` (injectable clock) writes a backup 1 s after the last change of a dirty document (a burst makes one write), discards it when the document is clean again, closed with Save or Don't Save, or renamed (it moves), skips empty untitled and read-only documents and texts over 100 MiB (the user is told once and closing falls back to the dialog), and `Prepare`/`BackupBatch.Write` read the texts on the UI thread and write on a goroutine. `closeDecision(hotExit, reason, hasFolder, otherWindows)` replaces the 7.2 stub: `off` always asks; `onExit` backs up on quit or when the last window closes and asks when another window closes; `onExitAndWindowClose` also backs up when a window with a folder closes; with one window both modes back up on close; if a backup fails the 7.2 dialog asks instead and Cancel keeps the window open; Save or Don't Save in the dialog removes the window's backups; closing an editor, group or folder still asks and removes that document's backup. The signal path writes the backups and removes the marker. Restore (inside `PrepareRestore`, whatever `files.hotExit` says at start and `window.restoreWindows`): a file with a backup is read from disk and the backup text is put over it as one undoable edit (`Document.RestoreUnsaved`: dirty, one undo returns to the disk text, encoding, BOM, line ending and language from the backup); untitled backups come back with their numbers (`TextInput.Serialize` now serializes untitled inputs as `untitled:N`; new untitled documents take the lowest free number); a file changed on disk since the backup is restored conflicted with the backup's stat (the 7.4 sticky notification is the only one: "'x' has changed on disk since its backup was made..." with Overwrite and Revert; a save raises `FileModifiedSince`); a deleted file is restored orphaned with one warning for all such files; a backup that no saved editor shows opens at the end of the active group in URI order; a leftover crash marker with restored backups gives one info notification ("Emetos did not close properly the last time. The unsaved changes of N files were restored from backups."); a backup equal to the disk text or unrestorable is removed.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/storage/{backup,backuptracker}.go`, `internal/core/document/restore.go`, `internal/core/editorgroup/textinput.go`, `internal/gui/app/{backup,backuprestore,closing,state,window,group,app,process,external}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §3.1, §10.3, §10.10, §10.11.
- **Tests:** 8 in `storage/backup_test.go`, 19 in `backuptracker_test.go` (fake clock: delay and bursts, discards, rename, orphaned flag, empty untitled, mode `off`, shutdown flush, no timers left), 3 in `document/restore_test.go`, 19 in `gui/app/backup_test.go` (quit backs up without a dialog and the next start restores dirty text, untitled documents, groups and cursors; mode `off` asks and discards; changed on disk; deleted; a crash restored with `off` at the next start; a backup write failure falls back to the dialog; an editor close still asks; untitled numbering; a corrupt backup ignored; backups without editors; the signal path; the decision table); route tests for `BackupWriteFailed`, `BackupTooLarge`, `BackupURIInvalid`, `BackupReadFailed`, `BackupNotFound`, `BackupCorrupt`, `BackupDiscardFailed`, `BackupMarkerFailed`, `BackupWaitCancelled`, `SavedUntitledWithoutBackup` (`BackupEncodeFailed` has none: `json.Marshal` of a `Backup` cannot fail); no goldens (no new UI); the test helpers `newTestWindow`, `settingsWindow` and `newStateEnv` default to `files.hotExit: off` so the 7.2 dialog tests keep working.
- **Not ported:** multi-window rules (7.8, `otherWindows()` is a stub with `TODO(step 7.8)`), remote files, `window.confirmBeforeClose`, a "Restore Backup" command.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.
