## 7.7 Command line and single instance

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.7-command-line
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.11's command line and `core/ipc`. `cmd/emetos` has a hand-written parser (`parseArgs`: `--x v`, `--x=v`, `-xv`, clustered `-nw`, `--`, repeated options, value counts) for `-n/--new-window`, `-r/--reuse-window`, `-g/--goto file[:line[:col]]`, `-d/--diff a b`, `-m/--merge p1 p2 base result`, `-w/--wait`, `--profile`, `--log`, `-v/--version`, `-h/--help`; `--help` and `--version` exit 0 before the window, the socket or the log is touched, a wrong command line exits 2, a failed request exits 1. `core/ipc` (the only package that imports `net`): a unix-socket server and client at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/emetos-<uid>.sock` with `emetos-<uid>.lock` beside it (fallback `<tmp>/emetos-<uid>/emetos.sock` in a real 0700 folder owned by the user; a path over 107 bytes is `IPCSocketPathTooLong` and the editor then starts without single instance), socket mode 0600, one JSON object per line at most 1 MiB (`{version:1,type:"open",pid,cwd,open:{folder,files[{path,line,column}],diff,merge,wait,newWindow,reuseWindow,profile}}`, replies `ok`, `done` or `error` with `exitCode` and `message`), the peer uid checked with `SO_PEERCRED`, a request must arrive within 5 s, a non-wait reply within 30 s. The race of two launches: `Join` takes an exclusive `flock` on the lock file, tries to connect, and if nobody answers listens before releasing the lock (a refused connect removes the stale socket first), so exactly one launch becomes the instance and the others hand over; a path that is not a socket of the user is `IPCSocketBusy` and left alone; `Close` removes the socket only if it is still the file this server made (device and inode). `--wait` keeps the connection open and the instance replies `done` when every file of that launch is closed (the window closing first gives `done` 0; files asked for but none opened gives 1; a killed client drops the connection and cancels the wait). In the running window (`Window.HandleLaunch`, requests that arrive before the window is on screen wait in the `Launcher` queue): the window is raised through the controller's `Activate`, a different folder opens through Open Folder with the dirty prompts (Cancel keeps the folder but the files still open), files open kept with the first shown and the `--goto` position revealed and clamped, `--diff` and `--merge` show "The diff editor is not available yet." / "The merge editor is not available yet." and reply exit 1, `--profile` shows a warning and is ignored (`TODO(step 8.6)`), `--new-window` shows "Multiple windows are not available yet: this window is used." (7.8). The first instance's own command line goes through the same code (`Options.Open`).
- **Main files:** `internal/core/ipc/{message,location,join,server,client}.go`, `cmd/emetos/{main,args}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{launch,app,window,group,explorer,process}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §10.11, §12, §15.1, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`.
- **Tests:** 32 in `core/ipc` (in-process: round trip, bad version, type, JSON and oversize messages, peer rejection, handler panic, stale socket takeover, a socket owned by another instance kept, concurrent clients, wait and done, a dropped client cancels the wait, graceful shutdown, lock timeout, a race of 6 joins; two-process tests that re-exec the test binary (`EMETOS_IPC_HELPER`, no window, each in its own process group with a deadline): hand-over with the cwd, `--wait` released over stdin, a killed client cancelling the wait, a stale socket after `kill -9` taken over by the next launch, and the 4-way race of launches over 3 rounds with exactly one server; every `IPC*` tag with a route test), 14 in `cmd/emetos` (parser tables for every option form and tag `ArgsUnknownOption`, `ArgsMissingValue`, `ArgsValueUnexpected`, `ArgsRepeated`, `ArgsConflict`, `ArgsStdinUnsupported`, `ArgsGotoInvalid`, `ArgsProfileInvalid`, `LogLevelInvalid`, `PathInvalid`; `run` exit codes; `handOver` against a real in-process server), 25 in `gui/app/launch_test.go` (`HandleLaunch`, `Launcher`, startup arguments, `WatchClose`); no goldens; nothing registered.
- **Not ported:** a new window for `--new-window` (7.8), the diff and merge editors (9.6, 9.7), profiles (8.6), `window.openFoldersInNewWindow` and `window.openFilesInNewWindow` (the SPEC lists neither and with one window they have no effect).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.
- **Proof:** none
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** the 6.6 entry now also covers `Activate`: `BaseWindowController` lacks it, so the window is raised through an interface assertion.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the SPEC gave no fallback without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` (added the tmp folder one) and no exit code for the diff and merge notices (1, so `git difftool` sees a failure); the parser lives in `cmd/emetos` because SPEC §5.2 has no `cli` package; positional paths are literal (`main.go:3` is a file by that name) and positions come only from `--goto`, parsed strictly; the old `flag`-based parser is gone, so `-version` with one dash no longer works; the race detector makes every exiting helper process sleep 1 s, so the helpers run with `GORACE=atexit_sleep_ms=0`; the 43 MB binary `emetos` that `go build ./cmd/emetos` leaves in the repo root had been committed in step 3.1: it is untracked now and `/emetos` is in `.gitignore` (it stays in the history).

## 7.8 Multiple windows

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-7.8-multiple-windows
- **Summary:** several windows in one process (SPEC §5.1, §10.10, §10.11). `Process.Windows` (`app.Windows`) is the manager: the windows in creation order, the active one, `Open`, `NewWindow`, `OpenFolder` (by the placement rules), `HandleLaunch` (the IPC routing) and `RequestQuit`. Shared by all windows in the `Process`: the command definitions, menus, views, keymap, themes, languages, snippets, the state store and the launcher; per window: its own forked `command.Registry` (`Registry.Fork()`), its own `notify.Service`, shell, editors, backups, explorer, quick input and folder (settings changes reach every window through the shared store; the recent lists and the state are written from the UI thread only). The implicit first window is entry 0 of a Glutter `WindowManager` (shown through `windowHost`); other windows are regular window controllers with their own `windowDelegate`; a closed regular window is unregistered and destroyed, the implicit one is hidden and retired (Glutter cannot drop it). New Window (`workbench.action.newWindow`, Ctrl+Shift+N, File menu) opens an empty window with its own state id (the primary empty id or a fresh random one). Opening a folder follows VS Code's rules for each source (menu, recent, IPC, dev command): a folder already open elsewhere focuses that window, otherwise `window.openFoldersInNewWindow` (`default`, `on`, `off`) decides (Ctrl on a recent row opens a new window; `--new-window` and `--reuse-window` are honored), files follow `window.openFilesInNewWindow`; the same-window case disposes the window's services and recreates them after the 7.2 prompts (`replaceWindow`: a keyed rebuild of the shell), which also restores the new folder's saved state (the 7.5 follow-up). Closing one window while others remain asks per the 7.6 table and only about that window's documents; quit (Ctrl+Q, app exit request) asks window after window (two-phase `closeAsk` then `commitClose`), Cancel anywhere keeps everything, hot exit backs up all windows without asking, and closing the last window quits once. Restore (`Process.startupPlan`): the global state keeps `OpenWindows` and `LastWindow`; `window.restoreWindows` `preserve`, `all`, `folders`, `one`, `none` with command-line folders and files on top; windows with backups always restore. `workbench.action.switchWindow` ("Switch Window...", a picker of the windows); `dev.openFolderInNewWindow {"path"}`; `StateStore.DeleteWindow` removes the state of an explicitly closed extra empty window. Settings `window.openFilesInNewWindow` (default `off`), `window.openFoldersInNewWindow` (default `default`), `window.newWindowDimensions` (default `default`).
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/app/{windows,windows_commands,startup,process,window,app,closing,backup,launch,explorer,recent,state,autosave,devcommands,devnotify}.go`, `internal/core/command/{command,builtin,menus_default}.go`, `internal/core/keybinding/defaults.go`, `internal/core/settings/builtin.go`, `internal/core/storage/{statefiles,statestore,writer,backup}.go`, `internal/gui/workbench/workbench.go`, `internal/gui/views/problems/view.go`, `scripts/proof.sh`, `docs/SPEC.md` §5.1, §10.10, §10.11, §11.2, §15.2, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`, `testdata/proof/7.8/`.
- **Tests:** 31 in `gui/app/windows_test.go` (the manager through `Windows()` and the harness, close order and Cancel, quit with dirty windows in two windows, restore of two windows in every mode, same-window folder replacement with leak checks, IPC routing incl. `--new-window` and `--wait` across windows, focus and active window, auto save on window change, the Switch Window picker, `parseOpenFolderInNewWindow` with tag `DevOpenFolderInvalid`), 7 more in `core/command`, `core/settings` and `core/storage` (`Fork`, the settings, `HasBackups`, `OpenWindows`, `DeleteWindow` with tags `WindowIDInvalid` and `StateDeleteFailed`), the keybinding and File menu rows; the six File menu and Open Recent goldens regenerated for the new "New Window  Ctrl+Shift+N" row (looked at).
- **Not ported:** `window.newWindowDimensions` `inherit` and `offset` (the same as `default` on Wayland, which has no placement API), the quick-input and editor focus observers are not filtered per window (the auto save focus observer is), state files of empty windows left open at quit are not cleaned up (only explicitly closed extra empty windows are deleted).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.
- **Proof:** `docs/implemented-proof-images/7.8-two-windows.png`, made with `scripts/proof.sh docs/implemented-proof-images/7.8-two-windows.png --output --commands '[["dev.openFolderInNewWindow",{"path":"testdata/proof/7.8/second"}]]' -- testdata/proof/7.8/first` (method C: the output of the headless compositor, with `--output` the script now tiles the windows (`HEADLESS_FLOATING=0`) and maps `--after` to `SCREENSHOT_SETTLE`); it shows two Emetos windows side by side: "first - Emetos" with the explorer FIRST (cmd, internal, go.mod, README.md) and "second - Emetos", the active one, with the explorer SECOND (src, tests, package.json, README.md)

  ![7.8 two windows](implemented-proof-images/7.8-two-windows.png)
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** the 7.2 entry is rewritten (the close request of the implicit first window reaches the app without the window and the window cannot be dropped; the workaround takes over `OnExitRequested` and hides it); new: a `Scrollable` that leaves the tree in the same frame after its metrics changed panics (`ScrollPositionBase.post(DidUpdateScrollMetrics)` after dispose; it crashed the tiled proof; workaround marked `// Glutter:`: the Problems panel actions and its filter box stay in the tree, offstage, when there is no room); windows cannot be placed or opened maximized by the controller; the 7.7 `Activate` note was updated.

## 8.2 Settings search and JSON views

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-8.2-settings-search
- **Summary:** search and the JSON commands (SPEC §7.1, §10.3, §11.1, §11.2). `settings.ParseQuery` (VS Code's regexes) and `UIModel.Search(target, text, LanguageResolver)`: `@modified` (settings with a value in the tab's file), `@id:a,b` (comma lists and several `@id:`; case-sensitive; a trailing `*` is a prefix), `@lang:<id or name>` (the language-overridable settings with the values of that language's `[lang]` block; editing writes the block, Reset removes the key and then the empty block), `@tag:`, `@feature:`, `@ext:`, `@hasPolicy`, `@stable` are stripped and ignored with a hint line; free text must match every word (case-insensitive) in the key (camelCase split), the title, the enum values or the description; ranking whole key word 4, key or title part 3, enum value 2, whole description word 2, description part 1, a whole typed key +1000; results are grouped by category in layout order with rows sorted by score (ties keep layout order), Commonly Used hidden while searching; `SearchResult.Summary()` gives "N Settings Found", "1 Setting Found", "No Settings Found". The editor shows the summary and the hints under the search box, a clear button and Escape to clear, tree labels with counts ("Font (4)"), and a "Language: Go" header with a note in `@lang:` mode. `workbench.action.openSettings` takes a string, `{"query"}` or `{"revealSetting":{"key"}}` (query `@id:key`). Commands (category Preferences, palette, VS Code ids): `workbench.action.openSettingsJson` ("Open User Settings (JSON)"), `workbench.action.openWorkspaceSettingsFile` ("Open Workspace Settings (JSON)", palette `when workbenchState != 'empty'`), `workbench.action.openRawDefaultSettings` ("Open Default Settings (JSON)"), `workbench.action.openGlobalSettings` ("Open User Settings"); the JSON commands create a missing file as `{\n}\n` and `revealSetting.key` puts the cursor on the key; the editor's "Open Settings (JSON)" button and the "Edit in settings.json" link now run these commands. `emetos-virtual:` read-only documents (`core/document/virtual.go`: `VirtualRegistry` with `Register`, `Has`, `Paths`, `Generate`, `VirtualProvider{Label,Language,Text}`; `Process.Virtual` registers `/defaultSettings.json` labelled "Default Settings", language `jsonc`; `Documents.OpenVirtual` regenerates on every open and refreshes an open document; never dirty, not saved, not backed up, serialized by URI and restored through the provider, an unknown provider drops the editor silently; Save and Save As on any read-only document say "Cannot save ... read-only" quietly). `settings.DefaultSettingsJSON` generates the default settings document: JSONC, tab-indented, a group comment per category ("// Text Editor > Font"), the description wrapped at 80 columns, allowed values, per-value descriptions, minimum, maximum and deprecated comments, `"key": default,` with no trailing comma, every registered setting once in layout order.

## 8.3 Keybindings editor

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-8.3-keybindings-editor
- **Summary:** the keybindings UI (SPEC §3.2, §10.3, §11.2, §11.3 "The keybindings editor as built"). Core (`core/keybinding`): `Model` builds the rows from the default registry and the user file (a user `-command` entry hides the default binding; commands without bindings are listed), `Fetch` searches (free text over the command id, title, when and key label with highlight ranges, a quoted chord for an exact sequence match including two-chord sequences, `@source:user|default` with `system` as an alias of `default`), `FindConflicts` (another command with exactly the same chord sequence whose `when` clauses can both hold, unless one provably excludes the other through `Implies`/`Negate`; prefix shadowing is not reported), and `Editing` ports `keybindingEditing.ts` as minimal JSONC text edits (`core/jsonc.DiffEdit`) that keep comments and layout, entries written in the order key, command, when, args: `Add`; `Edit` (a user row is edited in place found by `FileEntry`, a default row gets the new entry plus `{key: oldKey, command: "-cmd", when: oldWhen}`); `UpdateWhen` (validated first: "Not a when-clause: ..."); `Remove` (a user entry is deleted, a default one gets the `-cmd` entry); `Reset` (deletes every entry of the command, `-command` entries included); `Overwrite` (deletes the conflicting user entries and adds `-cmd` entries for default ones); a missing, empty or comments-only file becomes the header comment plus `[]`. The same open-dirty / open-clean / closed rule as the settings applies to `keybindings.json` (a dirty document is edited in place, VS Code refuses), and a saved typed `keybindings.json` now takes effect; `Resolver.Replace` reloads the live bindings after each edit so a new binding works at once and a removed one stops. `DefaultKeybindingsJSON` generates the read-only `emetos-virtual:/defaultKeybindings.json` document (VS Code's line layout, no per-entry title comments). UI (`gui/keybindingsui`): a search box (placeholder "Type to search in keybindings", the record keys button, a clear button), the table Command | Keybinding | When | Source with highlighted matches, the id under the title, key caps (`kit.NewKeyCaps`), a hover pencil, double click or Enter to change, a context menu (Change Keybinding, Add Keybinding, Remove, Reset, Copy, Copy Command ID, Copy Command Title, Change When Expression, Show Same Keybindings), and the define box (records up to two chords through the dispatcher's recording mode, "N existing command(s) have this keybinding", clicking that line filters the table; Escape clears the recording and then closes the box; Backspace is recorded as a key, as in VS Code); with conflicts, Enter opens the "Keybinding conflicts" dialog with Keep Both (default), Overwrite and Cancel. `editorgroup.KeybindingsInput` (type id `emetos.keybindings`, a never-dirty singleton like `SettingsInput`, serialized with query, command and key) is the second entry of `editorKinds()`; tab label "Keyboard Shortcuts" (icon record-keys, since the Codicons have no keyboard glyph). Commands: `workbench.action.openGlobalKeybindings` ("Open Keyboard Shortcuts", Ctrl+K Ctrl+S, takes a string or `{"query"}`), `openGlobalKeybindingsFile` (creates `[]`), `openDefaultKeybindingsFile`, rows "Keyboard Shortcuts" in File > Preferences and the Manage menu, and `keybindings.editor.*` (`searchKeybindings` Ctrl+F, `clearSearchResults` Escape, `recordSearchKeys` Alt+K, `focusKeybindings` Ctrl+Down, `defineKeybinding` Enter, `addKeybinding` Ctrl+K Ctrl+A, `defineWhenExpression` Ctrl+K Ctrl+E, `removeKeybinding` Delete, `copyKeybindingEntry` Ctrl+C, and `resetKeybinding`, `showConflicts`, `copyCommandKeybindingEntry`, `copyCommandTitle` without keys) under the context keys `inKeybindings`, `inKeybindingsSearch`, `keybindingsSearchHasValue`, `keybindingFocus`, `whenFocus`; colors `tree.tableColumnsBorder`, `tree.tableOddRowsBackground`, `keybindingTable.headerBackground`, `keybindingTable.rowsBackground`.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/keybinding/{model,search,conflicts,editing,defaultjson,resolver,userfile,defaults}.go`, `internal/core/jsonc/edit.go`, `internal/core/editorgroup/keybindingsinput.go`, `internal/gui/keybindingsui/{editor,row,define,record}.go`, `internal/gui/kit/{keycaps,list,theme}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{userkeys,keybindingspane,panes,settingsdocs,virtualdocs}.go`, `internal/core/{command,theme}`, `docs/SPEC.md` §3.2, §10.3, §11.2, §11.3, `testdata/proof/8.3/config/keybindings.json`.

## 8.4 Theme and icon pickers

- **Date:** 2026-10-24

- **Summary:** choosing themes (SPEC §3.2 "Themes", §8.4, §10.6, §10.8, §11.2). Core: `theme.Service.PickerGroups()` lists the themes for the picker grouped light, dark, high contrast (empty groups left out; Dark Modern or Light Modern first, then by label, user themes included) with `PickDescription` (the VS Code descriptions such as "Default Dark"), `FileIconChoices()` (None, "Disable File Icons", whose setting value is `null`, and "Seti (Visual Studio Code)", `vs-seti`), and `Service.Preview(name)`, `EndPreview()`, `Previewing()` (an `Apply` with different settings ends a preview, so a change in settings.json wins). ## 8.5 Zoom, zen mode, full screen

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-8.5-zoom-zen
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.9. `kit.Zoom` sits in `WidgetsApp.Builder` above the navigator (pages and every overlay are inside it): a `LayoutBuilder` giving an `OverflowBox` a child of `Transform.scale(f)` laid out in size/f, with `MediaQuery.size` = size/f and `devicePixelRatio` × f; layout, painting and hit testing go through the same matrix, text stays sharp (Glutter draws glyph outlines under the transform), the tree does not depend on the factor so widget state survives a zoom change; window coordinates equal overlay coordinates × f, so `kit.GlobalToOverlay` is used by the context menu and the tab-drag label layer. The factor is 1.2^level (`settings.ZoomFactor`, levels -8..8 as the reference's `MAX_ZOOM_LEVEL`, not 9). `window.zoomLevel` (application scope) and `window.zoomPerWindow` (the actions change the window's own level, kept in the window state field `ZoomLevel`; with `zoomPerWindow` false they write the setting; a settings change resets every window). Commands `workbench.action.zoomIn` (Ctrl+=, Ctrl+Shift+=, Ctrl+NumPad_Add), `zoomOut` (Ctrl+-, Ctrl+NumPad_Subtract), `zoomReset` (Ctrl+NumPad0). Full screen: `workbench.action.toggleFullScreen` (F11) calls `SetFullscreen` on the window controller by interface assertion (`BaseWindowController` lacks it; a window without a controller fails with `FullScreenUnavailable`); the state comes from the controller listener, so the `isFullscreen` context key, the check mark and the saved geometry stay right. Zen mode (`workbench.action.toggleZenMode`, Ctrl+K Z; `workbench.action.exitZenMode` on `escape escape` when `inZenMode`): the zen state lives in `LayoutState.Zen` (what was hidden, which parts the user changed meanwhile, whether zen turned on full screen, the centered layout or do-not-disturb); entering hides the side bar, panel and menu bar always, the activity bar and status bar per their settings, and applies `zenMode.fullScreen`, `zenMode.centerLayout` and `zenMode.silentNotifications`; tabs (`zenMode.showTabs`) and line numbers are derived overrides, the settings files are never written (a test asserts it byte for byte); exiting restores the hidden parts except the ones the user changed during zen and turns off what zen turned on; leaving full screen by F11 ends zen when zen made the full screen; the `zenMode.*` settings apply live; `zenMode.restore` brings a window back in zen. Centered layout (`workbench.action.toggleCenteredLayout`): margins of 0.1909 of the width each (at least 60 px, the editor keeps at least 220 px; fixed-width mode 900 px), only with at most one column of groups or a maximized group (nothing is lost when a second group opens), saved in `LayoutState.CenteredLayout`. View > Appearance rows Full Screen, Zen Mode, Centered Layout (checked) and Zoom In, Zoom Out, Reset Zoom; settings `zenMode.{fullScreen,centerLayout,showTabs,hideStatusBar,hideActivityBar,hideLineNumbers,restore,silentNotifications}`, `workbench.editor.centeredLayoutAutoResize`, `workbench.editor.centeredLayoutFixedWidth`; context keys `isFullscreen`, `inZenMode`, `isCenteredLayout`.
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/kit/{zoom,contextmenu}.go`, `internal/core/settings/{zoom,builtin}.go`, `internal/gui/workbench/{layout,workbench,commands}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{zoom,zen,centered,app,window,windows_commands,state,editors,gridview,group,panes,tabmenu,tabdrag}.go`, `internal/core/storage/statefiles.go`, `internal/core/{command,keybinding}`, `docs/SPEC.md` §10.9, §10.10, §11.2, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`.
- **Tests:** 4 in `core/settings/zoom_test.go`, 7 in `kit/zoom_test.go` (constraints and MediaQuery under zoom, hit testing, scroll and drag, state kept across factor changes, a context menu under zoom at three factors), 10 in `app/zoom_test.go` (the keys through the dispatcher including numpad, per-window and all-window zoom, two-window propagation, persistence), 15 in `app/zen_test.go` (each `zenMode.*` setting alone, live changes, byte-for-byte settings files, restart with `zenMode.restore` on and off, two windows, Ctrl+K Z, Escape Escape, F11 interplay, full screen through a fake controller and the real tester window controller), 5 in `app/centered_test.go`, 3 in `workbench/layout_test.go`; route test for `FullScreenUnavailable`; 14 new goldens (`zoom_in_*`, `zoom_out_*`, `zen_mode_*`, `zen_mode_single_tab_*`, `centered_layout_*`, `appearance_menu_*` in the app and `zoom_{dark,light}` in kit) and `settings_top_{dark,light}` regenerated for the new "Zen Mode" entry in the table of contents (the agent viewed all; I looked at `zoom_in_dark` and `zen_mode_light`). Existing tests changed: `TestChordsAndModifierKeys` and `TestTheChordMessageShowsAndClears` used Ctrl+K Z as an unbound chord (zen mode now), they use Ctrl+K Y; `TestEveryDefaultKeybindingRunsItsCommand` refocuses the editor per subtest because the new `exitZenMode` subtest unfocuses it.
- **Not ported:** draggable centered margins, `workbench.action.zenHideEditorTabs`, `zenShowMultipleEditorTabs`, `zenShowSingleEditorTab` and the zen Tab Bar submenu, the editor font zoom commands changing window zoom, `window.density`, zoom for webviews, the diff-editor rule for centering.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.
- **Proof:** none

- **Deviations and follow-ups:** `zenMode.hideTabs` is not registered (`zenMode.showTabs` replaces it, as in the reference); at zoom level 8 the window is about 300 px wide and the parts overflow; a 1 px border is anti-aliased at fractional levels; the wheel scrolls the same number of logical pixels (f times as many on screen); in full screen the `classic` menu bar behaves like `toggle`.

## 8.6 Profiles

- **Date:** 2026-10-24
- **Branch:** feat/step-8.6-profiles
- **Summary:** SPEC §3.2 "Profiles", §10.10–§10.12, §15.2. Core: `storage.Profiles` (`NewProfiles(paths, opts)`) with `List` (the default first, the others by name, case-insensitive), `Lookup`, `Exists`, `Path`, `Create` (`CreateEmpty` or `CreateFrom(profile)`, copying only `settings.json`, `keybindings.json` and `snippets/`, atomically through a temporary folder and a rename), `Ensure` (creates an empty profile for an unknown `--profile`), `Rename` (moves the config and state folders, rolls back on failure, rewrites the references), `Delete`, `LastProfile`/`SetLastProfile`; `ValidateName`/`ValidProfileName` is the single name rule (1–64 letters, digits, spaces, `-`, `_`; no leading/trailing space; case-insensitive clashes; `Default` reserved), also used by `cmd/emetos` for `ArgsProfileInvalid`. `GlobalState.LastProfiles` and `OpenWindow.Profile` are additive fields. `settings.Store.SetUserPath` and `snippet.Service.SetDir` rebind a layer in place (a stale reload is discarded). App: each `Window` has a profile (`Profile()`, `ProfileName()`, `OnProfileChange`) and `SwitchProfile(ctx, name)` rebinds, without closing anything, the user settings layer (the store's change events drive every `Settings.OnChange` consumer: title, autosave, backups, editors, explorer, themes, languages, zoom, zen, the settings editor), the keybindings (resolver replaced, keybindings editor rebuilt), the snippets, the config watcher and the state store (the old profile's window state is flushed first; later saves go to the new profile; the UI state is not restored on a switch). Themes and snippets became per-window services (`Window.Themes`, `Window.Snippets`). Launch rules: `--profile` > the restored window's profile > the folder's last profile > the default; a running instance opens a new window for a folder not yet open, focuses a folder already open with another profile with the notice "The folder is already open with the profile 'X'.". The `TODO(step 8.6)` warning is gone. `dev.switchProfile {"name"}` is the entry point for tests and for 8.6b.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/storage/{profiles,statefiles,statestore}.go`, `internal/core/settings/store.go`, `internal/core/snippet/files.go`, `cmd/emetos/{args,main}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{profile,process,window,windows,windows_commands,devcommands,startup,state,launch,workspace,userkeys,settingsdocs,keybindingspane,theme,themepickers,editors,explorer,app}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §10.10–§10.12, §15.2.

## 9.1 Line diff

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-9.1-line-diff
- **Summary:** SPEC §9.11, `core/diff`. A port of VS Code's `defaultLinesDiffComputer` up to, and excluding, the character refinement: `ComputeLines(ctx, original, modified, Options{IgnoreTrimWhitespace, MaxComputationTime, Now})` gives `LinesDiff{Changes []LineRangeMapping, HitTimeout}` (1-based line ranges with an exclusive end; `Inner []RangeMapping` is there for 9.2). Lines are hashed trimmed (JS-style `trim`); dynamic programming when both texts together have fewer than 1700 lines, Myers otherwise (DP scores an equal line 0.1 when empty, `1 + ln(1 + utf16len)` otherwise, 0.99 when equal only after trimming); the line-stage heuristics `optimizeSequenceDiffs` (join by shifting, shift to the best boundary score by indentation) and `removeVeryShortMatchingLinesBetweenDiffs`; the shortcuts of `computeDiff`; the line-stage part of `scanForWhitespaceChanges` (a line equal after trimming but not as written is a change, unless `IgnoreTrimWhitespace`). A timeout (`DateTimeout`, injectable clock) returns the trivial one-change diff with `HitTimeout`; the context is checked every 1024 steps (`DiffCancelled`). `Apply` rebuilds the modified lines from the original and the changes; `Validate` checks sortedness, bounds and equal unchanged gaps (`DiffInvalid`).
- **Main files:** `internal/core/diff/{doc,types,timeout,sequence,dp,myers,optimize,lines,apply}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.11.
- **Tests:** 31 top-level tests (188 with subtests, 99.5% coverage): 30 line diff table cases (each also `Validate`d and `Apply`d), heuristics, 500 random sequence pairs (Myers equals the LCS-optimal cost), the 1700 threshold, 600 seeded random `Apply == modified` cases, large cases up to 4000 lines, timeout with a stepping fake clock, cancellation mid-DP and mid-Myers, route tests for `DiffCancelled`, `DiffTimeoutInvalid`, `DiffAlignmentBroken` and 17 `DiffInvalid` cases; `fixtures_test.go` runs the 58 fixture folders of VS Code: 53 match `advanced.expected.diff.json` on the line ranges, the other 5 (`class-replacement`, `noisy-move1`, `shifting-twice`, `ts-confusing-2`, `ts-example1`) differ only where 9.2's refinement splits or trims a block and are validated and applied only (skipped when `reference/` is absent).
- **Not ported:** moved code detection (SPEC §2), the character stage (9.2).
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.
- **Proof:** none
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** columns are byte-based, not UTF-16; no settings registered (9.2 registers `diffEditor.maxComputationTime`, the diff editor `diffEditor.ignoreTrimWhitespace`); after the limit the line stage gives the trivial diff like VS Code's algorithm, 9.2 confirms the SPEC wording ("the unrefined line diff").

## 9.2 Character diff and limits

- **Date:** 2026-10-25

- **Summary:** SPEC §9.11, `core/diff`. `Compute(ctx, original, modified, Options)` runs the line stage of 9.1 and then VS Code's `refineDiff` on every changed block: `LinesSliceCharSequence` (code points as elements, `translateOffset/Range`, `findWordContaining`, `findSubWordContaining`, `extendToFullLines`, boundary scores by character category), dynamic programming under 500 characters and Myers above, `optimizeSequenceDiffs`, `extendDiffsToEntireWordIfAppropriate` (the subword pass only with `Options.ExtendToSubwords`, which VS Code's diff editor does not set), `removeShortMatches`, `removeVeryShortMatchingTextBetweenLongDiffs`, the equal-lines white-space scan, and `lineRangeMappingFromRangeMappings`; `Inner` holds the character changes. One clock covers both stages: after the limit the block being aligned and every block after it get one character change over the whole block (as the reference does), blocks refined earlier keep theirs, `HitTimeout` is set; the SPEC wording "the unrefined line diff" was corrected (`ComputeLines` stays for callers that want lines only). `Validate` also checks the inner ranges. ## 9.3 Three-way merge model

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-9.3-merge-model
- **Summary:** SPEC §9.11, `core/diff` (no UI). The marker parser `ParseConflictMarkers(lines)` ports `mergeConflictParser.ts` (`<<<<<<<`, optional `|||||||`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>` at column 0, labels, CRLF; as in the reference an unbalanced scan gives up, it does not restart). `MergeInputs` (Base, Input1 = incoming, Input2 = current, labels, EOL, `MarkedConflicts`) comes from three files (`MergeInputsFromFiles`) or from a marker file (`MergeInputsFromMarkers`, `MergeInputsFromMarkerText`: the base is the `|||||||` sections or empty regions; a conflict with no base stays an unhandled conflict through `MarkedConflicts`). `ModifiedBaseRangesFromDiffs` is the diff3 of `modifiedBaseRange.ts` and `mapping.ts`: changes whose base ranges intersect or touch are joined (one unchanged line keeps them apart), with `IsEqualChange`, `IsConflicting`, `TextForState` and the states `RangeState` (base, input1, input2, both with the order of the inputs). `MergeModel` (`NewMergeModel(ctx, inputs, opts)`): the result starts as the base with every change only one input made (or both made alike) applied and every conflict holding the base text, unhandled; regions are tracked through edits (`ApplyResultEdit`; a manual edit makes a region unrecognized or the state its text equals); `Accept(i, Choice)` with `AcceptBase`, `AcceptInput1` (incoming), `AcceptInput2` (current) and `AcceptBoth` (current then incoming), `AcceptAll`, `Reset`, `Toggle`, `SetState`, `SetHandled`, `Conflicts`, `UnhandledCount`, `HandledCount`, `Result`, `ResultText` (joined with the file's EOL: CRLF in, CRLF out) and the `Edit{StartLine, EndLine, NewLines}` each change returns, so the editor can apply it as one undoable edit. The model is a value API, not safe for concurrent use.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/diff/{markers,mergeinputs,modifiedbase,mergestate,mergemodel,doc}.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.11.
- **Tests:** 184 passing tests and subtests (the merge-conflict extension has no tests in `reference/`, so the cases are our own): 56 parser tables (balanced, diff3, labels, unbalanced, stray markers, 8-character markers, CRLF, empty sections, file start and end), 52 diff3 and state tests (one input changed, identical, differing, adjacent, one line between, same-place insertions, deletion against modification, empty base and inputs, the git documentation example, range invariants), 83 model tests (every choice, shifting of later conflicts, `AcceptAll`, `Reset`, `Toggle`, manual edits, counts, the marker flow with and without a base, CRLF), 900 seeded random cases in 3 tests (union merges, every choice against an independent expected text, random operations with region invariants after each step); route tests for `MergeConflictIndexInvalid`, `MergeChoiceInvalid`, `MergeStateInvalid`, `MergeEditInvalid`, `MergeEOLInvalid`, `MergeMarkersNotFound`, `MergeRangeWithoutChange`, `DiffCancelled` and `DiffTimeoutInvalid`.
- **Not ported:** smart combination of both inputs, re-deriving the states from a result text, `getResultValueWithConflictMarkers`, `mergeEditor.diffAlgorithm`.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.

## 9.4 View zones

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-9.4-view-zones
- **Summary:** SPEC §9.1. Rows inserted between the lines of an editor (VS Code's view zones / whitespace). `ViewModel` API: `AddZone(ZoneSpec{AfterLine, Rows, Ordinal, ShowInHiddenAreas, Widget})`, `ChangeZone`, `SetZoneRows`, `SetZoneAfterLine`, `RemoveZone`, `ChangeZones` (a batch with one notification), `Zone`, `Zones`, `ZoneAtRow`, `ZoneAtY`, `SetZonePressHandler`, `DisposeZones`, `RenderEditorText.ZoneAt`. Units are whole rows (`Rows >= 1`), so the row Y stays uniform and the scroll, minimap and scrollbar math is untouched. `AfterLine` counts the lines above (0: above the first line); zones sort by the row they follow, then `Ordinal`, then insertion; a zone after a wrapped line comes after all its rows; lookups are binary searches over prefix sums (O(log z)). Folding follows `viewZones.ts`: a zone is shown only if the line after it is not hidden (so a zone after a fold header is hidden, one after the last hidden line is shown after the header row), `ShowInHiddenAreas` forces it. Zones follow edits as VS Code's `onLinesDeleted/Inserted` do (lines inserted above push the zone down; deleting the anchor moves it after the line before the deleted ones; shrinking clamps; `SetText` puts every zone after line 1). The projections gained `RowZone`, `LineZoneRows`, `ZoneRows`, `ZonesIn`, `ZoneRowsBefore` (the identity, folded and wrapped ones return no zones; no zoned projection exists without zones). Zone rows: no line number, folding control or glyph margin content; no current-line highlight, selection, find matches, range highlights, guides, whitespace marks or fold background; a press moves no cursor and starts no selection (the press handler hears the primary button); dragging over a zone maps to the nearest text row; Up/Down skip zone rows, Page Up/Down count the viewport rows minus zone rows; reveal uses the text row; the scroll extent includes zones; the minimap draws them blank. The optional widget is laid out in the zone's rows, as wide as the text area, scrolls vertically but not horizontally, clipped; only zones within 20 rows of the viewport are built.
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/editor/{zones,zoneproj,zonelayer,projection,wrapproj,viewmodel,widget,pointer,render,geometry,gutter,overlay,display_paint,guides,find_paint,minimap_paint}.go`, `internal/gui/app/editors.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.1.
- **Tests:** 24 top-level tests and 52 subtests in `zones_test.go` and `zones_widget_test.go`: projection tables with zones, folds and wraps together, a seeded random test (300 rounds against a naive oracle with every projection query checked), `followLines` tables, edit following, shrink and clamp, add/change/remove and batch notification, route tests for `EditorZoneNotFound` and `EditorZoneInvalid`, widget tests (scroll extent, reveal, press and handler, Up/Down/Page Down, drag, selection rows and current line, wrapped lines, folding, widget placement while scrolling, minimap, ruler, sticky scroll); 4 goldens `zones_{selection,cursor}_{dark,light}` (wrap, a fold, a blank zone, a colored widget zone, a hidden zone; viewed); every earlier golden is unchanged; no existing test changed.
- **Not built:** pixel and zero heights, per-zone horizontal scroll, `afterColumn`, margin widgets in the gutter, zones in the minimap or ruler, accessibility for zones, a zone widget taking the mouse before the editor, a cursor shape change over zones.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · display tests none.
- **Proof:** none
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** the folding rule is VS Code's (a zone after a fold header is hidden), not "a zone after the header stays visible"; the widget layer rebuilds on every scroll tick (a custom render object could avoid it).

The 13 untested Tags got tests (`BackupEmpty`, `BackupEncodeFailed`, `CodiconFormatFailed`, `DevOpenFileFailed`, `EditorClipboardUnavailable`, `EditorClipboardFailed`, `JSONCNoValue`, `JSONCDecodeFailed`, `KeybindingsTableInvalid` (later removed, below), `QuickInputCommandMissing` (later removed), `WindowCreateFailed`, `WindowMissing`, `ErrorTagsExceptionsReadFailed`), with small seams where a failure could not happen (`BackupStoreOptions.Marshal`, the generator's formatter, `keybinding.NewModelOfRows`); `docs/ERROR-TAGS-UNTESTED.md` is not needed. ## 9b.1 Workspaces in one window

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-9b.1-workspaces
- **Summary:** SPEC D17, §10.14. `app.Window` is now `app.Workspace` and `app.Windows` is `app.Workspaces` (`NewWorkspace`, `WorkspaceSpec`, `WorkspaceScope`/`WorkspaceOf`/`PeekWorkspace`, `CloseReasonTab`, the tag `WorkspaceMissing`). `Workspaces` holds `WindowTab`s (`ID`, `Kind`, `Workspace`; `TabKind` is `TabWorkspace` until step 11.6) and hosts them in the one implicit window: an `IndexedStack` of slots keyed by each tab's `GlobalKey`, each a `TickerMode` (on for the active tab only) around the unchanged per-workspace page; only the shown tab paints, hit-tests and takes focus; leaving a tab remembers its focus and coming back restores it; only the active tab's key dispatcher uses keys; the window title is the active tab's. Inactive tabs keep their watchers, auto save, backups and file index running. `Open`, `Activate`, `ActivateIndex`, `Move`, `Close`, `NewTab`, `RequestQuit`; a new tab opens after the active one; after a close the most recently active tab becomes active; closing the last tab leaves a No Folder tab; the close button and the app's exit request run the quit flow over every tab. `workbench.action.newWindow` is "New Workspace Tab" and `workbench.action.closeWindow` "Close Workspace Tab". State: `workspaceTabs` (`{id, kind, stateId, folder, profile}`), `activeWorkspaceTab` and `windowGeometry` in `state.json`; an old `openWindows` list migrates to tabs in order (each tab keeps the old window id, so its `windows/<id>.json` and backups are found); `window.restoreWindows` reads as restore tabs. Profiles are per tab. Dev commands `dev.openFolderInNewTab {"path"}` (replacing `dev.openFolderInNewWindow`) and `dev.activateWindowTab {"index"}`. Removed: the window host, the window manager root, `CreateRegularWindowController`, the exit-request hook, the retired implicit window, window focus following, `newWindowSize`, the tags `WindowsUnavailable` and `WindowCreateFailed`.

## 9b.1b Glutter 1.7 and the end of the workarounds

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-9b.1b-glutter-1.7
- **Summary:** Emetos is on Glutter v1.7.0 (build, tests and every golden unchanged before any edit). Replaced with the 1.7 APIs: `kit.Hover` on `widgets.NewRawTooltip` (`HoverDelayFunc`, `OnShown`, `OnHidden`, `Controller`; Emetos's own key handler stays because `DismissOnKey` neither ignores a lone modifier nor cancels a hover still waiting for its delay; a press anywhere now hides the hover), the sash on `MouseRegionOpts.HoldCursorWhilePressed` (the whole-view cursor region is gone), the window controller through `widgets.WindowController`/`MaximizableWindowController`/`WindowControllerMaybeOf` (no interface assertions; tests read the title with `Tester.ViewTitle`), `testutil.New` relying on `gluttertest.New`'s unmount, the no-file-chooser tests on `FakeDesktop.DisableFileChooser()`, the panel actions and the Problems filter box leaving the tree again (27.1). Kept, with reasons: `kit.Tree` rebuilds its nodes (1.7 cannot set `expanded` on an existing node, and the model owns expansion; `NodeKey` broke four tree tests); the list and tab drags keep their own controllers (one controller per list works while rows scroll away, targets come from row geometry, scrolling and auto-expand use the binding's timers; the Glutter gaps are gone, so their comments are now design notes); `ProcessOptions.WatchFiles` stays off in tests (the leak is gone, but a live watcher races with tests that stage on-disk changes); the `SaveDialog` field stays for a dialog that fails another way. `scripts/perf.sh` reports the split first draw (renderers tried, GPU context, shaders built and from cache, frame) for three cache states and measures idle without focus headless (a second window takes the focus): 0 frames. `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md` keeps two entries, rewritten: `TreeSliver` expansion (`SetExpanded`/`IsExpanded` asked) and the cold start (a failed Vulkan try costs 560–605 ms headless; Glutter's shader cache saves about 13 ms over Mesa's). The close button's `TODO(step 9b.4)` points at `SetImplicitWindowDelegate`.
- **Main files:** `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `internal/gui/kit/{hover,sash,splitview,tree,listdnd,tabs}.go`, `internal/gui/testutil/testutil.go`, `internal/gui/app/{app,workspaces,workspacemodel,zen,state,save}.go`, `internal/gui/workbench/workbench.go`, `internal/gui/views/problems/view.go`, `scripts/perf.sh`, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`, `docs/SPEC.md` §10.2, §10.9, §20.

Changed: `autosave_test.go`, `save_test.go`, `save_golden_test.go` (setup only), `state_test.go` (`fakeWindow`), `workspacetabs_test.go`. No golden changed.
- **Not ported:** `DismissOnKey`, persistent tree nodes, `Draggable` for the list and tab drags.

## 9b.3 Launches open tabs

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-9b.3-launch-tabs
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.11, §10.12, §10.14, §15.1. Every launch (a hand-over over the socket; the first instance's own command line is still placed by the restore plan) and every Open Folder opens or focuses a tab: a folder that a tab has (through links) becomes active; otherwise `-n` (and Ctrl in Open Recent) opens a new tab after the active one and `-r` replaces the active tab with the unsaved-changes questions (Cancel keeps it; the tab keeps its place and id); otherwise `window.openFoldersInNewWindow` decides (`on` a new tab, `off` the active tab, `default` a new tab, replacing an untouched No Folder tab: no folder, no document, no editor). Open Folder, Open Recent, the empty Explorer's button and Close Folder follow the same rule (7.8's "picked inside the app replaces" exception and `FolderSource` are gone); Close Folder makes the active tab a No Folder tab. Files, `--goto`, `--diff` and `--merge` open in the active tab (`window.openFilesInNewWindow` `on` opens a new No Folder tab for files; `off` and `default` use the active tab); `--profile` keeps the 8.6 rules per tab (a folder not open goes to a new tab when the active tab lacks the profile; an open folder with another profile is focused with its notice) and now covers `--diff`/`--merge`. Every launch first shows and raises the window (`Workspaces.showWindow`: `SetHidden(false)` and `Activate` on Glutter 1.7's implicit controller), so step 9b.4 only adds the hiding. `emetos` with no argument shows the window. `scripts/proof.sh --launch '<args>'` (repeatable) runs further launches against the same isolated runtime folder (`scripts/run-with-launches.sh`). ## 10.1 Performance pass

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-10.1-performance
- **Summary:** SPEC §14, §8.3, §15.2; `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`. `scripts/perf.sh` now measures every target of §14: typing, scrolling, the 10 MB and 200 MB opens, the cold start in three cache states and with four restored tabs, Emetos's own share of the start (before the window and the first build), idle with and without focus, memory with its split by mapping, and Go benchmarks for the UI thread, fuzzy search, quick open and grammar loading (`--no-go`, `--no-huge`, `--profile dir`, `PERF_KEEP`); two bugs of the old script fixed (typing and scrolling counted the first frame; the first-frame wait could be seconds late). Dev profiling in `emetos_dev` builds: `EMETOS_PROFILE_DIR` with SIGUSR1 (heap, allocs, goroutines, memstats) and SIGUSR2 (CPU on/off), `EMETOS_PROFILE_START=cpu`. Fixes: (1) **a tab character made Glutter load all 62 monospace system fonts** (no font has a glyph for U+0009): a 288-byte bundled font with an empty tab glyph (`fonts.ControlsFont`) goes first in the families of rows with a tab; resident memory 738 → 418 MB, the first build of a 10 MB file 206 → 12 ms, a restore with four tabs 725 → 406 MB; (2) **every tokenizer slice made the next frame re-pair every bracket of the file**: `brackets.Index.Invalidate` notes the dirty lines and the next question re-reads only those on the UI thread, re-pairing only when brackets changed; scrolling build 8.3 → 1.5 ms average, worst 25.7 → 5.6 ms; (3) **a closed Output panel drew a frame on every log line**: `output.ViewOpts.Visible`; idle frames 31 → 21 per 10 s; (4) **grammar rules built in the first frame**: `Process.WarmGrammars` compiles the grammars of the files the window opens with on a goroutine while the renderer starts, and `Tokenizer.Ensure` no longer waits for a grammar another goroutine is compiling; (5) **the synchronous tokenization budget was spent by layout, paint and the minimap each**: one 4 ms budget per frame shared by all three (was 6 ms each); scrolling to unseen highlighted lines 7.8 → 4.7 ms. The targets still missed headless were decided by me (SPEC §14 rows revised).
- **Main files:** `scripts/perf.sh`, `cmd/emetos/{main,profile_dev,profile_off}.go`, `internal/gui/kit/fonts/{fonts,controls}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{text,tokens}.go`, `internal/core/brackets/index.go`, `internal/core/textmate/grammar.go`, `internal/core/tokens/tokenizer.go`, `internal/gui/app/{panels,process,workspaces}.go`, `internal/gui/views/output/view.go`, `docs/{PERFORMANCE,SPEC,GLUTTER-ISSUES,MANUAL-CHECKS}.md`.

Existing tests changed: `TestSources` and `TestFontsAreGoMonoAndTheIconFonts` pin the list of bundled fonts, which gains `emetos-controls`. No golden changed.

## 11.2 Events

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-11.2-events
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.15 "Events". `api.Events()`: `Publish`, `Subscribe` (patterns: `*` one segment, a final `**` one or more), `Request(ctx, topic, value, reply)` (callback, 10 s default timeout on the window's timers, `EventNoHandler`, `EventTimeout`, `EventCanceled`, the handler's error as `EventHandlerFailed`), `Handle` and `HandleAsync` (reply once from any goroutine); `Manifest.Events` declares published (optionally fast), handled and subscribed topics; an extension publishes and handles only its own id's topics and the ones it declares (`EventTopicNotOwned`), `emetos.*` ids are reserved. Values are JSON copies; delivery is on the UI thread in order per publisher and topic, never re-entrant; fast topics are batched per frame (one event with `Batch` per publisher and topic) and flushed before a later normal event; handlers or subscribers over 50 ms are logged; subscriber, handler and reply-callback panics fail the extension in that scope (own tags). The core events published by every workspace scope: `emetos.workspace.opened`/`closed`, `emetos.windowTab.activated`, `emetos.document.opened`/`changed` (fast, with the changes)/`saved`/`closed`, `emetos.editor.activeChanged` (coalesced per turn), `emetos.editor.selectionChanged` (fast). Delivery and handler lookup go through `Host.targets`/`Host.handlerFor`, where step 11.3 adds the links. `api.Documents().Read` was already built in 11.1.

## 11.3 Event sharing between window tabs

- **Date:** 2026-10-25
- **Branch:** feat/step-11.3-event-sharing
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.15 "Event sharing". `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/event-sharing.json` (`storage.SharingStore`: versioned `{"version":1,"links":[{"from","to","events"}],"private":[...]}`, atomic, 0600, read at start, written on each change from the UI). A tab's sharing id is its folder (No Folder tabs have none). Delivery across scopes is checked per event at delivery: only along a saved or session link `from → to` carrying the topic, never out of a private workspace; queued events stop when a link is removed; fast batches cross as one. `Manifest.Events.CrossTab` lists the topics an extension may get from other tabs; `Subscribe(..., FromOtherScopes()|FromScopes(...))`, `Request(..., ToOtherScopes()|ToScopes(...))` (needs the link from the handler's tab to the requester's; the reply is checked again on arrival), `Documents().Read(..., FromScope(id))` (needs a link carrying `emetos.document.changed`). The question "Let events from A reach B?" in the receiving tab (Allow saves the link, This Session Only keeps it in memory, Deny/Escape is remembered until the extension is activated again; one question per pair at a time; topics outside `CrossTab` are never asked about). The page "Extensions › Event Sharing" (`emetos.extensions.manageEventSharing`, an editor input restored with the window, an "Event Sharing..." button on the Extensions page): saved and session links as `from → to` with topics and Remove, every open tab and every private scope with "Private: never send events to other tabs". `emetos.sharing.revoked` (`{from, fromName, topics, reason}`) in the receiving tab when a link is removed or its source turns private. A file that cannot be written keeps the link for the session with a warning; a corrupt file is ignored with a warning.
- **Main files:** `internal/core/storage/sharing.go`, `internal/core/editorgroup/eventsharinginput.go`, `internal/gui/exthost/{sharing,bus,events,api,host,scope}.go`, `internal/gui/extensionsui/{sharingpage,page}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{eventsharingpane,process,extensions,extensionspane,panes}.go`, `extension/`, `internal/core/command/builtin.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` §10.15.
- **Tests:** `exthost/sharing_test.go` (`notes → office` delivers and nothing goes back, a topic-limited link, removal stops queued events and tells the receiver, private sends nothing and refuses reads, requests and being asked, the three answers with the file written or not, dedup and re-ask after reactivation, undeclared topics never asked, links survive a restart, unnamed tabs, requests and replies along links with ask/deny/timeout, a reply stopped by a removed link, cross-tab reads, fast batches, write failure falls back to a session link); `storage/sharing_test.go` (direction, merge, private, session links never written, restart round trip with 0600, unusable files and write/encode failures route-tested); `extension` (`PatternWithin`, scope filters, the `CrossTab` check); `app/eventsharing_test.go` (the dialog's four answers, a link allowed before a restart works after it, a corrupt file ignored with a warning, No Folder tabs, the page flow with Private, Remove, the revoked event and the file contents, the editor kind restores); all in isolated folders. ## 12.2 The JSON-RPC and LSP client core

- **Date:** 2026-10-26
- **Branch:** feat/step-12.2-lsp-client
- **Summary:** SPEC §9.12 "The client", D6, D20. `internal/core/lsp`: `Content-Length` framing (CRLF headers, 64 MiB body limit, any framing error ends the connection), JSON-RPC over any `io.ReadWriteCloser` with one reader, one writer draining an unbounded FIFO (so `Notify` never blocks and a `didChange` is written before a later request), notifications delivered in order on one goroutine and server requests answered concurrently; cancellation from the caller's `ctx` (`$/cancelRequest`, late responses dropped, no timeout of its own); `NewClient` does `initialize`/`initialized` with only the capabilities area 3 builds, negotiates the position encoding (offers UTF-8 and UTF-16, understands UTF-32) and keeps the server's capabilities and dynamic registrations; `Shutdown` (`shutdown`, `exit`, close); handlers for every server-to-client request and notification of §9.12 with defined defaults and error-code mapping; byte columns ⇄ UTF-8/16/32 conversion with clamping rules; document sync from the document model's change events (incremental, last edit first with ranges in the old text, or full; CRLF kept; versions; `willSave`, `willSaveWaitUntil`, `didSave` with text when asked; rename and Save As close and reopen; dynamic registration honoured); percent-encoded URIs; the typed messages of area 3 written by hand; a trace callback for step 12.3. `internal/core/lsp/lsptest`: a scripted fake server (answers, delays, sequences, messages it sends, crash and stall) that records the traffic, rebuilds each document counting characters as a server of its encoding does, and lists protocol violations, run in process over pipes or as the real `fakeserver` program in its own process group. ## Fix: Glutter 1.8.1

- **Date:** 2026-10-26
- **Branch:** fix/glutter-1.8 (not a step of the plan)
- **Summary:** Emetos moves to Glutter v1.8.1 and drops the workarounds the new version makes unneeded. Font fallback (Glutter 28.16) replaces `kit/fonts/controls.go`, the controls font that joined Inter and the symbol font, and simplifies the editor's font families. `TreeSliverNode.SetExpanded`/`SetChildren` (28.17) let `kit.Tree` update its nodes in place instead of rebuilding the tree on every change. `widgets.NewErrorBoundary` (28.20) replaces `ui.NewBuilder`/`ui.BoxScope` (`extension/ui/box.go` is deleted): the box of an extension view puts a boundary keyed by the instance around the extension's widget, so a panic anywhere below it fails the extension with `ExtensionViewWidgetPanicked`. WindowDecoration's drag area (28.18) replaces the title bar's gesture-swallowing detectors: the menu and the workspace tabs are now `Leading`, and the empty title moves the window. This needed a new workaround, because `Leading` gets no width limit; it is the only entry left in `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`. `scripts/proof.sh` and `scripts/perf.sh` run headless with `GLUTTER_RENDERER=gles` unless the caller sets it. Also fixed: two flaky app tests, autosave (now waits for the dialog to show) and Save As while closing (now waits until the close is no longer busy).
- **Main files:** `go.mod`, `internal/gui/kit/{tree,fonts/fonts}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/text.go`, `internal/gui/exthost/box.go`, `internal/gui/workbench/titlebar.go`, `scripts/{proof,perf}.sh`, `docs/{SPEC,PERFORMANCE,GLUTTER-ISSUES}.md`.
- **Tests:** tree updates in place (expanded state kept, children replaced); a widget panic below an extension's view, and a re-enabled extension getting a fresh boundary (`exthost/views_test.go`); font fallback in the editor's text; the flaky closing and autosave tests (100 runs, and 20 with `-race` under load). No golden changed.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `emetos_gopls` tests ✅ · release build ✅ · display tests none.
- **Measurements:** `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` "Results after Glutter 1.8". Memory is 422 MB without the old workaround. Warm cold start went from 920 to 340 ms, and opening a 10 MB file from 1000 to 470 ms. A restored 4-tab session uses 30–46 MB more; this is not chased yet, because the renderer change confounds the measurement.
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** four removed (the Vulkan try headless, now avoided with `GLUTTER_RENDERER=gles` as Glutter's owner advises; the font loading for a missing character; tree node updates; the error boundary); the title bar entry was replaced by the `Leading` width one (still so in 1.8.1).

## 12.6 Hover and signature help

- **Date:** 2026-10-26
- **Branch:** feat/step-12.6-hover-signature
- **Summary:** SPEC §9.12 "Hover" and "Signature help".
  - **Hover:** VS Code's `HoverOperation` timing (H = `editor.hover.delay`): providers are asked at H/2, results show at H with the diagnostics part from 12.4, later answers are added, and "Loading..." appears at 3H. There is one operation per word (a diagnostic's range, else the word, else the character) and no request over white space or past the end of the line. `Registry.HoverEach` runs off the UI thread and hands each answer back as it resolves; answers for a replaced operation or an older document version are dropped, and the requests are cancelled with the operation. Parts stack diagnostics first, then the providers in order. The sticky hover keeps the `hidingDelay` grace. The box is at most 500 px wide and as tall as max(a quarter of the editor, 250), and scrolls. Markdown uses a new `Options.Hover` look of `extension/ui/markdown`, with code blocks colored by the fenced language's grammar and the theme (`SuggestHost.Tokenize`). Ctrl+K Ctrl+I shows the hover and, pressed again, focuses it; the eight scroll commands, `editor.action.hideHover`, and the `editorHoverVisible`/`editorHoverFocused` keys are added.
  - **Signature help:** a port of VS Code's `ParameterHintsModel`. It triggers on trigger characters after 120 ms, or at once with Ctrl+Shift+Space. Retrigger characters, typing and cursor moves ask again while the hints show, and requests carry `isRetrigger` and `activeSignatureHelp`. The hints close on Escape, blur, a mouse press, an empty answer or the setting turned off. Superseded requests are cancelled and stale answers dropped. Overloads switch with Up/Down (and Alt+Up/Down) or the arrows; the counter is "1/3", and `editor.parameterHints.cycle` makes the list wrap. The active parameter, found by the server's offsets or VS Code's whole-word rule, is drawn bold in `editorHoverWidget.highlightForeground`. Parameter and signature documentation are Markdown. The hints coexist with the suggest widget (Escape closes suggest first). New: `editor.parameterHints.enabled`/`cycle`, 4 commands, 3 context keys and `dev.triggerParameterHints`; `dev.showHover` now asks the providers too.
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/editor/{signature,signature_widget,hover,hover_widget,suggest,viewmodel,options,commands,input,pointer,widget,dev}.go`, `internal/core/langfeatures/{types,registry,merge,server,convert}.go`, `extension/ui/markdown/view.go`, `internal/gui/app/{suggest,devcommands}.go`, `internal/core/{command,keybinding,settings,theme}`, `internal/gui/kit/theme.go`, `testdata/proof/12.6/`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.12.

## 12.7 Navigation and symbols

- **Date:** 2026-10-26
- **Branch:** feat/step-12.7-navigation
- **Summary:** SPEC §9.12 "Navigation" and "Symbols", §9.6, §9.7, §10.9.
  - **Go-to commands:** definition (F12, Ctrl+K F12 aside), Peek Definition (Alt+F12), declaration, type definition, implementation (Ctrl+F12, peek Ctrl+Shift+F12), references (Shift+F12) and Peek References (Shift+Alt+F12), each needing its `editorHas<Kind>Provider` key. They are in the Go menu and the editor context menu (with a Peek submenu). One result jumps and records history, as a preview editor for another file. Several results follow `editor.gotoLocation.multiple*` (default `peek`). The alternative command runs when the cursor is already on the only result, and no result shows "No definition found".
  - **Links:** Ctrl+hover underlines a word with a definition in `editorLink.activeForeground` with a hand cursor. Ctrl+click goes to the definition, or peeks with `editor.definitionLinkOpensInPeek`; Ctrl+Alt+click opens to the side.
  - **Peek view:** an inline zone with a title bar, an embedded editor (flex 7) and the grouped location list (flex 3). The embedded editor shares an open document or reads the file from disk without a tab, and is coloured by its grammar. Keys: F4/Shift+F4, Up/Down, Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Escape. ## 12.8 Code actions, formatting and rename

- **Summary:** SPEC §9.12 "Code actions", "Formatting", "Rename", §10.11.
  - **Code actions:** VS Code's `getCodeActions` (hierarchical kinds, include, exclude and preferred filters, the `source.*` gate, VS Code's order, disabled actions kept apart).
    - **Light bulb:** asked 250 ms after the cursor rests or the diagnostics change, with the server's raw diagnostic (`Marker.Data`); it follows `editor.lightbulb.enabled` and uses the auto-fix icon for a preferred fix.
    - **List:** Ctrl+., Ctrl+Shift+R, Shift+Alt+O, Shift+Alt+. and the context menu, with headers, Show Disabled, key hints and Ctrl+Enter to preview. Quick Fix also asks at the nearest diagnostic of the line, and the diagnostic hover has "Quick Fix...".
    - **Applying:** resolve when needed, then the edit through `langfeatures.Apply` with every editor's cursors following and one undo step, then the command.
  - **Save participants:** they run before the write, in VS Code's order: trim, `editor.codeActionsOnSave` (`source.fixAll` first, `explicit`/`always`/`never` and the legacy forms), format on save, then the final newline. Each participant is bounded by `editor.codeActionsOnSaveTimeout`/`formatOnSaveTimeout` (750 ms); a timeout shows a silent notification and the save goes on. The participants' edits are one undo step. Auto save skips them, and Save without Formatting skips all. A save with no participants does no extra work.
  - **Formatting:** Format Document (Ctrl+Shift+I) and Format Selection (Ctrl+K Ctrl+F); a range-only formatter serves Format Document. VS Code's `computeMoreMinimalEdits` makes one undo step. Format on type and on paste, `editor.defaultFormatter`, and format on save in modes `file`, `modifications` and `modificationsIfAvailable`. The `modifications` modes compare with the file on disk, since there is no SCM.
  - **Rename:** F2 asks `prepareRename`, and a refusal shows its message. The box over the symbol takes Enter to apply across files and Ctrl+Enter for the refactor preview: a panel with a check box per file and per change, which applies only what is checked.
  - **Fixed on the way:** disposing an editor with a widget open notified a listener on an inactive element.

## 12.9 Code lens, inlay hints, semantic tokens, folding and selection ranges

- **Date:** 2026-10-26
- **Branch:** feat/step-12.9-lens-hints-tokens
- **Summary:** SPEC §9.12, §8.6, §9.2.
  - **Code lenses:** a one-line view-zone row above their line, with the titles of a line joined by " | ". They are resolved when their row comes into view, and a click runs the command. Requests are debounced, and stale answers are dropped by generation and version. Settings: `editor.codeLens`, `codeLensFontFamily`, `codeLensFontSize`.
  - **Inlay hints:** injected into the row's paragraph only, with one map between document and drawn offsets. The document, clipboard, find and undo never see them, and the cursor never rests inside a hint. They support the four `editor.inlayHints.enabled` modes with Ctrl+Alt, padding, `maximumLength` (43, ellipsis), `fontSize` and `fontFamily`, and the `editorInlayHint.*` colours. Label parts have tooltips, and Ctrl+click on a part opens its location or runs its command. Requests cover the viewport plus 30 lines.
  - **Semantic tokens:**
    - a per-window cache with full, delta (`ApplySemanticEdits`) and range requests while a full one is pending, and `workspace/semanticTokens/refresh`;
    - decoding in UTF-16 (UTF-8 and UTF-32 servers converted);
    - styling with VS Code's ported `parseTokenSelector` scoring, the theme's `semanticTokenColors`, `editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations` rules, and the type and modifier fallback to TextMate scopes, drawn over the TextMate spans;
    - tokens move with edits until the next answer;
    - cost per key: about 0.26 ms for a letter and 0.57 ms for a line break, with 100,000 tokens over 20,000 lines;
    - new error tags: `SemanticTokensEditInvalid`, `SemanticTokensDeltaUnexpected`.
  - **Folding ranges:** the server's ranges replace the indentation provider (`editor.foldingStrategy`), cleaned by a port of `sanitizeRanges` (kinds, `foldingMaximumRegions`, crossing ranges dropped). They support `collapsedText` and `editor.foldingImportsByDefault`.
  - **Selection ranges:** Expand Selection asks `textDocument/selectionRange` once for all cursors, and falls back to the editor's own ranges.
  - **gopls:** inlay hints and semantic tokens are switched on through the `go.gopls` settings (`semanticTokens`, `hints`).
- **Main files:**
  - core: `internal/core/langfeatures/{lens,ranges,semantic,registry,server}.go`, `internal/core/folding/{syntax,provider,regions}.go`, `internal/core/theme/{semantic,resolve,theme}.go`, `internal/core/settings/lens.go`;
  - editor and app: `internal/gui/editor/{codelens,inlay,inlay_interact,semantic,selectionranges,lensoptions,geometry,render,folding,viewmodel}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{editors,workspacemodel}.go`, `internal/gui/exthost/servers.go`;
  - other: `testdata/proof/12.9/`, `docs/SPEC.md` §9.12.
- **Tests:**
  - added:
    - core: conversion and resolve of lenses and hints, folding answers and `Sanitize`, semantic decoding and delta edits with both tag routes, the cache, theme selectors, scoring, fallback and flag merge.
    - editor: lens rows and click; hints that leave the text unchanged, cursor skipping, the four modes, padding and truncation, hover and click, stale answers, a settings change; `moveTokens` and `mergeSemantic` tables and the request flow; server folding against the fallback; the selection range expansion.
    - `TestGoplsAnswersHintsTokensFoldingAndSelectionRanges` runs the real `gopls`: 15 hints, 68 tokens, folding, selection ranges and the `//go:generate` lens.
  - changed: span literals in two editor tests, an argument in a hit-test test, and the options defaults.
- **Goldens:**

  - changed: `settings_font_{dark,light}`, where a search for "font" now finds the four new font settings.

## 13.1 The `claude` adapter's protocol

- **Date:** 2026-10-26
- **Branch:** feat/step-13.1-agents
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.16. This step adds `extensions/agents/claude`, a Go client of the `claude` program's stream-json mode, with no UI.
  - **Finding the program:** `Find` reads `agents.claude.path`, else `PATH`.
  - **Login status:** `AuthStatus(ctx)` reads `claude auth status`, using the exit status as the answer and keeping the JSON's method, provider, email, organization and subscription.
  - **Starting:** `Adapter.Start` runs the §10.16 command line in the workspace folder, in its own process group:
    ```
    -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --replay-user-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio --permission-mode <mode> [--session-id|--resume] [--model]
    ```
    It does the `initialize` handshake before it returns. The environment is the user's, unchanged, plus `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING=true`: never `--bare`, never `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, never a key or token.
  - **Messages:** typed `system/init` (with capabilities), `assistant` (text, thinking, `tool_use`), `user` (`tool_result`, replays), `stream_event` (partial text joined per parent tool use), and `result`. Unknown types keep their raw JSON.
  - **Control channel:**
    - out: `interrupt`, `set_permission_mode`, `set_model`, `rewind_files`;
    - in: `can_use_tool`, one goroutine per request; a cancel request ends its `ctx`;
    - request IDs with a 60 s timeout, and a dead program fails every pending request.
  - **Events:** delivered in order through an unbounded queue, so a slow UI never blocks the reading.
  - **Lines:** up to 16 MiB; a bad line becomes an event and the stream goes on.
  - **Ending:** `Close` closes stdin, then TERM and KILL to the group.
  - **Error tags:** 16, all route-tested.
  - **Sources of the wire shapes:** the Agent SDK documentation and the Python SDK, read online, not copied.
- **Main files:** `extensions/agents/claude/{command,auth,lines,messages,partial,control,process,session}.go`, `extensions/agents/claude/internal/fakeclaude/main.go`, `extensions/agents/claude/claudetest/`, `extensions/agents/claude/testdata/*.jsonl` (17 fixtures), `docs/SPEC.md` §10.16, `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md`, `docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md` (13.3's rewind wording).
- **Tests:** everything runs against a fake `claude` that the tests build. It replays the JSONL fixtures, answers control requests, and records its argv, environment and process group. `TestMain` makes `PATH` an empty folder, moves `HOME` and `XDG_*`, and unsets `CLAUDE*`/`ANTHROPIC*`, so the real program can't be reached. Covered:
  - parsing: every message type (a table of fixtures) and partial text;
  - the command line, environment, working folder and process group;
  - permissions: the `can_use_tool` round trip (allow with `updatedInput` and `updatedPermissions`, deny, handler error, nil handler, cancel);
  - the control channel: interrupt, mode, model, rewind, timeouts, a bad handshake;
  - failures: a dead program, malformed lines, a slow `OnEvent`;
  - the auth status cases;
  - processes: cancel and `Close` kill the process group, including a program that ignores TERM.

  `real_test.go` (tag `emetos_claude`) is compiled, not run.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also with `emetos_claude`) · golangci-lint ✅ · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `emetos_gopls` tests ✅ · display tests none.
- **Proof:** none; this step has no UI. The test logs of the fake program are the proof.
- **Manual checks:** withdrawn: the extension was removed in step 17c.1 (D26) before the check was run, and the check left docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md.
- **Glutter issues:** none
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** SPEC §10.16 "As built (step 13.1)" lists 10 decisions.
  - `--permission-prompt-tool stdio` is added to the command line, as the Python SDK does when a permission callback is set.
  - `CLAUDECODE` is passed through unchanged; the Python SDK removes it (decision 74).
  - Rewind is offered on every session Emetos started, because no capability names it, and a refusal shows the program's reason. Step 13.3's tasks and tests now say so.

## 13.3 Permissions, proposed edits, plans and checkpoints

- **Date:** 2026-10-26

- **Summary:** SPEC §10.16, §9.11, §10.15.
  - **`Editors().OpenProposedChange`** is new in `extension/`. It takes `ProposedChange{URI, Original, Proposed, Title, Language}` and returns `ProposedResult{Accepted, Text, Edited}`. It blocks and takes a `ctx`; cancelling closes the tab.
    - The diff opens beside the active group, with an editable right side made of virtual documents that are never dirty, saved or backed up. Accept and Reject are in its title, and closing it in any way rejects.
    - Emetos never writes the proposed text; the program applies the edit after `allow`.
  - **Edits:**
    - `Edit`: `old_string` is replaced in the file's text, with `replace_all` and CRLF handled. Impossible edits are denied at once with the reason.
    - `Write`: the new content against the current file, or an empty one.
    - `NotebookEdit`: the cell's source.
    - An edited Accept sends `updatedInput`. For `Edit`, that is a minimal unique `old_string`/`new_string` that reproduces the user's text exactly.
    - Files outside the folder, excluded by a deny rule or unreadable go to the dialog.
  - **The panel above the input:**
    - the tool dialog (the command, the URL or the input, and the reason), with Allow once, Allow for this session (the request's suggestions with the `session` destination), and Deny with a message;

    - `AskUserQuestion` (options, an own answer, Answer or Skip).

## 15.1 The protocol and the headless view

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Branch:** feat/step-15.1-remotework
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.18.
  - **Protocol** (`extensions/remotework/protocol`, version 1, magic `EMRW`): a message is `type:1 | length:4 | payload`, and each of the 13 types (Hello, Tile, FrameConfirm, Refresh, Key, Mouse, Scroll, Clipboard, Notification, NotificationAction, Resize, Ping, Disconnect) has its own limit. The largest is 1 MiB.
    - The length is checked against the type's limit before anything is read or allocated. An unknown type is refused, not skipped.
    - Payloads must match their sizes exactly, and fields are strictly validated (enums, UTF-8, finite floats, nonzero sizes), so the format is canonical: decoding then encoding gives the same bytes.
    - Encoding allocates nothing.
  - **Tile differ** (`extensions/remotework/tiles`): 64x64 tiles changed since the confirmed frame, each deflated alone at `flate.DefaultCompression`.
    - The host keeps only `maphash` hashes of the last 16 unconfirmed frames: 33 KB at 1280x800.
    - It does a full picture on request (Refresh), on an unknown confirm, and periodically.
    - The client's `Canvas` drops stale tiles and says when to confirm.
    - At 1280x800, a whole picture is 260 tiles, 113 KB and 7.8 ms; one typed character is 7 tiles and 6 KB.
  - **Headless view:** `api.Workspace().NewHeadlessView(size)` in `extension/headless.go`, implemented in `internal/gui/app`.
    - It is a second Glutter binding on the application's UI thread, with a window-less platform host and a workbench of its own.
    - The view has its own commands, focus, layout, dialogs, quick input, status bar and zoom. It shares documents, settings, theme, notifications, problems and file operations with the main window.
    - Pictures are rasterized with Glutter's software renderer and handed to `OnFrame` on a delivery goroutine, at most one frame per `max(33 ms, 2 x the last raster cost)`.
    - Keys, pointer, scroll and clipboard go in. `Resize` re-lays out the view; `Close`, deactivation, a folder change or the workspace closing end it.
    - The view's editors don't blink, so an idle view makes no frames.
    - Commands that act on Emetos itself (quit, tabs, new window) are not bound. Save As uses the quick input. Opening a link does nothing.
  - **Exthost:** the size is checked, the scope is asked (`ScopeOptions.NewHeadlessView`), and the view closes with the activation. `fakeapi` has a fake view.
  - **New error tags:** 23, all route-tested.
- **Tests:**
  - protocol: table round trips of every message, malformed and oversized input with routes, an allocation test, 20,000 seeded random inputs (the canonical property), and `FuzzDecode`.
  - tiles: round trips, a lossy-link simulation, stale tiles and confirms, refresh and reset, measurements on real editor pictures.
  - exthost and fakeapi: the size table, unavailable, closed with the activation.
  - app: about 20 tests (an edit in the main view shows in the headless view, typing, shortcuts, mouse, scroll, quick input, dialogs, zoom, resize, close on a folder change, an idle view makes no frames), and a benchmark.
- **Goldens:** new `headless_editor`, `headless_typed` and `headless_scrolled`. I viewed all three. They are skipped under `-race` (the software renderer is about 100 times slower there) and run in the normal and cgo-free runs. No existing golden changed.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also with `emetos_claude`) · golangci-lint ✅ · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `emetos_gopls` tests ✅ · `FuzzDecode` 30 s (`-parallel=1`, `GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB`) ✅ with no crashers · display tests none.
- **Proof:** the step has no UI of its own (the Remote Work tab is 15.4), so the proof is the `headless_typed` golden: the headless view of a workspace after `x` was typed into it. `docs/implemented-proof-images/15.1-headless-typed.png`.

  ![15.1 headless view](implemented-proof-images/15.1-headless-typed.png)
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** new in `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`: "No public way to draw a view off screen and to read its pixels". The workaround in `internal/gui/app/headless_engine.go` uses a `gluttertest.Tester` as the rasterizer, on the UI thread (rendering on another goroutine races in the text engine's shape cache), and replaces it every 8 frames. This puts `gluttertest` and `testing` in the editor binary (+0.7 MB; it registers no flags) and makes a 1280x800 picture cost about 85 ms of the UI thread.
- **Deviations and follow-ups:** SPEC §10.18 "As built (step 15.1)" holds the wire table and the decisions:
  - fixed 4-byte lengths;
  - versions must be equal;
  - frames are relative to the confirmed picture;
  - the host keeps hashes, not pictures;
  - no caret blink in a view;
  - `NewHeadlessView` is not privilege-restricted (16.1's privileges cover events and commands only).

  Not built: extension contributions in the view, damage-limited rendering (needs Glutter), a view of a workspace that is not on screen. `TestHoverShowHoverCommandShowsFocusesAndHides` (editor) failed once under `-race` in a loaded full run and passed on every rerun; it is watched as a possible flake.
