- **Summary:** SPEC §10.18.
  - **Dependency:** `golang.org/x/crypto` v0.58.0 (`ssh`, `ssh/agent`), which brings in `golang.org/x/term` v0.47.0.
  - **`extensions/internal/sshlogin`** (used by Remote Work):
    - **Server on A:** public keys only (no password, keyboard-interactive or none), checked against the list at every attempt and again after the signature is verified. The host key is Ed25519 only, and there are at most 5 tries per connection.
    - **Channels and requests:** one channel of the given type (`emetos-remotework`). Any other channel type, any channel request (shell, exec, pty, env, subsystem, forwarding) and any global request is refused.
    - **Deadlines:** 10 s to log in, 10 s to open the channel, at most 16 connections logging in at once.
    - **Rate limit:** 5 failures per sliding minute per address (an IPv6 address counts as its /64), checked at accept and bounded to 4096 addresses.
    - **Client on B:** an OpenSSH or PEM key file with up to 3 passphrase tries (bytes wiped after parsing), or an `ssh-agent` socket passed in by the caller.
    - **Host key pinning:** in `remote-work-hosts.json`. First use is asked with no connection open; a changed key is refused (`SSHLoginHostKeyChanged`) and sends nothing.
  - **`extensions/internal/statefile`:** atomic 0600 writes in a 0700 folder, and a checked read: a regular file within its size, not group- or world-writable, and a private key not readable by others.
  - **The hub** (`extensions/remotework`):
    - one SSH listener while any open workspace with a folder has Remote Work on;
    - one session per workspace, where a new login replaces the old one;
    - a 256-bit token in memory, and the grant carries the QUIC certificate fingerprint (empty until 15.3, meaning "SSH only");
    - the idle timeout;
    - the banner "Remote Work: <comment> connected" with Disconnect;
    - notifications for logins and refused attempts, at most one per address per minute.
  - **Login on B:** `extensions/remotework/login` (the request and grant over the channel, `Connect`) and `loginui` (the passphrase, first-use and changed-key dialogs for the 15.4 tab).
  - **The page "Remote Work"** (`emetos.remotework.manage`):
    - the per-workspace switch with the listener status and connected clients;
    - the port (47123) and the idle timeout (1–1440 minutes) with Apply;
    - the allowed keys with Remove, paste, "Choose .pub File...", and a place for 15.5's Scan QR Code;
    - the host fingerprint;
    - the security notes.

    An unsafe `remote-work.json` locks the page and leaves Remote Work off.
  - **New APIs:** `api.Banners()`, `api.FileChooser()`, and `InputBoxOpts.Obscure`, each with a fake.
  - **Scripts:** `scripts/isolated.sh` and `scripts/proof.sh` take `--state <dir>`.
  - **New error tags:** about 50 (`SSHLogin*`, `StateFile*`, `RemoteWork*`, `LoginUICancelled`, `ExtensionBanner*`, `ExtensionFileChooser*`), all route-tested.
- **Tests:** all on loopback with ephemeral ports and isolated `XDG_*` folders:
  - a listed key logs in;
  - refused: an unlisted key, passwords and keyboard-interactive, other channel types, shell and exec, a second channel, silence, too many connections logging in;
  - an in-process agent on a temp socket;
  - a wrong passphrase;
  - first-use pinning, a changed key, and `Forget`;

  - the page, the dialogs and the banner in `gluttertest`.

## 15.3 QUIC transport and the TCP fallback

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Branch:** feat/step-15.3-quic
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.18.
  - **Dependency:** `github.com/quic-go/quic-go` v0.64.1 (MIT), which adds `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 as an indirect dependency. `NOTICE` lists quic-go, plus `x/crypto` and `x/net`, which were missing.
  - **`extensions/remotework/transport`:** one `Conn` interface for both links.
    - `Send` is reliable and bounded (512 messages, 8 MiB). `SendTiles` is best effort, latest wins. `Next` gives messages, completed tiles and the peer's Disconnect. `Close` takes a reason.
    - `HostConn` is A's side and `ClientConn` is B's.
    - `Presenter` (A: the differ, at most 2 pictures in flight, a retry, the 5 s full refresh over QUIC only) and `Screen` (B: canvas, confirm, refresh request) carry the picture flow.
  - **Host (A):** QUIC on the UDP port with the SSH port's number, with a self-signed P-256 certificate made in memory at start.
    - The certificate's SHA-256 goes into the 15.2 grant. A hub whose UDP port cannot open runs over SSH.
    - B's first stream must be a Hello, checked by its header before the payload (at most 133 bytes before the token is known). The token is compared in constant time and looked up with `Hub.SessionByToken`.
    - A connection that stays silent for 5 s is closed, and at most 32 connections may wait for their Hello.
  - **Client (B):** TLS 1.3 only, with ALPN `emetos-remotework/1`. `VerifyConnection` accepts exactly one certificate whose SHA-256 matches, in constant time, and never consults system roots. A mismatch is fatal and does not fall back to SSH (DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW 75).
  - **Tiles as datagrams:** an encoded `Tile` is split into chunks of 1,100 bytes behind a 14-byte header (frame, index, total, fragment, fragments), and is counted only when every fragment has arrived.
    - At 1280x800, 86% of a whole picture's tiles fit one datagram, the median tile is 128 bytes, and the largest is 3 KB.
    - B follows only the newest picture. Reassembly is bounded to 256 partial tiles and 2 MiB.
    - After a quiet time, B asks for what is missing with a new message, **`Missing` (type 14)**: frame, total and a bitmap. It backs off and asks at most 8 times without progress. The protocol stays at version 1 (DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW 76).
  - **Reliable stream:** one bidirectional QUIC stream. A write stalled for 15 s drops the link.
  - **Resume:** a dropped QUIC connection is redialled with the token (3 tries of 3 s), queued messages survive, and Refresh goes first.
  - **Fallback:** no QUIC handshake within 3 s, a grant without a fingerprint, or a failed resume moves the session to the SSH channel, with the same messages (tiles latest-wins). A session with no transport after 20 s ends.
  - **Idle timeout:** `Session.Touch` is called on every message A receives (not on tiles sent or keep-alives). The QUIC idle timeout is 15 s with a 5 s keep-alive.
  - **New error tags:** 15 `Transport*`, plus the protocol tags reused for `Missing`, all route-tested.
- **Tests:** all on loopback:
  - a session over QUIC with the real differ, presenter and screen;
  - refused: a wrong or expired token, a wrong certificate, bad Hellos (type, version, magic, a lying length, silence), another ALPN, the pending limit;
  - tiles of every size, stale tiles dropped, lost tiles asked for and resent;
  - the fallback with UDP blocked (a dropping proxy and a fake clock);
  - resume, and resume falling back to SSH;
  - bounded queues and malformed datagrams;
  - the hub end to end with the real 15.2 login, the idle timeout, turning Remote Work off freeing the UDP port;
  - `Missing` round trips and refusals.

  The agent ran the transport and hub tests with `-count=5 -race`; they passed.
- **Lossy-link measurement** (`TestLossyLinkMeasurement`: a UDP proxy with 50 ms each way, the real differ on the 1280x800 fixtures, 4 s of typing at 10 pictures a second). The agent's run:

  | Link | First picture (260 tiles) | Typing: shown / complete per s | Typing latency median / p95 | Scroll (132 tiles, 129 KB) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | no loss, no delay | 17 ms | 10.0 / 10.0 | 2 / 2 ms | 14 ms |
  | no loss, 50 ms each way | 197 ms | 6.8 / 6.8 | 54 / 58 ms | 278 ms |
  | 5% loss, 50 ms each way | 1.45 s | 6.2 / 5.0 | 55 / 221 ms | 3.6 s |

  Over 6 seeds of the lossy link: first picture 0.78–1.41 s, typing 6.0–7.3 pictures shown a second, scroll 3.4–4.6 s.

  My run: first picture 1.43 s; typing 5.5 shown and 5.0 complete a second, latency median 55 ms and p95 343 ms; scroll 2.6 s, and 3.4 s back; 80 of 1,537 packets dropped and 7 requests for lost tiles.

## 15.4 The remote window tab

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Branch:** feat/step-15.4-remote-tab
- **Summary:** SPEC §10.18, §10.14, §10.15.
  - **Window tab kind `emetos.remotework.tab`** ("Remote Work..." in the `+` menu): a connect form with host, port (47123), and a private key file (Choose...) or an SSH agent key (by comment and fingerprint), with a place for 15.5's QR code.
    - Connect unlocks the key (the passphrase dialog, asked once and kept unlocked only in memory for the tab's life), logs in (15.2's first-use and changed-key dialogs), asks for the workspace when A has several, and opens the 15.3 transport.
    - The tab is titled `<host>: <workspace>` with the remote icon.
    - Cards show connecting, reconnecting (over the last picture), and ended (Connect Again, Edit Connection, Close Tab).
  - **The picture** is the tab's size in logical pixels, drawn from `transport.Screen`. A resize is sent after 150 ms.
  - **Input:** keys with their text, input-method commits, mouse (moves coalesced at 8 ms) and scroll go to A.
    - A new `WindowTab.CaptureKeys` keeps keys away from B's workbench while the tab has focus.
    - B keeps its window and tab shortcuts (DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW 80).
  - **Clipboard:**
    - A's copy goes to B's clipboard;
    - B's paste chord sends B's clipboard text first, then the key;
    - at most 1 MiB, and never polled.
  - **Notifications:** A forwards its view's notifications (except its own Remote Work ones), with their actions run on A (new `HeadlessView.OnNotification` and `RunNotificationAction`, `notify.Service.RunAction`, `notify.Presenter.Mute`).
  - **Reconnection:** network failures (and A's `ReasonClosed`) retry after 1, 2, 4 ... 30 s. A refused key, Remote Work turned off, an unknown workspace or a changed host key end with their card.
  - **A's side** (`hostview.go`):
    - B's first Resize opens a headless view, and later ones resize it;
    - frames go to `Presenter`, input goes in order on the UI thread, and copies become Clipboard messages;
    - a closed view sends Disconnect (workspace closed), and any unexpected message ends the session with `ReasonProtocol`.
  - **Saved state:** host, port, key choice, key file, fingerprint and workspace, never a passphrase or token. A restored tab shows its form and does not connect by itself.
  - **Dev command:** `dev.remotework.connect` (debug and `emetos_dev` builds only).

## 15.5 Public keys by QR code

- **Date:** 2026-10-27

  - **Dependency:** `github.com/makiuchi-d/gozxing` v0.1.1, which brings in `golang.org/x/xerrors`.
    - Its license is MIT, not Apache-2.0 as the step said; the step's text is corrected.
    - `third_party/gozxing/` holds its MIT license and the Apache-2.0 license of ZXing, which it ports. `NOTICE` entry 15.
  - **`extensions/internal/keyqr`:**
    - **V4L2 through ioctls** with `golang.org/x/sys/unix`, without cgo, for 64-bit amd64 and arm64. Struct sizes, offsets and ioctl numbers are tested against the kernel's.
      - Capture devices only. MJPEG at 1280x720 is preferred, else YUYV at 640x480.
      - Four mmap buffers; the newest frame wins.
      - A poll in 50 ms slices, so a cancel or `Close` is answered quickly.
      - Errnos become tags (busy, denied, gone).
    - **Frames:** MJPEG with the standard Huffman tables inserted when missing, and YUYV to `image.YCbCr`. Dimensions are checked before decoding, and frames over 1920x1080 or 16 MiB are refused.
    - **QR decoding** with gozxing (TRY_HARDER, also at 2/3 and 1/2 scale), off the UI thread, one frame every 100 ms. The text is parsed with the 15.2 authorized-key rules.
    - **QR encoding** of a public line only: level M, else L, up to 452 px with whole pixels per module.

    - a live preview with a camera picker;
    - the first valid key stops the camera and shows its type, fingerprint and comment (Cancel, Scan Again, Add Key);
    - other QR codes say "not a public key";
    - no frame is kept.
  - **Show My Public Key as QR Code** in the "Remote Work..." form shows the public half only. It comes from the `.pub`, or from the clear header of an OpenSSH key, or from the agent key; a PEM key asks for its passphrase.

  - The image widget.

## Fix: Glutter 1.9.1

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Branch:** fix/glutter-1.9.1 (not a step of the plan)
- **Summary:** Emetos moves to Glutter v1.9.1. That fixes the 15.1 entry of `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`, "No public way to draw a view off screen and to read its pixels".
  - **The headless view runs on `offscreen.View`.**
    - The hand-made binding, the `PlatformHost`, the `gluttertest.Tester` used as a rasterizer and `headlessPaceFactor` are gone (`headless_engine.go` is deleted).
    - Frames are paced by `MaxFrameRate` (30), and are drawn on the view's goroutine, redrawing only the damage.
    - `gluttertest` is no longer in the editor binary.
    - The extension API is unchanged.
  - **The view's clipboard:** the view keeps a clipboard of its own, through a parent binding that never draws (DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW 94). Without it, Glutter's view would have reached the host's desktop clipboard.
  - **Numbers at 1280x800:**
    - a typed character takes 4.7 ms of the UI thread (82 ms with 1.8.3) and reaches `OnFrame` about 20 ms after the key;
    - the view takes at most about 14% of the UI thread;
    - the binary is 88.3 MB with the release tag (88.6 MB before).
  - **The tile differ** does not use the damage yet (DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW 95).
  - **The view's caret** stays solid.
- **Main files:** `go.mod`, `internal/gui/app/headless.go`, `headless_clipboard.go` (new), `headless_engine.go`, `race_test.go` and `norace_test.go` (deleted), `docs/SPEC.md` (§10.18 "As built (Glutter 1.9.1)"), `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`.
- **Tests:**
  - **clipboard:** the find and quick input boxes of a view never read or write the host's clipboard or primary selection; the paste is the client's text and copies reach `OnCopy`. Removing the fix makes these tests fail with the host's sentinel text.
  - **main window:** its boxes keep the desktop clipboard.
  - **view clipboard:** the formats and selections of the view's clipboard.
  - **pictures:** a picture made before `OnFrame` was set is handed over.
  - **benchmark:** `BenchmarkHeadlessFrame` has typed, scroll and window-only cases.
  - **race:** the headless golden now runs under `-race` too, and the headless tests passed with `-race -count=5`.
  - **rig fix:** the Remote Work test rig closes its views before stopping the host (a goroutine leak the race run found).
- **Goldens:** none changed. The three headless goldens match, as does every other golden on 1.9.1.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also with `emetos_claude` and `emetos_camera`) · golangci-lint ✅ · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `emetos_gopls` tests ✅ · `go mod tidy -diff` clean · display tests none.

## Step 17b.1: Real input, and typing reaches every input box

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Branch:** feat/step-17b.1-real-input
- **Summary:** Emetos is now tested with real keyboard and pointer events (a Wayland virtual keyboard and pointer in sway). Every input box keeps taking keys after the first one, which fixes the desktop bug "the keyboard stopped working until I clicked again the input box".
- **Cause:** `kit.InputBox` removed the placeholder's `Stack` at the first key. That mounted the `EditableText` again with the focus already on its node, and Glutter opens the input connection only on a focus change, so every later key was dropped.
- **Fix:**
  - the input box's tree is the same with or without the placeholder;
  - a click in a focused box with no connection reconnects it (`RequestKeyboard`);
  - the quick input takes typed keys from the moment it is shown, and a focus node takes the arrows, Enter and Escape at once;
  - `kit.TypeAhead` (new) does the same for Find, Replace, the rename box and the explorer's inline input;
  - the editor's `Stack` layers are keyed, so a layer that appears no longer remounts the rename box.
- **Also found by real input and fixed:**
  - Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z in an input box went to the editor's commands; the box now runs them on its own text;
  - a group's focus retry could take the focus from a quick input opened just after it and close it.
- **Harness:**
  - `internal/testenv/realinput`: the Wayland client, with one keyboard and one pointer for the whole run, plus sway IPC;
  - `internal/testenv/display`: starts an isolated debug Emetos, sends real input, reads state through the dev socket, takes screenshots;
  - dev server `EMETOS_DEV_SOCKET`, with the read-only `dev.inputs` and `dev.editor` (SPEC §15.2);
  - `scripts/realinput.sh [--desktop]`: runs under the headless sway, or in a nested sway window on the desktop.
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/kit/inputbox.go`, `kit/typeahead.go` (new), `internal/gui/quickinput/host.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{widget,findstate,rename_widget}.go`, `internal/gui/views/explorer/{edit,view}.go`, `internal/gui/app/{keys,group,devserver,devquery}.go`, `internal/testenv/`, `cmd/emetos/realinput_display_test.go`, `scripts/realinput.sh`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§10.2, §10.6, §15.1, §15.2 "As built (step 17b.1)").
- **Tests:**
  - 12 real-input display tests: Quick Open, Find, settings search, keybindings search, explorer rename, Notes, Problems filter, scratchpad, edit shortcuts, command palette, Go to Line, and the proofs. Before the fix, ten of them failed (`app.go` gave `"p"`, `hello world` gave `"h"`); the command palette and Go to Line tests passed and are kept as regression tests;
  - unit tests through the platform's key path: `TestInputBoxTypedKeysReachTheBox`, the click reconnect, the edit shortcuts, `TestHostTakesTheKeysTypedBeforeItsFirstFrame` and `TestEditChordsInATextFieldAreTheFields` all failed before the fix;
  - `TypeAhead`, dev server and `realinput` tests, with route tests for every new tag;
  - `TestTheInputBoxesOfTheWindowKeepTheClipboardOfTheDesktop` changed: Ctrl+A then Ctrl+V in the command palette now replaces the `>` too, as in VS Code.
- **Goldens:** `keybindings_recording_{dark,light}`, `dialog_passphrase_dark` (asterisks, and the caret in the right place) and agents `completion_commands`; viewed.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also with `emetos_display`) · golangci-lint ✅ · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ (`internal/gui/app` was killed once for lack of memory while other programs filled the swap, and passed when run alone) · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `scripts/realinput.sh` (headless sway, race, 12 tests) ✅.
- **Proof:** `docs/implemented-proof-images/17b.1-quickopen.png` (Quick Open with `app.go` typed by the virtual keyboard) and `17b.1-note.png` (a note whose title and two-line body were typed the same way), made with `scripts/realinput.sh --shots docs/implemented-proof-images`.

## Step 17b.2: A fast Markdown preview

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Branch:** feat/step-17b.2-markdown-preview
- **Summary:** The preview of a large document opens at once and stays light. The preview of a document of 700 KB with 150 images (the size of this file) used to freeze the window and take 2 GB.
- **Changes:**
  - **Lazy list:** the page preview (`markdown.NewView`) builds only the blocks within 250 px of the viewport. Their heights are estimated, then measured, in a Fenwick tree, and positions are anchored to the block at the top, so an image that loads above the viewport moves nothing on screen. `ScrollToLine`, `TopLine` and the editor's scroll sync work as before. Hover, Flow and Compact keep the column.
  - **Images:** `markdown.ImageCache` decodes off the UI thread, two at a time, at the size shown on screen. Its budget is 64 MB, with least recently used images dropped first. Failures are cached and keep the alt text.
  - **Updates:** a change is parsed after a 300 ms throttle (as VS Code's `preview.ts`). A text over 16 KB is parsed off the UI thread. Blocks are keyed by their content, so an edit builds only its block.
  - **Highlighting:** done once per block, from a cache of the last 256 code blocks.
  - **Start:** a restored session with the preview of a large file draws its first frame without waiting for the parse.
  - **Dev command:** `dev.markdown` returns the preview's statistics.
- **Also fixed:** the README's link to SPEC §10.16, which the M17c plan had broken.
- **Main files:** `extension/ui/markdown/{preview,controller,heights,estimate,keys,images,imageview,tokens,render,view}.go`, `extensions/markdown/markdown.go`, `extension/ui/uitest/mdfixture/` (the generated fixture), `internal/testenv/display/framestats.go`, `internal/gui/app/devquery.go`, `cmd/emetos/preview_display_test.go`, `scripts/perf.sh`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§10.15 "As built (step 17b.2)", §14, §15.2), `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`.
- **Tests:**
  - only the visible blocks are built;
  - the wheel and the scroll bar, and `ScrollToLine`/`TopLine` over estimated and measured heights;
  - scrolling before the parse ends;
  - an edit rebuilds only its block, after the delay, and the view stays at its block;
  - the image cache: sizes, budget, eviction, failures, abandoned decodes, with route tests for its tags;
  - `BenchmarkPreview*`;
  - real-input display tests: `TestRealInputBigPreviewOpensAndScrolls`, its proof, and `...StartDoesNotWaitForThePreview`;
  - before the fix, the display scenario took 9.2 s to answer, used 2,096 MB more, and drew every frame in over 16 ms.
- **Numbers** (headless, llvmpipe, 1280x800):

  | Metric | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Open to first blocks | 9.1–9.6 s | 157–259 ms |
  | Memory over the file as text | +2,090–2,290 MB | +116–129 MB |
  | Blocks built | 3,224 | 7–11 |
  | Raster per frame, average | 786 ms | 12.6–18 ms |

  - The worst UI-thread frame, 40–69 ms, is the first frame after a jump, which highlights code on the UI thread.
  - The GPU numbers come from the desktop pass, step 17b.5.
- **Goldens:** none changed; `preview_dark.png` viewed.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also `emetos_display`) · golangci-lint ✅ · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ (my full run: 100 packages, exit 0) · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `scripts/realinput.sh` ✅.
  - `TestAPictureThatWaitedForOnFrameAndARefreshAreHandedOver` (`internal/gui/app`) failed in the agent's run while the machine was short of memory, also on main. It passed 3 times out of 3 when run again; it is timing-sensitive under load.
- **Proof:** `docs/implemented-proof-images/17b.2-preview.png`, made through the real-input harness: the preview of the fixture scrolled to its middle.

## Step 17b.3: Brackets, snippets and signature help as in VS Code

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Branch:** feat/step-17b.3-overtype-snippets
- **Summary:** Typing `)` before a `)` that the user typed inserts a new one, as VS Code does. The closing `)` of a completion is typed over and no longer stays in a growing tab stop. The signature help closes when its answer is stale.
- **Causes and fixes:**
  - **Typing over the user's `)`**
    - *Cause:* the input method hands the editor the whole line, and the change was worked out from the first and last differing characters. `// z)` → `// z))` read as "a `)` replaced by itself", so it took the composition path, which skips typing-over and auto-closing.
    - *Fix:* `editedStretch` (`internal/gui/editor/input.go`) starts from the input method's selection, as VS Code's `TextAreaState.deduceInput` does.
  - **The closing `)` of a completion**
    - *Cause:* gopls sends `Println(${1:})`. VS Code tracks the closing character at the end of a snippet as auto-closed (`cursor.ts` `_findAutoClosingPairs`); Emetos did not, so a typed `)` went into the empty `$1`, which grew.
    - *Fix:* ported as `edit.SnippetPairs` / `SnippetAutoClosed`, through a new `snippet.Editor.OnAutoClosed` hook (completions, `insertSnippet` and Emmet).
  - **Signature help**
    - *Cause:* an answer about changed text was dropped, but the request stayed pending, so the old hints stayed on screen.
    - *Fix:* it now cancels the request. Closing on cursor moves and on Escape already matched VS Code.
  - **A snippet with only `$0`** (`Sprintf($0)`) already ended its session at once. Regression tests were added; they passed before the fix.
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/editor/{input,snippets,signature,dev}.go`, `internal/core/edit/snippetclosed.go` (new), `internal/core/snippet/session.go`, `internal/core/autoclose/autoclose.go`, `internal/core/lsp/lsptest/` (an `insideParens` answer, as gopls does for signature help), `internal/gui/app/devquery.go` (`dev.editor` gives `inSnippet`, `tabStops`, `suggestVisible` and `signatureVisible`), `cmd/emetos/editing_display_test.go` (new), `docs/SPEC.md` (§8.6.4, §9.9.2, §9.12, §15.1 "As built (step 17b.3)").
- **Tests:**
  - `TestSnippetPairs` (17 cases) and `TestSnippetAutoClosed`, from `_findAutoClosingPairs`;
  - `TestEditedStretch` (15) and `TestKeysTypeOver...` (6; 3 failed before the fix);
  - snippet, controller, signature, Emmet and `dev.editor` tests;
  - VS Code's 10 `autoClosingOvertype` cases, already ported, still pass.
  - **Real input**, with a fake language server, and how each did on the unfixed code:
    - `TestRealInputTypingOverAClosingBracketTheUserTyped` failed, giving `// z)`;
    - `TestRealInputCompletionWithAFinalTabStopEndsTheSnippet` (Enter and Tab) failed, giving `fmt.Sprintf(("x")`, with the signature help still open;
    - `TestRealInputTypingOverTheClosingBracketOfACompletion` failed with the snippet fix removed, giving `fmt.Println("x"))`;
    - `TestRealInputSignatureHelpClosesWhenTheCursorLeavesTheArguments` passed before the fix; it is a guard.
- **Goldens:** none changed.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also `emetos_display`) · golangci-lint ✅ · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ (100 packages) · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `scripts/realinput.sh` ✅ (19 tests).
- **Proof:** the real-input tests above, which type with a virtual keyboard and read the document through `dev.editor`; the step asks for no image.
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none

## Step 17b.4: The Glutter issues and the cost of an idle window

- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Branch:** feat/step-17b.4-glutter-idle
- **Summary:** Glutter's bugs from the desktop test are written down with the fix Glutter should make. The crash of the gesture arena is avoided in Emetos, and Emetos's own share of what an idle window allocates is almost halved. What is left is Glutter's renderer.
- **Gesture arena (crash):**
  - *What triggers it:* every tap target is the lone member of an arena that a mouse moving away rejects. Slow frames batch the pointer events, and Linux gives the mouse pointer id 0, so the posted `resolveByDefault` takes a member of an old, empty arena and panics.
  - *Workaround:* `fixGestureArena` (`internal/gui/app/arenafix.go`, `// Glutter:`) gives the binding an arena manager whose microtasks run before the next pointer event, as Flutter's do. It is installed at the window root and in each headless view.
- **Idle cost:**
  - **Emetos's share:** the cursors layer read the text of every visible row on every blink to find control characters. `controlCache` (`internal/gui/editor/display_paint.go`) now keeps them per row until the document changes.
  - **Glutter's share:** 99% of what an idle frame allocates is Glutter's renderer, which flattens the whole scene every frame (new `GLUTTER-ISSUES.md` entry). It is garbage, not a leak: the live heap stays flat.

  | Case | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Emetos's share, per blink frame, 10,000-line Go file (headless) | 17.0 KB, 283 allocations | 10.5 KB, 132 allocations |
  | Same, with the Markdown preview | 24.3 KB | 13.1 KB |
  | Whole frame, Go file | 1.94 MB | 1.87 MB |
  | Whole frame, preview | 8.4 MB | 8.5 MB |
- **Main files:** `internal/gui/app/arenafix.go` (new), `tray.go`, `headless.go`, `internal/gui/editor/display_paint.go`, `overlay.go`, `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` ("Idle allocation"), `docs/SPEC.md` (§14 "As built (step 17b.4)").
- **Tests:**
  - `TestGestureArenaSurvivesPointerIDReuseInOneTurn` (Glutter alone panics with `index out of range [0] with length 0`);
  - `TestTheArenaIsFixedInTheApplicationAndInTheView` (fails if either call is removed);
  - `controlcache_test.go` (an unchanged frame allocates nothing);
  - `TestIdleBlinkFrameAllocationStaysInBudget`: 10,000-line Go file, budget 6 KB and 120 allocations per blink frame. It measured 8.0 KB and 147 allocations before the fix, 4.6 KB and 92 after.
- **Goldens:** none changed.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also `emetos_display`) · golangci-lint ✅ · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ · `scripts/realinput.sh` ✅ (my full run, exit 0; the agent's two runs had timing failures while the machine was at load 50, each passing alone).
- **Proof:** the tests above; the step asks for no image.
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:**
  - completed: the renderer draws shapes outside the clip and hashes every path every frame;
  - new:
    - the gesture arena resolves on the next loop turn, and the mouse always has pointer id 0;
    - the keyboard logs `no_keymap` at error level;
    - the renderers flatten the whole scene every frame.

## Step 17b.6: The findings of the desktop pass

- **Date:** 2026-10-28
- **Branch:** feat/step-17b.6-desktop-findings (rebased onto the Glutter 1.9.2 fix)
- **Summary:** the findings that 17b.5 planned (D4, D5, D6, D10, D11) and the two flaky tests (D12) are fixed, each with a regression test that failed before its fix. Every finding of `docs/DESKTOP-PASS.md` is now fixed or not a bug. The manager's pass on the user's desktop is below.
- **Fixed:**
  - **D5, keys typed fast.** The cause was a key that arrived before its input was built and was handled by the old widgets.
    - `kit.TypeAhead` put the keys it took into the input but never told the input's owner, so the find widget did not search.
    - A handler of the hardware keyboard cannot keep the focus tree from seeing a key. So the letter after F2 also started the tree's find, and Enter made a new line.
    - After Ctrl+, no node had the focus for a few frames.
    - The fix: `TypeAhead` takes the key with a hardware handler and claims it from the focus tree with an early handler. It tells the owner through `onChange`, and keeps Enter, the arrows, Home, End and Delete, in order, until the input has the focus. `StartTypeAheadLater` waits for an input that is not built yet (the settings and keybindings editors' search).
  - **D4, the panel's tabs** (`workbench/paneloverflow.go`). The tabs get their room first. The view's actions get what is left and hide under 130 px. Tabs that do not fit go into a `...` menu, and the active tab always shows. A tab is never cut.
  - **D6:** a right click hides the editor's hover (`secondaryDown` calls `HideHover`).
  - **D10:** the empty Notes view shows "No notes yet." over a "New Note" button.
  - **D11:** a window tab is 1 px wider than its measured label (`tabLabelSlack`), so a label is never cut when there is room. `dev.texts` reports `cut` paragraphs.
  - **D12, two flaky tests, both wrong in the test:**
    - `TestAPictureThatWaitedForOnFrameAndARefreshAreHandedOver` read pictures queued before `Close`. It also showed a real window: `headlessView.Close` now waits up to 250 ms for a call of the frame function that is running.
    - `TestTheCoreTopicsDriveARealWorkspace` read the tab strip before the frames that build it.
    - Each now passes 200 runs in a row.
- **Harness:** `realinput.NoKeyDelay`, `TypeBatch`, `PressBatch`, `Hold` and `TextCombos`. `display.App` gets `SetKeyRepeat` (sway's repeat rate) and `ResizeWindow`. The 25 ms delays of the older desktop tests are gone; they type at 10 ms.
- **Main files:**
  - `internal/gui/kit/{typeahead,tabs}.go`, `internal/gui/editor/{findstate,rename_widget,pointer}.go`, `internal/gui/views/explorer/edit.go`;
  - `internal/gui/{settingsui,keybindingsui}/editor.go`, `internal/gui/app/{settingspane,keybindingspane,devworkbench,headless}.go`;
  - `internal/gui/workbench/{paneloverflow,workbench}.go`, `extensions/notes/notes.go`, `extension/headless.go`;
  - `internal/testenv/{display/app.go,realinput/*}`;
  - `docs/DESKTOP-PASS.md`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§15.1 "Real input as built (step 17b.6)"), `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`.
- **Tests:**
  - `TestDesktopFastKeys{Find,Rename,NewFile,QuickOpen,CommandPalette,SettingsSearch,KeybindingsSearch,Notes}` each run at 10 ms, with no delay, and in one batch. Before the fix:
    - Find: "timed out waiting for the cursor on the end of the first match";
    - Rename: the input was left with "f";
    - Settings search: `last state: ""`.
  - `TestDesktopFastKeysHeld` holds a key at 25 and 50 repeats a second, in the editor and in the find box.
  - `TestFastKeysAfterCtrlFSearch`, `TestKeysTypedRightAfterTheKeyThatOpensTheInputGoToIt` and three `TypeAhead` tests fail when the claim is removed.
  - `TestDesktopPanelTabsAreWholeAndOverflow` checks the tabs at 1280, 1024 and 760 px. `TestPanelTabsAreWholeAndOverflowIntoAMenu` and `TestPanelOverflowMenuListsTheHiddenTabs` also cover D4.
  - `TestDesktopHoverHidesWhenTheContextMenuOpens`, `TestDesktopEmptyNotesViewHasAWelcomeButton`, `TestDesktopWindowTabLabelIsNotCutWhenThereIsRoom`.
  - `TestCloseWaitsForTheCallOfOnFrameThatIsRunning` and `TestAFunctionOfOnFrameMayCloseTheView`.
- **Goldens:** 66 changed in `internal/gui/app` and `internal/gui/workbench`. The window tab is 1 px wider, and only the title bar's tab strip moves. The agent looked at every one, old beside new.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also `emetos_display` and `emetos_gopls`) · golangci-lint ✅ (also `--build-tags emetos_display`) · error-tags --untested ✅ · go test -race ✅ (my run on the final code, 100 packages, exit 0) · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ (my run, 100 packages, exit 0) · `scripts/realinput.sh` ✅ (my headless run after the rebase onto Glutter 1.9.2: 101 tests and subtests, exit 0; the D13 agent's run after its change: exit 0).
- **Proof:** the 83 screenshots of the agent's last run, viewed by the agent; I viewed the panel tabs at 1024 px and with the menu, and the Notes welcome.
- **The manager's desktop pass** (`scripts/realinput.sh --desktop` in a nested sway on the user's desktop, Radeon 8060S, Vulkan, `EMETOS_REALINPUT_RACE=0`). I viewed all 83 screenshots and found nothing new in them. Every test passed except `TestRealInputBigPreviewOpensAndScrolls` (4 of 4 runs), which is finding **D13**:
  - the test counted the editor window's first draw as scrolling, because frame statistics are logged once a second and the first window had not been flushed;
  - that first draw is 0.9 s on the GPU and 4 to 5 s on llvmpipe with an empty Mesa shader cache. Every display test starts with one, because `XDG_CACHE_HOME` is fresh. With a warm cache it is 0.29 s;
  - the 100 to 120 ms of UI thread is the debug build's `AssertCurrent` (`runtime.Stack`); the release build takes 10 to 20 ms;
  - the fix: the scrolling is measured from the next stats window (`App.WaitFrameWindow`), and the open's frames have their own budget (`previewFirstFrameBudget`, `App.SlowFrames`);
  - afterwards it passed 2 of 2 on the desktop: 43 to 45 ms for the open's slowest frame (debug build), 0 frames over 16 ms while scrolling, 2.0 to 2.2 ms of renderer per frame.
  - **GPU numbers** (`scripts/perf.sh --session --no-go --no-huge`, `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` "Desktop pass (step 17b.6)"):
    - met: idle with the focus 0.47% of a core, without it 0 frames; typing 2.3 ms a frame; the start with no folder 260 ms;
    - missed: the 10 MB open 410 ms (target 300), the restored start 570 ms (target 400), the worst scrolling build 8.24 ms (target 8).
    - `docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md` 3.11/10.1 now leaves only the 200 MB open, the Go benchmarks and the decision on the missed targets to the user.
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** two new entries. The first: still present in 1.9.2 (its keyboard and focus code is unchanged from 1.9.1). A handler of the hardware keyboard cannot keep the focus tree from seeing a key, and early key handlers do not run while no node has the focus. The workaround is in `kit/typeahead.go`.
  The second (D13): in a debug build, `UIThread.AssertCurrent` calls `runtime.Stack` on every mark-dirty call; there is no workaround in Emetos.

## Step 17d.1: The emulator

- **Date:** 2026-10-28
- **Branch:** feat/step-17d.1-emulator
- **Summary:** Emetos's own terminal emulator, with no UI (`extensions/terminal/emulator`), written in Go from ECMA-48, the DEC manuals and parser state machine of vt100.net, "XTerm Control Sequences" and `infocmp xterm-256color`. Nothing of xterm.js or of any other terminal was used, read or copied.
- **API:** `New(rows, cols, Options)`; the owner goroutine calls `Write`, `Resize`, `SetScrollback`, `Reset` and `SetTheme`; the UI takes `Snapshot(*Frame)` (only the changed rows, under one lock, with the cursor, the modes, the style and link tables and the palette); `ReadLines`, `LineText` and `Text` read the scrollback; callbacks for replies, the title, the bell, the working folder (OSC 7), the palette, the clipboard and the OSC codes it does not handle (for shell integration, 17d.5); `EncodeKey`, `EncodePaste`, `EncodeFocus` and `EncodeMouse`; `Serialize`.
- **Built:** the C0 and C1 controls, the ESC and CSI sequences of cursor movement, erasing, editing, scroll regions, tabs and character sets; SGR with 16, 256 and true colors and every attribute of SPEC §10.25 (underline styles and colors too); the DEC private modes of §10.25 (the alternate screen, bracketed paste, mouse tracking with the 1006 and 1015 encodings, focus events, synchronized output, the cursor); the device status and attribute replies; OSC 0/1/2, 4, 10/11/12, 7, 8 and 52 (to a callback); wide characters, combining marks, reflow on resize and serialization. Each handler cites its document. What is ignored (sixel, rectangular operations, the kitty keyboard protocol and others) is listed in SPEC §10.25 "As built (step 17d.1)". Limits bound every size (2,000×2,000 cells, 32 parameters, a 64 KiB OSC string, a 16,384-cell reflowed line).
- **Speed** (my run, 160×45, no `-race`; SPEC §14): plain ASCII 854 MB/s (budget 400), a color change every 8 characters 241 MB/s (100), CJK and emoji 371 MB/s (150), scrolling in a region 400 MB/s, cursor motion 228 MB/s, a new true color every 8 characters 110 MB/s; 10,000 lines of scrollback at 160 columns 13.4 MB (limit 16 MB); an idle snapshot, a write with a snapshot and a scroll with a snapshot allocate nothing. `TestThroughputBudgets`, `TestScrollbackMemory` and `TestSnapshotAllocations` hold them.
- **Tests:** table-driven from the documents (every sequence with its defaults and limits, the parser's states with input cut at every byte, C1, invalid UTF-8, scroll regions, the alternate screen, wide characters at the edge, combining marks, reflow, the key and mouse tables, the replies); a serialization round trip over seeded random sequences (60,000 seeds passed once, 400 in the suite; it found about ten bugs, all fixed); invariants checked after every random, fuzzed and recorded input; `vim`, `less`, `htop`, `tmux` and `git log --color` recorded through the test's own pseudo-terminal in a temporary `HOME`, with goldens of the cells, and the recordings replayed without the programs; `FuzzParser` (30 s, `-parallel=1`, no failure); the archtest rule `EmulatorImportsUI`.
- **Decisions:** 120 to 126 of `docs/DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW.md`. Decision 121 (ED 2 does not push the screen into the scrollback) differs from what VS Code shows after Ctrl+L, and step 17d.2 changes it.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also `emetos_display`) · golangci-lint ✅ (also `--build-tags emetos_display`) · error-tags --untested ✅ · `go mod tidy -diff` clean · go test -race ✅ (my run, 99 packages, exit 0) · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ (my run, 99 packages, exit 0).
- **Proof:** none (the emulator has no UI; the goldens of the recorded programs are its proof).
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none new.

## Step 17d.2: The Terminal panel

- **Date:** 2026-10-28
- **Branch:** feat/step-17d.2-terminal-panel
- **Summary:** terminals in the panel, as VS Code has them. Ctrl+\` opens a shell in a pseudo-terminal, drawn by Emetos's own emulator (17d.1) with a glyph atlas, with several terminals, splits, the tabs list, selection, copy and paste, the scrollback, the context menu and VS Code's commands, keys, context keys, settings and colors. Nothing of xterm.js or of another terminal was used, read or copied; `foot` was only run, as a program, for the comparison.
- **The emulator's ED 2:** on the normal screen, `CSI 2 J` now moves the lines up to the last non-blank one into the scrollback before it clears, as VS Code shows after Ctrl+L in bash (decision 121 updated). ED 3 still clears the scrollback.
- **Structure** (`extensions/terminal`):
  - `Terminal` (`session.go`) is the model and does not know where it is shown. It holds the process, the emulator, and reader, parser and writer goroutines, with flow control (64 KiB reads, a pause above 100,000 bytes, a resume below 5,000).
  - The pane (`pane.go`, `pane_input.go`) handles keys, the mouse, selection, the wheel, the scrollbar, the input method and bracketed paste with VS Code's multi-line warning (a bar, not a dialog).
  - The widget (`atlas.go`, `grid.go`, `render.go`, `shapes.go`, `decor.go`) draws the cells with two `DrawAtlas` calls. Box-drawing, block, braille and Powerline characters are drawn as shapes. A frame with no change paints nothing.
  - `terminals.go`, `panel.go` and `terminal.go` hold the groups, the tabs list, the splits, the commands and the manifest.
- **New in the extension API:**
  - `Contributes.ContextKeys`;
  - `ViewContent.AllowCommand` (VS Code's `commandsToSkipShell`);
  - `ViewHandle.Hide`;
  - `extension.MenuTerminal`;
  - the refusal class `terminal` for clients of a hosted workspace;
  - `ui.SplitView` and `ui.ContextMenu`.
  - Also: `pty.ForegroundPid`, and the dev query `dev.terminals`.
- **Registered** with VS Code's ids and Linux keys:
  - toggle, new, split, kill, focus, next and previous, pane focus and resize, copy, paste, select all, clear and the scroll commands;
  - the 15 context keys, the `terminal.integrated.*` settings and every `terminal.*` color.

## Fix: Glutter 1.9.4

- **Date:** 2026-10-28
- **Branch:** fix/glutter-1.9.3 (it began with 1.9.3 and ended with 1.9.4)
- **Summary:** Glutter 1.9.3 fixed both entries of `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md` that Emetos had sent: the early key handlers of the focus manager now run also when no node has the focus (its step 29.23), and `UIThread.IsCurrent` compares a goroutine token in about 2 ns instead of parsing `runtime.Stack` (29.24). 1.9.4 (29.26) makes the token one that is never reused.
- **Changes:**
  - `kit.TypeAhead` takes the keys with one early key handler; the hardware handler and the claim of the key it took are gone, and so is the `// Glutter:` comment.
  - The two entries are removed from `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`; the two of step 17d.2 stay (still present in 1.9.4).
  - **A race in Emetos's test rig, not a Glutter bug.** With 1.9.3, `TestTheInputBoxesOfAViewNeverTouchTheClipboardOfTheHost` (its `shift+insert` cases) failed in 19 runs of 20 without the race detector. The manager first blamed the token; the agent showed it was the rig: `offscreen.View` paces its frames by the real clock while the test pumps a fake one, so a key came before the view laid out the pasted text, and 1.9.2's slow check had spent enough real time to hide it. `rigFrameRate` is now 1,000,000 (the pacing never holds a frame back); the test fails 20 of 20 on 1.9.4 without it and passes 40 of 40 with it.
  - The debug build is faster (`docs/PERFORMANCE.md` "After Glutter 1.9.3"): the UI thread of the frame that opens the 700 KB preview 8.3 to 9.1 ms (before 42 to 55 ms), the first frame of the window 10 to 12.5 ms (before 100 to 114 ms). `previewFirstFrameBudget` is 20 ms (was 100 ms).
- **Checks** (the manager's run on top of 17e.3): gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also `emetos_display` and `emetos_gopls`) · golangci-lint ✅ (also `--build-tags emetos_display`) · error-tags --untested ✅ · `go mod tidy -diff` clean · go test -race ✅ (98 packages, exit 0) · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ (98 packages, exit 0) · `scripts/realinput.sh` ✅ (the whole suite, exit 0).
- **Glutter issues:** two removed; none new (a wish, not a bug: `offscreen.ViewOpts` could take a clock, so that tests are not paced by the real one).

## Step 17e.2: Search across files

## Fix: the preview's start test measured the driver's noise

- **Date:** 2026-10-28
- **Branch:** fix/preview-start-test-noise
- **Summary:** `TestRealInputBigPreviewStartDoesNotWaitForThePreview` compared one cold start with a small preview and one with the big one against 150 ms; each first frame was 4 to 5 s of llvmpipe's shader compile with an empty Mesa cache, about ±500 ms of noise, so it failed under load (by 241, 410, 471 and 672 ms in the runs of 17c.1 to 17d.3). ## Fix: the Search view's frame test measured the machine's load

- **Date:** 2026-10-28
- **Branch:** fix/search-frame-test-load
- **Summary:** `TestTheUIThreadStaysUnderAFrameWhileAHugeSearchStreams` (17e.2; SPEC §14 "Search") timed each turn of the UI thread by the wall clock. Alone the longest turn is 9 to 12 ms against 16 ms, but beside the other agents' builds it measured 18.8 to 66 ms and failed three runs. Now each turn is timed by the CPU clock of its thread, the stream runs up to five times and the best run counts, and the limit scales by a fixed reference workload timed in the same run (never below 16 ms; under `-race` both ×4). A new test, `TestTheEngineAsksTheUIThreadOnceForAllItsFilesAndWaitsBetweenAsks`, checks the batching of decision 158 with no clock: 1,000 files that come before the UI thread looks are one ask and one take.
- **Numbers:** 20 of 20 under 24 memory-burning processes and the other agents (before: 5 of 5 failed at load 28); `-race` 5 of 5 (31 to 34 ms against its limit). A tree rebuild made 4 times slower fails it 3 of 3; making the engine ask once per file fails the batching test.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · `go vet` (also `CGO_ENABLED=0`) ✅ · golangci-lint on the package ✅ · my run after the rebase onto 17d.5: `go test -race -count=2` and `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -count=3` of `extensions/search` ✅. Only the test file changed.

## Fix: four tests that failed when the machine was loaded

- **Branch:** fix/load-sensitive-tests
- **`TestThroughputBudgets`** (17d.1; `extensions/terminal/emulator/bench_test.go`) measured MB/s by the wall clock and failed at 311 and 327 MB/s for 400 (plain ASCII), 164 for 200 (scrolling in a region) and 36 for 40 (the worst-case style table) while other builds ran. It now times a run by the CPU clock of its OS thread (`CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID`, the subtest locks its thread), runs a case up to 8 times and fails only when the best run is under the budget, and scales the budget of each run down by how much slower a piece of reference work (`referenceWork`, which does not use the emulator; 8.5 ms of CPU time on a quiet machine) was than on a quiet one. `TestThroughputBudgetsFailASlowEmulator` holds that mechanism without a clock. With the ASCII fast path of `parse` switched off for a moment (`if false && ...`) the test fails (plain ASCII 122 MB/s, scrolling in a region 97 MB/s); with 40 busy loops on the 32 cores it passed 20 of 20 (the budgets of the runs were 157 to 161 MB/s then).
- **`TestTheEventsOfATerminalFromItsStartToItsEnd`** (17d.4; `extensions/terminal/events_test.go`): the test shell turns the terminal's ECHO off as soon as it has started (raw mode, as bash's readline does), and an input event is `Hidden` when ECHO is off (decision 185), so the first event was hidden or not by whether the test typed before or after the shell started. The test now runs the shell with the new argument `--tty-echo` (it leaves ECHO on and lets the terminal echo) and waits for the shell's "ready"; `TestInputToAShellThatTurnedEchoOffIsHidden` holds the other half, also after waiting for "ready".
- **`TestGoldenTheFindWidgetAndItsHighlights`** (17d.3; `extensions/terminal/pane_find_test.go`): `waitSearched` drew frames (80 ms of the fake clock each) while it waited in real time for the search goroutine, so the number of frames, and with it the phase of the find input's blinking caret in the golden image (30 pixels), depended on the load. It now hands over the posted answers without drawing and then draws a fixed number of frames. With the old helper and 40 busy loops 12 of 80 runs differed by 30 pixels; with the new one 0 of 80.
- **`TestDesktopFindAllReferences`** (17e.3; `cmd/emetos/desktop_references_display_test.go`): no click was lost. A result keeps the files that were open in the one before it (`setItems` keeps the expanded keys), and Find All Implementations had opened extra.go (the file nearest to the cursor), so the row was open before the test clicked it: the first click closed it, which the test took for a click that had not opened it. The test now checks that the row is open, clicks (closed), waits 500 ms (two clicks on a row within 400 ms are a double click, which toggles nothing) and clicks again (open). No code changed.

- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ (also `emetos_display`, and `emetos_display emetos_gopls`) · golangci-lint ✅ (also `--build-tags emetos_display ./cmd/... ./internal/testenv/...`) · error-tags --untested ✅ · `go mod tidy -diff` clean · go test -race: the whole run had failures only in `internal/gui/app` (and one watcher test of `internal/core/workspace`) when the build's temp folder was moved off the full /tmp (the golden of the save prompt shows a path); `internal/gui/app` alone with the default temp folder ✅ (exit 0, none killed) and `internal/core/workspace` ✅ on rerun · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ (100 packages) · `scripts/realinput.sh` whole suite with `--alone` ✅ (exit 0).

## Fix: what a terminal hides from its events

- **Branch:** fix/terminal-input-hidden
- **The problem.** Decision 185 (17d.4) hid the data of `emetos.terminal.input` when the pty's `ECHO` was off. bash's readline (and zsh's line editor, fish, vim, less, htop) put the terminal in raw mode (`ICANON` off and `ECHO` off) at their prompt and echo by themselves, so every key typed at an ordinary bash prompt was published as hidden and no client of the events ever saw an input event for normal typing.
- **The rule now** (decision 185 rewritten; SPEC §10.25 "As built (step 17d.4)"): the data is hidden only when `ECHO` is off and `ICANON` is on, which is how `getpass`, `sudo`, `ssh`, `passwd` and `read -s` read a password, or when the mode cannot be read. Raw mode (`ICANON` off, `ECHO` on or off) publishes the data: the program draws what it wants on the screen, which the output events carry.
- **Built:** `pty.Process.LineMode() (echo, canonical bool, err error)` replaces `EchoOn` (one `TCGETS`, cgo-free, Tag `PtyLineModeFailed`); `extensions/terminal/stream.go` (`secretInput`) uses it. The test shell got `--password` (only `ECHO` off, canonical, and it never prints what it reads).
- **Tests:** `extensions/internal/pty` (`LineMode` for the four combinations with real ptys and for a closed terminal, with the route of the Tag); `extensions/terminal` (`TestWhatIsTypedIsHiddenOnlyAtAPasswordPrompt`, the five cases with a fake process including an ioctl error; `TestInputIsHiddenOnlyAtAPasswordPrompt`, the test shell in its three modes, a password typed by the user and by an extension, and no event of any topic holds the secret; `TestInputToARealBashAtItsPromptIsPublished`, real bash with readline in an isolated home).
- **Docs:** decision 185, SPEC §10.25, the README line about the security of hosting.
- **Manual checks:** none
- **Glutter issues:** none new.
- **The manager's runs after the rebase onto 17d.6:** `go vet ./...` ✅; `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test` of `extensions/internal/pty`, and `extensions/terminal/...` ✅; `go test -race -count=2` of the same: the first run printed one `FAIL` whose package and test were cut off by the summary of the log, then two runs of pty and the terminal package and ten runs of the new tests with `-race` all passed. The full race run of the milestone's final check covers them again.

## Fix: the architecture test refused the emulator's CPU clock

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** fix/archtest-emulator-test-imports
- **Summary:** "Make four tests measure their subject instead of the machine's load" made `extensions/terminal/emulator/bench_test.go` time the emulator by the CPU clock of its thread, with `golang.org/x/sys/unix`, which the rule `EmulatorImportsUI` refused, so `internal/archtest` `TestRepository` failed on `main`. The manager had merged that fix after testing only the packages it changed; the agent of step 18.1 found the failure in its full run. ## Step 19.2: SQL drivers, dialects and the schema explorer

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** feat/step-19.2-sql-drivers
- **Summary:** The SQL extension (`emetos.sql`, the language pack and now also the driver) connects to PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQLite and SQL Server through their pure Go drivers (pgx v5.11.0, go-sql-driver/mysql v1.10.1, modernc.org/sqlite v1.61.0, go-mssqldb v1.11.2) and shows their schema in the Databases view: databases, schemas, Tables, Views, Functions, Procedures, and below a table its Columns (type, NOT NULL, key icons), Indexes and Foreign Keys, read lazily, with the tree's filter and the view's Refresh. `extensions/sql/dialect` holds what differs between the engines (catalog queries, quoting, `TOP` or `LIMIT`, cancel, read-only statements, statement generators). Connections use TLS modes, a connect timeout, read-only sessions, URLs and a password that never reaches an error. The context menus open generated statements (Select Top 1000, SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, Drop as text) in new untitled SQL editors.

## Fix: two window tabs that closed at once left a connection open

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** feat/step-19.2-sql-drivers (a commit of its own after the step)
- **What:** `dbconn.Hub.RegisterDriver`'s unregister looked at the other registrations in one locked section and removed its own in a later one, so two window tabs that closed at the same time could each see the other still registered: neither closed the connection, and it stayed open with no driver. The unregister now removes its own registration in the same locked section that looks at the others. Found by the race run of step 19.2 (`TestTwoWindowTabsShareTheConnectionsAndEachOpensEditorsInItsOwn` timed out; it failed once in 600 runs alone too). The new `TestTwoTabsThatCloseAtOnceCloseTheConnections` (300 runs of two closes at once) fails on the old code and passes on the new.
- **Two tests made deterministic:** `TestDecryptRefusesWhatIsNotASecret` (its "another key" and "damaged padding" cases depended on the random IV and passed about once in 256 runs; they now use a fixed IV and a flipped IV byte), and `TestExecLimitsAndWaits/a_cancelled_wait_is_an_error` (a 150 ms timer could fire while the exec was still being created; the wait is now cancelled from the engine's first answer to the poll). `containerapi.Client.Exec` now reports a cancel that arrives during a poll of the engine as `ContainerAPIExecCancelled`, not as a failed request.

## Fix: the terminal's test rig looked at the screen before it had parsed what the test wrote

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** fix/terminal-feed-wait
- **What:** `paneRig.feed` waited until no read bytes were waiting for the parser, which is also true before the reader has taken the bytes from the fake program at all, so a test could look at the screen too early: `TestSuggestListClosesWhenThePaneChanges/the_program_uses_the_alternate_screen` failed about 5 times in 100 on `main` (found by the manager's check of 17d.7 after its rebase). `Terminal` now counts the bytes its parser has taken (`parsedNow`), and `feed` waits until that count reaches all the bytes the rig has sent. 300 runs with `-race` pass.

## Step 17d.7: Terminals in the editor area, the tabs list and persistent sessions

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** feat/step-17d.7-terminal-editors
- **Summary:** A terminal can live in an editor tab beside the files, with its title and icon, and moves between the panel and the editor area (commands, or a drag from the tabs list to a tab strip, the middle of an area or an edge that splits it) keeping its process and its cells. The tabs list got VS Code's icons and colors, drag to reorder, join, unsplit, kill all, new with a profile or a folder, size to content width, the tab hover and the title that follows the process. The sessions persist: when Emetos ends each terminal is saved with its last lines (a serialization the emulator writes itself), and at the next start it comes back before the first frame of the panel with that content, VS Code's "History restored" line and a new shell in the same folder; a setting turns it off (SPEC §10.25 "As built (step 17d.7)").

- **API of `extension/`:** `EditorTab.SetIcon(icon, color)` (the icon and its color are kept with the tab in the window state), `EditorTabContent.AllowCommand` (the tab's own `commandsToSkipShell`, as `ViewContent.AllowCommand` is the panel's), `Editors().BeginDrag(kind, label, state)` returning `EditorDrag` (the tabs list starts a drag toward the editor area), `ui.CodiconNames()` (the pickers of icons). ## Fix: an --alone command of heavy.sh could wait for hours

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** fix/heavy-alone-first
- **What:** `scripts/heavy.sh --alone` took slot 1 and then waited for slot 2, while commands that were not alone kept taking slot 2 whenever it came free, so a real-input run could wait more than an hour behind other agents' test runs (reported by the agent of step 18.4). A third lock, the gate, is held by an `--alone` command while it waits (it gives back a slot its quick try took, so two `--alone` commands cannot hold one lock each and wait for the other); a command that is not alone takes a free slot only through the gate (shared, held for the two tries), so none starts while an `--alone` command waits. Tried with two running commands, two `--alone` commands and one more command queued behind them in a temporary `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`: both `--alone` commands ran before the queued one.

## 18.4 The Podman extension

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** feat/step-18.4-podman
- **Summary:** The Podman extension (`emetos.podman`, `extensions/podman`) is the second `Config` of the shared container code: its own activity-bar icon, view, commands (`podman.*`), settings (`podman.host`, `podman.composeBuild`, `podman.composeDetached`, `podman.imageBuildContextPath`), events (`emetos.podman.changed`, `emetos.podman.buildFinished`) and panel ("Podman Logs"). ## 19.3 SQL query editors and the results panel

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** feat/step-19.3-sql-queries
- **Summary:** A `.sql` editor is bound to a connection and a database (status bar item, "Select Connection..." and the menus of the explorer open one already bound), and Run (Ctrl+Enter, the statement at the cursor or the selection), Run All (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) and Cancel run its statements one by one on a session of their own: autocommit by default, with Begin, Commit and Rollback, a tinted status item while a transaction is open and a guard on Disconnect. The statements are cut by a lexer per dialect (dollar quotes, `DELIMITER`, `GO`, trigger and procedure bodies), classified (read, write, transaction, session, destructive), and refused on a read-only connection or confirmed when destructive. The results panel has the grid of every result set (Fetch More, tabs, the last 10 runs, Messages with affected rows, timings and the errors with their place marked in the editor), export to CSV, TSV, JSON and SQL INSERTs, and SQL completion from the live catalog and the keywords of the dialect.

## 22.1 A container's database, and the refusal to clients

- **Date:** 2026-10-29
- **Branch:** feat/step-22.1-container-database
- **Summary:** **Connect to Database** is in the menu of one running container of `postgres`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server`, `mongo`, `redis` or `valkey/valkey`, in both container extensions (`containers.containers.connectDatabase`, `podman.containers.connectDatabase`). It reads the container's inspect and publishes `emetos.containers.connectDatabase` (`emetos.podman.connectDatabase`) with `{engine, name, host, port, user, database}` from the published port and the image's environment, never a password. ## 24.1 The Git client and the test harness

- **Date:** 2026-10-30
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.1-git-client
- **Summary:** `extensions/gitscm/git` runs the user's `git` safely (found by `Find`, at least 2.30; a fixed environment; a process group per command stopped by SIGTERM and SIGKILL; bounded or streamed output; the Git channel log with masked URLs; the failures classified into VS Code's `GitErrorCodes`), orders the commands of a repository (`Queue`) and parses what git prints (status, log, for-each-ref, rev-parse, config, remote, stash, blame, name-status, ls-files, ls-tree, check-ignore), with the read commands of one repository gathered in `Repo` and `Init` and `Clone` on the `Runner`. `extensions/gitscm/gittest` is the harness that runs the real `git` in isolated temporary repositories (own `HOME` and configuration, the author Ada Example, fixed dates, the trust file, a fake `git`, a local `git http-backend` server); `cmd/gitfixture` and `scripts/git-fixture.sh` build the four deterministic fixtures. CLAUDE.md "Testing notes" has the paragraph the user approved on 2026-10-30.
- **Main files:** `extensions/gitscm/git/` (`runner.go`, `classify.go`, `queue.go`, `find.go`, `version.go`, `env.go`, `repo.go`, `repoinfo.go`, `status.go`, `commits.go`, `refs.go`, `blame.go`, `stash.go`, `configtext.go`, `objects.go`, `doc.go`); `extensions/gitscm/gittest/` (`env.go`, `repo.go`, `fake.go`, `http.go`, `fixture.go`, `doc.go`); `cmd/gitfixture/main.go`; `scripts/git-fixture.sh`; `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Tests:** `extensions/gitscm/git` 82 tests, `extensions/gitscm/gittest` 15 and `cmd/gitfixture` 2, 99 in all with 302 subtests, none skipped (git is installed here: 2.56.0). Table-driven throughout. Ported from `extensions/git/src/test/git.test.ts`: all 44 cases, none skipped (the process-input case 1, `GitStatusParser` 12, `parseGitmodules` 5, `parseGitRemotes` 6, `parseGitCommit` 8, `parseGitFileLog` 2, `parseLsTree` 1, `parseLsFiles` 1, `parseCoAuthors` 7, `splitInChunks` 1 with its 14 assertions); `parseLsTree` and `parseLsFiles` are read as the `-z` forms Emetos runs, and a rename's two paths are named `Path` (new) and `OrigPath` (old) where VS Code says `rename` and `path`. Emetos's own: every parser against recorded outputs and against the real git (renames, copies, the seven conflict forms made by real merges, names with spaces, quotes, tabs, newlines, non-UTF-8 bytes and Unicode, empty outputs, truncated records, every stream cut at every byte and fed in two chunks cut at every byte); the environment of a command (a table; the user's `LC_ALL` removed, `LC_CTYPE` kept); the background flags only on background commands, and that they do their job (a `diff.external`, a `diff.<driver>.textconv` and a `core.fsmonitor` program of the repository are started by a foreground command and not by a background one); the version parsing and comparison (`2.30`, `2.43.0.windows.1`, `2.56.0.rc1`, `2.30.1 (Apple Git-130)`); `Find` with the fake git (hints, PATH, too old, missing); the classification of the 38 `GitErrorCodes` of the SPEC's list (34 by `classify`, `NoLocalChanges` by `classifySuccess`, `GitNotFound` by `Find` and `Runner`, `NotAtRepositoryRoot` by `Open` and `UnknownPath` by `ObjectDetails`, each with a route test) with git's real messages where they can be provoked (locked index, conflicts in merge, pull and rebase, stash, push rejected, tag clobbered, identity, dubious ownership, authentication over the local HTTP server, a port nobody listens on...) and fixed text otherwise; cancellation kills the whole process group (a fake git that starts a child), SIGKILL after the grace period for a git that ignores SIGTERM; the queue (reads parallel up to four, writes in order, a read waits only for earlier writes of its scope, a cancelled wait, a coalesced refresh, under `-race`); log masking of `https://user:secret@host/x`; the output bound; the pathspec file for 5,000 paths (fake and real git); 8 MiB of input for a git that exits at once; a repository fixture of every kind read through `Repo`. The harness itself: `git config --global -l` and `--system -l` find nothing, no variable of the user's environment (`GIT_*`, `SSH_*`, `XDG_*`, `HOME`, proxies) leaks, `git rev-parse` in a temporary folder inside the project finds no repository (with a control that does find the project's), the trust file, the fixed dates, hooks, remotes, submodules, the fake git, the HTTP server with and without credentials; the four fixtures are byte-for-byte reproducible (two runs in two folders, equal manifests of every ref, the index, the status and every file) and `cmd/gitfixture` is tested through its `run`. Route tests for every new Tag (`scripts/error-tags.sh --untested` prints nothing).

- **Deviations and follow-ups:**
  - *Tags.* Besides the 38 of the SPEC's list the client has its own: `GitTooOld`, `GitVersionUnreadable`, `GitVersionFailed`, `GitDirMissing`, `GitStartFailed`, `GitStdinConflict`, `GitCancelled`, `GitQueueCancelled`, `GitOutputTooLarge`, `GitContentTooLarge`, `GitOutputUnexpected` and `GitCommandFailed` (a failure git printed nothing known for). VS Code's codes that the SPEC's list leaves out (`BadConfigFile`, `BadRevision`, `BranchFastForwardRejected`, `ForcePushWithLease*`, `CherryPick*`, `Worktree*`) are not built; the steps 24.13 to 24.15 and 24.19 add them where they use them. The SPEC's `UnsafeRepository` is VS Code's `NotASafeGitRepository`.
  - *`NotAtRepositoryRoot` and `CantOpenResource`* are in VS Code's list but nothing in VS Code raises them. Emetos raises the first in `Open` (the folder is inside a repository, not its top level) and the second for a `show`/`cat-file` of a path or an object git does not have (`does not exist in`, `Not a valid object name`).
  - *Messages of today's git.* VS Code's expressions match the git of 2019; today's differs in case (`couldn't find remote ref`, `a branch named ... already exists`), in the wording of the stash (`No stash entries found.`) and in where it prints (`git stash push` with nothing to stash prints `No local changes to save` on standard output and exits 0, so VS Code's `NoLocalChanges` never fires on it). The expressions are case-insensitive where needed and `Runner` raises `NoLocalChanges` for that output of a successful `stash push`. `git commit` with no identity at all names the e-mail first ("no email was given"), so that is `NoUserEmailConfigured`, where VS Code (which asks `git config` name first) says `NoUserNameConfigured`.
  - *Configuration of the harness.* The SPEC says `core.hooksPath` is an empty folder; settings in `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` (the variable `git -c` fills, understood by every version; `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` needs 2.31) win over a repository's own configuration, so `init.defaultBranch`, `protocol.file.allow`, the identity, `gc.auto` and the like are given that way and `core.hooksPath` is written to the local configuration of each repository the harness makes (`Repo.Hook` replaces it). `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` points at a script that fails and `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` is `file:http`, because ssh reads the keys of the account's real home, not `$HOME`.
  - *Runner.* `Result.Stderr` is the last 2 KiB (the SPEC); the classification reads the last 32 KiB. The reads of `Repo` are all background commands. `Queue` writes do not wait for the reads that run (git's own locks do that), and a read waits only for the earlier writes whose scope overlaps its own. A command with more than 200 paths gets them on its standard input only for the commands that read a pathspec file (add, rm, reset, restore, checkout, commit, stash); `SplitInChunks` (ported) is for the others. `rev-parse` is run twice (`--show-toplevel` fails in a bare repository, and `--path-format` needs 2.31).
  - *Not ported.* VS Code's `cache.ts` (an LRU cache for blame and history) and the `OperationManager` of `operation.ts` (blocking, progress, retry): nothing in this step needs them; the Repository model of 24.5 does. `RefNames` of a commit with no decoration is empty (VS Code gives `[""]`).
  - *Names.* `HTTPBackend` and `Trust(env)` are methods of `gittest.Env`; `Trust(t, path)` (package function) follows the `XDG_STATE_HOME` of the process for a test that isolated its folders with the storage helper.
  - *Fixture `many`* with 100,000 files: built in 12 min 27 s of wall time, almost all of it the wait for a `scripts/heavy.sh` slot (the program used 4.8 s of user and 6.4 s of system time), 406 MB on disk, and `git status --porcelain` lists 100,000 changed files in it..

## Fix: Glutter 1.9.8

- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Branch:** fix/glutter-1.9.8 (not a step of the plan)
- **Summary:** Emetos moves to Glutter v1.9.8 (`RunAppContext`) and uses it, so that SIGINT and SIGTERM end Emetos as a Quit without a dialog, with status 0 (decision 459, SPEC §10.3 "Quitting on a signal"). `go.mod` and `go.sum` change the Glutter version only (`go mod verify` passes).
  - **The run:** `Run` calls `widgets.RunAppContext` with `runContext`, a context of its own. Glutter ends a run whose context ends at once and asks nobody, so the signal context itself would end the loop before the backups were written. The quit that the signal asks for was already built (`Workspaces.watchSignal`, step 9b.1: backups of every tab, state, `ExitApplication`) and worked; the new context ends the loop only when it returned, or 40 s after the signal (the 30 s of the backups and 10 s more), so a stuck UI thread cannot keep the process alive.
  - **The bounds:** the backups of all the tabs share one deadline of 30 s (before, each tab had its own); the last write of the state files after the loop is bounded by 30 s too; the failure of a backup is logged and the exit goes on.
  - **A second signal:** `signalContext` (`cmd/emetos`) takes Emetos's handler away at the first signal, so a second one ends the process with the default action.
  - **The harness:** `display.App.Signal(sig, within)` sends a signal to the editor and returns its exit status, with no SIGKILL; `stop` keeps its SIGTERM then SIGKILL.
- **Main files:** `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `cmd/emetos/main.go`, `internal/gui/app/{app.go,backup.go,workspaces.go}`, `internal/testenv/display/app.go`, `docs/SPEC.md` (§10.3), `docs/DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW.md` (459).
- **Tests:** `TestTheSignalQuitBacksUpEveryTabAndEndsWithoutAsking` (two tabs, backups of both, one exit request, no dialog), `TestABackupThatFailsOnTheSignalIsLoggedAndTheQuitEnds`, `TestRunContext` (3 cases), `TestSignalContext` (SIGTERM and SIGINT: the first signal ends the context, the second kills a stuck process), and the display test `TestRealInputSignalEndsAsAQuit` (SIGTERM and SIGINT: the editor with an unsaved edit ends by itself with status 0 and the next start restores the text). The display test also passes on the code before this change: the quit on the signal worked already; `RunAppContext` is the safety net.
- **Glutter issues:** none new.

## Fix: Glutter 1.9.9

- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Branch:** feat/glutter-1.9.9 (not a step of the plan)
- **Summary:** Emetos moves to Glutter v1.9.9 (its steps 29.40 and 29.41), which fixes the only entry of `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md`, "`SliverVariedExtentList` is linear in the number of rows". `kit/sliverrows.go` (`sliverRows`, `renderSliverRows`, `exactExtentDelegate`) and its `// Glutter:` comment are deleted, and the file is deleted. Only sliver files changed between 1.9.8 and 1.9.9, with no change of API.
  - **`kit.List`:** with `HeightOf` it builds a `SliverVariedExtentList` whose extent builder is the model's `RowHeightAt` (none past the last row, so that the scroll extent is exact). The rule of 1.9.9 (the builder does not change until the widget is built again) holds because every change of the model sets the state of the list, which makes a new builder (decision 609).
  - **Tests:** `TestListJumpToTheEndOfAHundredThousandRows` (new; 100,000 rows of six heights; jumps to the end, the top, the end, the middle and the end again, one frame each: the offset is exact, the last row is built and ends where the content ends, the frame is bounded), `TestListRowsFollowTheHeightsWhenTheyChange` (new; a row taller, rows removed, rows added: the rows are at the new tops, and the end of the view is the end of the content; it fails when the builder is kept across builds), and `TestHugeChanges` of the Source Control view now jumps to the exact end of its content (twice) and checks it. `TestListRowsOfDifferentHeights` and `...AtTheEnd` are unchanged. No golden changed.
  - **Measured** (`TestHugeChanges`, 100,000 files, a jump to the exact end, processor time of the UI thread): 9 to 10 ms before, 10 to 13 ms after (the same, within the noise; the machine was shared). The kit list of 100,000 rows: 2 to 3 ms a jump, before and after.
- **Checks:** gofmt ✅ · go vet ✅ · golangci-lint ✅ · go test -race ✅ (`./...`; `TestGoToRecentDirectory` failed once at the removal of its temporary folder ("directory not empty", a file written by a background goroutine of the terminal extension while the folder was removed), and `extensions/terminal` passed three more runs with `-count=3`) · `scripts/error-tags.sh --untested` prints nothing · CGO_ENABLED=0 build ✅ · CGO_ENABLED=0 test ✅ (`./...`) · no golden changed · `scripts/perf.sh` has no case for long lists, so it was not run.
- **Main files:** `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `internal/gui/kit/{list.go,listembedded_test.go}`, `internal/gui/kit/sliverrows.go` (deleted), `internal/gui/views/scm/huge_test.go`, `docs/{SPEC.md,DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW.md}` (609, 462 amended), `docs/GLUTTER-ISSUES.md` (deleted).
- **Glutter issues:** one removed, none new; the file is deleted.

## 24.4 The commit input and the action button

- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.4-scm-input
- **Summary:** The Changes view has, for each repository, the commit box and the action button as rows of its list. The box is a multi-line `kit.InputBox` (the placeholder of the provider with the key of the accept command in it, between `scm.inputMinLineCount` and `scm.inputMaxLineCount` lines, `scm.inputFontFamily` and `scm.inputFontSize`) that grows with its text; the message of the validation function is drawn under it with the colors of its level (error, warning, information) while the box has the keyboard. Ctrl+Enter runs the accept command with the repository as argument; Escape clears the validation, then collapses a selection, then empties the box; Up at the very start and Down at the very end of the text bring the previous and the next message of the history of the repository (Alt+Up and Alt+Down from anywhere); the history is the session's, per provider and folder. The action button is a split button (command, and a dropdown of the secondary commands in groups with separators), disabled with the provider's flag, hidden with `scm.showActionButton`; these settings take effect while the view is open. The keyboard goes to the box when the view opens.

## 24.5 The Git extension: repositories and status

- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.5-git-repos (based on 24.3, rebased onto `main` 3a2fe1c)
- **Summary:** `extensions/gitscm` (`emetos.gitscm`, "Git") is in `extensions.All()`. It reads the settings (VS Code's keys, in Extensions > Git of the settings editor), finds `git` (2.30 or newer; a message and the welcome content when it is missing or too old), discovers repositories from the file system with no process (the folder, parent folders with `git.openRepositoryInParentFolders`, subfolders by `git.autoRepositoryDetection` and depth, open editors' files, submodules, `git.ignoredRepositories`), asks the trust question of D37 (dialog with Trust Repository, Trust All Repositories in the parent, Don't Trust, with the programs the configuration names; `$XDG_STATE_HOME/emetos/git-trust.json`), and for a trusted repository makes a source control with the groups Merge Changes, Staged Changes, Changes and Untracked Changes (VS Code's status-to-group split, letters, colors and tooltips, `git.untrackedChanges`, `git.statusLimit` and its warning once, `git.similarityThreshold`, the badge count `git.countBadge`), the status bar items (the branch item with `*`, `+`, `!`, the icon rules, a tag or the short commit when detached, `(Rebasing)`; the sync item `2↓ 1↑`, Publish Branch) and the progress while a command runs. It refreshes from a debounced watcher (500 ms, a fixed window), after its own commands, on save and when the window gets the focus. It publishes `emetos.gitscm.repositoryChanged` and answers `emetos.gitscm.status`. Commands: `git.refresh`, `git.close`, `git.closeOtherRepositories`, `git.reopenClosedRepositories`, `git.openRepository`, `git.openRepositoriesInParentFolders`, `git.manageUnsafeRepositories`, `git.trustRepository`, `git.manageTrustedRepositories`. New API: `Workspace().Watch` (on the window's watcher, `Watcher.Subscribe`), `Dialogs().Ask`, `emetos.window.focusChanged`, `SettingSpec.AlsoTypes/Scope/EnumDescriptions`.
