## 24.6 File decorations

- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.6-decorations (based on `main` bf0d232, after 24.5)
- **Summary:** a decorations service (`internal/core/decorations`) replaces the interim letter of 24.3 and 24.5 (decisions 447 and 493). It is a port of VS Code's `DecorationsService` for providers that answer at once: answers are cached by (URI, provider) in a trie of path segments, the aggregates of folders (`Propagate`) are memoized and dropped along the path of a change, weights sort the answers and the newest provider wins a tie, tooltips are joined with " • ", the colors fall back to the next color the theme knows, letters are joined with ", ", and a folder with marks inside shows the dot (Codicon `circle-small-filled`, 40% opacity, "Contains emphasized items") in place of its own badge. The cache is bounded (250,000 entries), a provider slower than 1 ms is logged and, after 20 slow answers, suspended for new URIs until it fires. Extensions get `api.Decorations().Register(provider)` with `Fire(uris...)` and `Dispose` (`FileDecoration{Badge, Icon, Tooltip, Color, Propagate, Priority}`); a panic in a provider fails the extension. The widgets read the look through `kit.FileDecorations` (an inherited widget fed by `kit.FileDecorationsHost`, which rebuilds only the dependents) and `kit.FileLookOf`: the Explorer, Open Editors, tabs, breadcrumbs (bar and picker), Search results (list and tree) and the Source Control rows. The Git provider (`extensions/gitscm/decorations.go`) is one per repository, from the groups in the order index, untracked, working, merge, with the old path of a rename, submodules from `.gitmodules`, and a global ignore provider that batches paths and runs `git check-ignore` per repository. `dev.scm.fake` registers its own provider through the service.
- **Main files:**
  - `internal/core/decorations/` (new: `service.go`, `types.go`, `uri.go`, `doc.go`), `extension/decorations.go`, `extension/decorationstest/` (new), `extension/api.go`, `extension/scm.go` (`Letter` removed), `extension/ui/ui.go`;
  - `internal/gui/exthost/decorations.go` (new), `scope.go`, `scm.go`; `extensions/internal/fakeapi/decorations.go` (new);

## 24.17 The multi-file diff editor

- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.17-multidiff (based on `feat/step-24.7-diffs`, 1e80139)
- **Summary:** the changes of many files open in one scrolling editor. The extension contract gets `Documents().ProvideMultiDiff(MultiDiffProvider{Kind, Resources})`, `Documents().OpenMultiDiff(MultiDiffSpec)` and the menu `MenuMultiDiffFileToolbar` (decisions 560, 561, 567); the host validates and contains them, and `fakeapi` and `extension/contenttest` cover them on both sides. `internal/gui/multidiff` is the layout (prefix sums, estimated and measured heights, scroll anchoring, the sections near the viewport) and the widget (headers with chevron, icon, name, folder, the file's actions and its status letter; keyboard on the headers); `internal/gui/app/multidiffpane.go` makes the body of a section (the diff editor of §9.11, own scrolling off, sized to its content) when it comes near the viewport and ends it when it leaves (563, 564). The title bar has Go to Previous/Next Change and Collapse/Expand All Diffs, Alt+F5 and Shift+Alt+F5 cross files, the tab says "(N files)" (565, 566). A saved editor holds its kind, key and title; after a restart it waits for the provider and asks it again (560, 562). `extensions/gitscm` provides the kind `git.changes` for `group/<repo>/<group>` and `commit/<repo>/<hash>`; `git.viewChanges`, `git.viewStagedChanges`, `git.viewUntrackedChanges` and `git.viewCommit` open it, `git.openAllChanges` opens one editor instead of many tabs (568), and `Repo.CommitChanges` reads a commit against its first parent or the empty tree (569).

## 24.22 Blame

- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.22-blame (based on `main`, 1e80139, steps 24.1 to 24.7; steps 24.8 and 24.17 were built at the same time on other branches)
- **Summary:** who changed the line the cursor is on, as a muted text after the line and as a status bar item. The extension contract gets `api.EditorDecorations()` (`Set(key, uri, []LineAnnotation)`, `Clear`) with hovers that take `command:` links to the extension's own commands; the editor draws the annotations after the end of the text of a line (it moves nothing) and shows their hover; the Git extension blames the version of the file in HEAD 150 ms after the cursor stops (cached by file and HEAD, cancelled by the next move), maps the document's lines to it with a line diff (a line that is not in HEAD is "Uncommitted changes" with the name from `user.name`), and fills the two templates, the hover with **Open Commit** and **Copy Hash**, the status bar item and the two toggle commands.

## 24.9 Passwords and editors: the helper

- **Date:** 2026-10-31
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.9-helper
- **Summary:** git can now ask Emetos for a password, a passphrase, a host-key answer or an editor, and Emetos answers in its own window and stores nothing. `extensions/gitscm/helper` is the program git runs (`emetos --git-askpass`, `--git-ssh-askpass`, `--git-editor`, served by `cmd/emetos` before anything else) and the server of the extension (a Unix socket in a private folder of the runtime folder, token and peer check, size bound and deadline, stale folders removed); the prompts are classified from the real texts of git and ssh and asked one at a time in an input box (dots for secrets, a "Git: https://host" line, the box stays when the focus leaves it) or a quick pick; Escape fails the command with `AuthenticationFailed` and Retry; the editor opens the file git wants in a tab and answers when it closes (0 after a save), with Accept and Cancel as title actions of a commit message. `git.fetch` exists in its smallest form so there is a command that asks (decisions 620 to 632).

## 24.14 Merge, rebase, cherry-pick and conflicts

- **Date:** 2026-11-01
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.14-merge-rebase (based on step 24.13, 5f65989)
- **Summary:** the operations that stop on conflicts can be started, followed and finished from the Source Control view. `git.merge` (a pick of branches, remote branches and tags), `git.rebase` (the upstream first), `git.rebaseInteractive` (the list of commits opens in an editor tab), `git.cherryPick` (an input box for the hash) and their aborts run through the new `Repo.Merge`, `Rebase`, `CherryPick`, `MergeAbort`, `RebaseAbort`, `RebaseSkip`, `CherryPickAbort`, `Continue` and `MergeFile`; a conflict is a warning that leaves the operation in progress. While a merge, a rebase, a cherry-pick or a revert waits (found from `MERGE_HEAD`, `rebase-merge/`, `rebase-apply/`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` and `REVERT_HEAD`, also after a restart) the branch item has the conflicts icon, the box says "{0} to continue the ...", the button is **Continue** (on when Merge Changes is empty), and the commit finishes the operation; for a rebase the box shows the message of the stopped commit and warns when it is changed. A click on a Merge Changes row opens the diff, the file or, with `git.mergeEditor` on, the merge editor; Complete Merge of the merge editor publishes the new core event `emetos.mergeEditor.completed` and the extension stages the file; `git.runGitMerge` and `git.runGitMergeDiff3` rebuild the markers of the merge editor's file from the three stages. The contract gets `OpenSpec.MergeEditor`, `Documents().ActiveMergeEditor()` and the event; the `TODO(step 24.14)` of 24.7 and the open points of decisions 689 and 748 are resolved.

## 24.15 Remotes, fetch, pull, push, sync and autofetch

- **Date:** 2026-11-01
- **Branch:** feat/step-24.15-remotes (based on step 24.14, f9624e8)
- **Summary:** the Git extension talks to remotes with the user's `git`, credential helpers and keys. `git.fetch` (the only remote, else a pick), `git.fetchPrune`, `git.fetchAll`, `git.fetchRef`, `git.pull`, `git.pullRebase`, `git.pullFrom`, `git.pullRef`, `git.push` and its force, `Push to...`, follow-tags and tags variants, `git.pushRef`, `git.sync`, `git.syncRebase`, `git.publish` (to any remote, adding one first when there is none; no service repository), `git.addRemote` (URL validated) and `git.removeRemote` run through the new `Repo.Fetch`, `FetchTags`, `Pull`, `Push`, `SetUpstream`, `FastForwardBranch`, `AddRemote`, `RemoveRemote`, `MaybeRebased` and `ValidateRemoteURL`, with VS Code's questions and failures: a rejected push offers **Pull**, a branch with no upstream asks to publish (or offers **Publish Branch**), a refusal of the server shows its message (new tag `RemoteRejected`), a failed authentication offers **Retry**, tags that differ offer to be replaced, a branch that looks rebased asks before it is pulled into, a sync asks to confirm, a force push is allowed by `git.allowForcePush` and confirmed, with `--force-with-lease` and `--force-if-includes` by their settings. The contract gets `Notifications().Progress` (a notification with a progress bar and Cancel); `git.supportCancellation` uses it for the sync.

- **Date:** 2026-11-01

## 24.25 Extensions and the terminal in the Remote Work view

## 25.1 The DAP client and the fake adapter

- **Date:** 2026-11-02
- **Branch:** feat/step-25.1-dap (based on main at a00611b)
- **Summary:** `internal/core/dap` speaks the Debug Adapter Protocol: the framing, the protocol types ported from VS Code's `debugProtocol.d.ts`, a `Client` (numbered requests matched to their responses, `cancel` when a context ends, the events through a bounded channel with back-pressure, the adapter's own requests answered by a handler, `Close`) and the transports that reach an adapter (a program on its standard input and output in its own process group, a TCP port, a Unix socket, and a program that prints its port). `internal/core/dap/daptest` is the scripted fake adapter that every later test of M25 uses: a script of steps, a server that records the traffic and the protocol violations, a program built by `TestMain`, and a harness that connects a client to it over each transport.
- **Main files:**
  - `internal/core/dap/{doc,frame,queue,client,process,transport}.go`, `types.go`, `types_requests.go`, `types_events.go`, `capabilities.go`;
  - `internal/core/dap/daptest/{doc,script,server,harness}.go`, `daptest/fakeadapter/main.go`;
  - tests: `frame_test.go`, `types_test.go`, `client_test.go`, `process_test.go`, `burst_test.go`, `main_test.go`, `daptest/daptest_test.go`;
  - `docs/SPEC.md` (§5 layout, "As built (step 25.1)" under §10.31), `docs/DECISIONS-TO-REVIEW.md` (1100 to 1111), this entry.
- **Tests:** 57 top-level tests with 184 subtests (the list is below). The framing: split headers byte by byte, several messages in one read, a body across reads, bare line feeds, other headers, an empty body, garbage, a header that is too long, too many headers, a missing or bad length, the 64 MiB limit refused before the body is read, truncation in the header and in the body, failing reads and writes. The client, over each of five transports (in process, stdio, TCP, Unix socket, a program that prints its port): the whole initialize-launch-breakpoints-stop-disconnect sequence with its events and capabilities; three requests answered in another order with events between; reverse requests (`runInTerminal` answered, `startDebugging` refused, an unknown one, no handler); `cancel` sent with the right request number only when supported, and a late answer dropped; a timeout of the client and of the context; the adapter dying in the middle of a request (with its exit status); three kinds of garbage on the stream; a message that is not JSON, one with an unknown type and an event with no name, logged and skipped; a message over the limit; failed responses with `{variables}` filled; a `Close` with a request pending; the capabilities event merged; the trace in the order of the wire; arguments that cannot be sent; a body that does not fit; a failing write and a failing close. The transports: not found, cannot start, stderr and stdout lines, a line over 64 KiB cut, the environment and folder, `Close` ending the whole group, a program that ignores SIGTERM killed after three seconds, the context ending the program, `Stop`, the port of a server program found in seven spellings (dlv's, js-debug's, a host name, a bare port, `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`, a pattern of the debugger), a server program that exits, prints no port in time, prints a port that is not one or one nobody listens on, and is stopped when its start fails. **The burst:** an adapter sends 10,000 events of 1 KB while nobody reads; exactly the buffer (64) is held, the adapter has written under a tenth of them (in process), the heap grew by less than 4 MiB, and then all 10,000 come in order. `daptest` itself: the script round trip and its errors, the arguments matching, every violation it notes, the requests it answers while stalled, crash and exit, stderr, burst, raw and bad frames, write failures. No VS Code test cases are ported (the step has none; `debugProtocol.d.ts` is the source of the types).

## 25.2 The debug model and launch configurations

- **Date:** 2026-11-02
- **Branch:** feat/step-25.2-debugmodel (based on step 25.1, c5e42fa)
- **Summary:** `internal/core/debug` is the model of a debugging window and the driver of its sessions over `core/dap`, without a UI. `Model` holds the sessions, threads, call stacks, scopes, variables (lazy, paged by 100, with stable ids), watch expressions, the line, inline, function and exception breakpoints with the data each adapter gave (verified, moved line, message) and the focus, and tells the views by `Event`s. `Service` starts sessions from a launch configuration (variables, providers, tasks before and after, compounds with `stopAll`, child sessions and `runInTerminal`), restarts and stops them, and sends the breakpoints in VS Code's order. `ParseLaunch` and `Launches` read `.emetos/launch.json` (JSONC with positioned problems), the `launch` settings of the workspace and the user, and keep the selected configuration. `ResolveConfig` substitutes the variables, with `${input:...}` prompts. `Tracker` makes the breakpoints follow the edits of an open document (a `core/document` decoration each). `SaveState` and `RestoreState` keep the breakpoints, watch expressions and selection in the new opaque `storage.WindowState.Debug`.

## 26.1 The Testing API and model

- **Date:** 2026-11-02
- **Branch:** feat/step-26.1-testing-model (based on step 25.13, 3c5ce5a)
- **Summary:** extensions can describe tests and report runs, and the core keeps the results. `extension/testing.go` adds `api.Tests()` (like `vscode.tests`): controllers with a tree of `TestItem`s, run profiles of the kinds Run, Debug and Coverage, run requests with include and exclude, and a `TestRun` that reports enqueued, started, skipped, passed, failed and errored tests with messages (text or Markdown, expected and actual output, location, stack trace), output and coverage. `internal/core/testing` is the model: the item tree by controller, the profiles and their defaults, `RunTests` with one result for a request and a task for each `CreateTestRun`, results with VS Code's states, precedence, computed states and durations, the last 16 results saved in the new `WindowState.Testing` (output trimmed to 1 MiB), continuous runs that start again when a file of an item changes, and coverage with its sums and lazily loaded details. `exthost.TestingHost` (`ScopeOptions.Testing`) and `fakeapi` implement the API together. A Remote Work client's `testing.` commands are not refused (D46).
- **Main files:**
  - `extension/testing.go` (the contract and the tree of items), `extension/api.go` (`Tests()`);
  - `internal/core/testing/{doc,id,state,model,controllers,request,result,coverage,continuous,store}.go`;
  - `internal/core/storage/statefiles.go` (`WindowState.Testing`);

## 26.2 The Test Explorer

- **Date:** 2026-11-02
- **Branch:** feat/step-26.2-test-explorer (based on step 26.1, 6eae016)
- **Summary:** the tests can be seen and run. The activity bar has a Testing container (the beaker, after Run and Debug, with a "Testing" entry in the View menu) whose Test Explorer shows the tests of the controllers as a tree or a flat list with the state icon, the label, the description and the duration of each, the filter box with VS Code's terms (`@failed`, `@executed`, `@doc`, `@openedFiles`, `@hidden`, tags, text, `@ctrl:<id>`) and its menu, the summary line ("3/5 tests passed (60%, 1 skipped), 4.2 s") with the buttons that run the last run again, the sort orders, hiding, the inline buttons and the context menu of a test, and the count badge of the icon. The title has Run, Debug and Coverage of what the tree shows, Refresh, Cancel, Continuous Run, Show Output and the "..." menu. Every command and key of §10.32 that belongs to the Explorer works (the Ctrl+; chords). The window makes one testing host for each workspace tab (`ScopeOptions.Testing`), restores and saves the results with its state, feeds the changes of files to the continuous runs, runs the tests on a goroutine of its own and hands the events to the UI thread (decision 1533); a client's view has its own Explorer over the host's model. A dev controller `dev.testing.fake` runs a script of results in debug builds.
- **Main files:**
  - `internal/gui/views/testing/` (new: `explorer.go`, `elements.go`, `filter.go`, `body.go`, `format.go`, `style.go`, `doc.go`);
